examples.zh: 示例账户从国内生产总值换算为国内生产净值时扣除「固定资本消耗」。

examples.en: Our worksheet shows how consumption of fixed capital reduces the net figure for the example economy.
examples.zh: 练习纸展示了「固定资本消耗」如何降低示例经济体的净额数据。

collocations: consumption of fixed capital by industry

words.enDefinition: a market whose incumbents face strong pressure from potential entrants because entry and exit can occur without significant sunk costs

examples.en: The contestable market example had only two active sellers but newcomers could rent the same equipment temporarily.
examples.zh: 「可竞争市场」示例中只有两个活跃卖家，但新进入者可以临时租用同样的设备。

examples.en: We discussed whether it remained a contestable market after adding equipment costs that entrants could not recover.
examples.zh: 模型加入进入者无法收回的设备成本后，我们讨论这个市场是否仍然是「可竞争市场」。

collocations: assess whether a market is a contestable market
compare prices in a contestable market

words.enDefinition: A plan whose prescribed action depends on what the player observes or on which situation arises.

examples.en: The group chose a contingent strategy that used the smaller room if the larger one was booked.
examples.zh: 小组采用「条件式策略」，如果大教室被预订，就改用小教室。

examples.en: We read the contingent strategy to see what the second club would do after each possible offer.
examples.zh: 我们查看「条件式策略」，了解面对每种可能的提议，第二个社团会怎样做。

collocations: write a contingent strategy for later choices

words.enDefinition: The payoff expected from the remaining part of a game after a specified point or history.

examples.en: We calculated the continuation payoff from the remaining rounds before comparing the two actions available now.
examples.zh: 我们先算出余下各轮的「后续收益」，再比较当前可选的两项行动。

examples.en: The tutor asked how rejecting the offer would affect the group's continuation payoff in the example.
examples.zh: 老师问，拒绝该提议将怎样影响例题中小组的「后续收益」。

collocations: include the continuation payoff in an earlier decision

words.enDefinition: The part of a strategy governing choices after a specified history or stage.

examples.en: The worksheet asked us to state the continuation strategy after the second group declined the first proposal.
examples.zh: 练习表要求我们写出第二组拒绝首个提议之后的「后续策略」。

examples.en: Our tutor changed the continuation strategy while holding the opening choice fixed in the exercise.
examples.zh: 老师改变了练习中的「后续策略」，同时保持初始选择不变。

collocations: compare continuation strategies after different histories
check the continuation strategy at a later decision

words.enDefinition: In a regression discontinuity design, the assumption that the conditional mean of each potential outcome is continuous at the cutoff.

examples.en: The continuity assumption would be doubtful if another service also changed abruptly at the same cutoff.
examples.zh: 如果另一项服务也在同一阈值处突然变化，「连续性假设」就值得怀疑。

examples.en: We stated the continuity assumption before interpreting the apparent jump in the classroom outcome graph.
examples.zh: 我们先明确「连续性假设」，再解读课堂结果图上看似突然的跳变。

words.enDefinition: A baseline experimental condition used to compare outcomes with a changed condition.

examples.en: The control treatment kept the original rules while the other group could see earlier contributions.
examples.zh: 「实验对照条件」沿用原规则，另一组则可以看到此前的出资。

examples.en: We compared choices in the control treatment with choices after the information display was introduced.
examples.zh: 我们把「实验对照条件」中的选择与引入信息显示后的选择作了比较。

collocations: compare outcomes with a control treatment
define the rules for the control treatment

words.enDefinition: preferences under which any mixture of two bundles is at least as desirable as the less preferred of the two

examples.en: With convex preferences, the midpoint of two equally liked bundles is at least as good.
examples.zh: 在「凸偏好」下，两个同样受偏好的组合的中点至少与原来的组合一样好。

examples.en: The class used convex preferences to explain why a balanced mix could be preferable.
examples.zh: 全班用「凸偏好」解释为什么分配均衡的组合可能更受青睐。

words.enDefinition: A game in which players gain by aligning their choices in one of the compatible ways.

examples.en: The coordination game rewarded both groups when they independently picked the same slot for the workshop.
examples.zh: 两组各自为工作坊选择同一时段时，「协调博弈」会让双方都获得奖励。

examples.en: Our tutor used a coordination game to discuss how conventions could develop between neighbouring clubs.
examples.zh: 老师用「协调博弈」讨论邻近社团之间怎样形成惯例。

collocations: identify equilibria in a coordination game

words.enDefinition: Measure of price growth designed to filter some volatile components

examples.en: The US example measures core inflation using a consumer index excluding food and energy.
examples.zh: 美国的这个例子用剔除食品和能源的消费价格指数衡量「核心通胀」。

examples.en: The professor explained why core inflation can differ depending on which series we use.
examples.zh: 老师解释了为什么选用的统计序列不同，「核心通胀」可能不同。

words.enDefinition: Best feasible choice where at least one good's chosen quantity is zero

examples.en: The model gives a corner solution in which the shopper buys only apples.
examples.zh: 模型给出了一个购物者只买苹果的「角点解」。

examples.en: We checked for a corner solution after finding that every affordable mix scored lower.
examples.zh: 发现买得起的各个混合组合得分都更低后，我们检查了是否有「角点解」。

words.enDefinition: A subsidy intended to encourage an activity with external benefits by making some of those benefits privately valuable.

examples.en: The worksheet applied a corrective subsidy to reflect the extra benefits one more training place created for others.
examples.zh: 练习表采用「矫正性补贴」，将增加一个培训名额给他人带来的额外收益纳入考虑。

examples.en: Our class set the corrective subsidy equal to the marginal external benefit at the efficient quantity.
examples.zh: 我们全班把「矫正性补贴」设为有效数量下的边际外部收益。

collocations: a corrective subsidy for a positive externality

words.enDefinition: the lower boundary formed by choosing the least costly among several cost curves at each output level

examples.en: The cost envelope traced the lowest available average cost across three possible factory sizes in our diagram.
examples.zh: 我们图中的「成本包络线」沿三种可选工厂规模中能达到的最低平均成本画出。

examples.en: We read the cost envelope to see when a larger plant became cheaper for a given output.
examples.zh: 我们读取「成本包络线」，判断在给定产量下何时采用更大的工厂成本更低。

collocations: derive a long-run curve as a cost envelope

words.enDefinition: the curve joining least-cost input combinations at different output levels while input prices remain fixed

examples.en: The cost expansion path connected the producer's least-cost choices for small, medium and large output levels.
examples.zh: 「成本最小化扩张路径」连接生产者在低、中、高产量下成本最低的选择。

examples.en: We traced the cost expansion path without changing the input prices used to draw the graph.
examples.zh: 我们保持作图所用的要素价格不变，描出了「成本最小化扩张路径」。

collocations: derive a cost expansion path from input choices

words.enDefinition: the extent to which a change in a producer's costs changes the price charged to buyers

examples.en: The cost pass-through was incomplete because the example seller absorbed part of the increase in input prices.
examples.zh: 示例卖家吸收了要素涨价的一部分，所以「成本传导」不完全。

examples.en: We compared cost pass-through across two markets where sellers faced buyers with different demand responsiveness.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两个市场的「成本传导」，两地买家对价格的响应程度不同。

collocations: compare cost pass-through across market structures

words.enDefinition: Price growth driven by higher production costs or adverse supply pressures

examples.en: We modeled cost-push inflation after higher energy costs made deliveries more expensive.
examples.zh: 能源成本上升使配送变贵后，我们对「成本推动型通胀」建模。

examples.en: The class discussed cost-push inflation using a temporary increase in the cost of imported materials.
examples.zh: 全班以进口原材料成本暂时增加为例讨论了「成本推动型通胀」。

words.enDefinition: Using an observable action that takes resources and is harder for some types to imitate.

examples.en: Our worksheet used costly signaling to explain why an inspection could distinguish two types of seller.
examples.zh: 练习表用「有成本的信号传递」解释为什么检验能够区分两类卖家。

examples.en: The tutor asked why costly signaling failed to separate the sellers when both could pass inspection cheaply.
examples.zh: 老师问，两类卖家都能以很低的成本通过检验时，「有成本的信号传递」为什么不能将他们区分开。

collocations: explain costly signaling in a used goods market

words.enDefinition: Tending to move in the opposite direction from the business cycle or to offset its swings.

examples.en: The indicator is countercyclical in the example because it rises during months when production falls.
examples.zh: 示例中，该指标是「逆周期的」，因为它在生产下降的月份上涨。

examples.en: We called the plotted series countercyclical after finding that it usually fell during expansions.
examples.zh: 发现该序列通常在扩张期下降后，我们把它描述为「逆周期的」。

words.enDefinition: Tax and spending choices that offset expansions or downturns in aggregate activity

examples.en: The lecture models countercyclical fiscal policy by raising purchases after a drop in private spending.
examples.zh: 课堂通过在私人支出下降后提高政府购买，来模拟「逆周期财政政策」。

examples.en: We compared two examples of countercyclical fiscal policy that used different mixes of taxes and spending.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两个采用不同税收和支出组合的「逆周期财政政策」示例。

words.enDefinition: The outcome a unit would have experienced under a condition different from the one actually observed.

examples.en: The counterfactual outcome is the score a tutored student would have achieved without the support.
examples.zh: 「反事实结果」是接受辅导的学生如果没有得到辅导本会取得的分数。

examples.en: We explained why the counterfactual outcome cannot be observed directly for the same student.
examples.zh: 我们解释了为什么无法直接观测同一学生的「反事实结果」。

words.enDefinition: an oligopoly model where firms choose quantities simultaneously, taking rivals' quantities as given when choosing their own

examples.en: In the Cournot model, each firm chose output based on what it expected its rival to supply.
examples.zh: 在「古诺模型」中，每家厂商根据对另一家供给量的预期选择自己的产量。

examples.en: We used the Cournot model to compare industry output with the amount chosen by a single seller.
examples.zh: 我们用「古诺模型」比较行业产量与单一卖家选定的产量。

collocations: compare outputs in the Cournot model
draw response curves for a Cournot model

words.enDefinition: Similarity in the distributions of observed characteristics across the groups being compared.

examples.en: We checked covariate balance by comparing prior grades in the fictional treatment and comparison groups.
examples.zh: 我们通过比较虚构处理组与比较组的既往成绩，检查「协变量平衡」。

examples.en: The adjusted groups showed better covariate balance on attendance than they did before the adjustment.
examples.zh: 调整之后，各组在出勤率上的「协变量平衡」比调整前更好。

words.enDefinition: Continuity of the conditional means of pre-treatment characteristics across the cutoff, used as a design check.

examples.en: We checked covariate continuity by looking for a jump in prior grades at the threshold.
examples.zh: 我们查看阈值处既往成绩是否跳变，以检查「协变量连续性」。

examples.en: The tutor explained how a failure of covariate continuity could weaken confidence in the design.
examples.zh: 老师解释「协变量连续性」不成立为何会削弱对设计的信心。

words.enDefinition: an exchange rate peg whose target level is adjusted in small steps at intervals under the arrangement

examples.en: The example used a crawling peg that adjusted its reference rate by small scheduled steps during the year.
examples.zh: 示例采用「爬行盯住安排」，在一年内按计划小幅逐步调整参考汇率。

examples.en: We compared the crawling peg with a fixed target that stayed unchanged throughout the same period.
examples.zh: 我们把「爬行盯住安排」和同期始终不变的固定目标汇率作了比较。

collocations: adjust a rate under a crawling peg
compare a crawling peg with a conventional peg

words.enDefinition: A commitment others have reason to believe because later choices are constrained or following through remains worthwhile.

examples.en: The example treated the fixed room booking as a credible commitment because it could not be changed.
examples.zh: 由于教室预订一经确定便无法更改，例题把它视为「可信承诺」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked why the other group would take a credible commitment into account before choosing.
examples.zh: 老师问，另一组为什么会在作选择前考虑「可信承诺」。

words.enDefinition: a promised future action that the promiser has incentives to carry out when choosing whether to do it

examples.en: The worksheet asked whether sharing spare materials later was a credible promise for the first team.
examples.zh: 练习表问，对第一队来说，之后分享备用材料是否构成「可信许诺」。

examples.en: We examined the later incentives before deciding whether the group had made a credible promise.
examples.zh: 我们先考察后期激励，再判断该组是否作出了「可信许诺」。

collocations: distinguish a credible promise from an empty one

words.enDefinition: An observable action or indicator that receivers have reason to trust as evidence of hidden information.

examples.en: The case treated independently verified test results as a credible signal about the condition of equipment.
examples.zh: 案例把经过独立核实的检测结果视为有关设备状况的「可信信号」。

examples.en: We discussed what made a credible signal costly for sellers whose products had significant defects.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了什么因素会使产品存在严重缺陷的卖家付出高代价才能发出「可信信号」。

collocations: a credible signal of product quality

words.enDefinition: One good's percentage demand change divided by another good's percentage price change

examples.en: The question uses cross-price elasticity of demand to relate tea purchases to the price of coffee.
examples.zh: 这道题用「需求交叉价格弹性」表示茶的购买量和咖啡价格之间的关系。

examples.en: We calculated the cross-price elasticity of demand for bus trips with respect to the price of train tickets.
examples.zh: 我们计算了公交出行对火车票价格的「需求交叉价格弹性」。

collocations: calculate the cross-price elasticity of demand

words.enDefinition: Reduction in private spending associated with an increase in government borrowing or expenditure

examples.en: Our model illustrates crowding out when higher government borrowing raises rates and reduces private investment.
examples.zh: 我们的模型展示了政府借款增加导致利率上升、私人投资减少时的「挤出效应」。

examples.en: The exercise compares crowding out under two assumptions about how interest rates respond.
examples.zh: 习题在两种不同的利率反应假设下比较了「挤出效应」。

words.enDefinition: a monetary arrangement backed by a commitment to exchange domestic currency at a fixed rate with specified foreign reserve backing

examples.en: The course used a currency board example to show how domestic currency issuance could depend on foreign reserves.
examples.zh: 课程用「货币发行局制度」示例说明，国内货币发行如何取决于外汇储备。

examples.en: We checked the formal conversion commitment before distinguishing a currency board from a conventional exchange rate peg.
examples.zh: 在区分「货币发行局制度」与传统盯住汇率之前，我们核对了正式兑换承诺。

collocations: analyse the rules of a currency board

words.enDefinition: an official reduction in a currency's fixed or targeted value against its anchor

examples.en: The historical example showed a currency devaluation announced under an arrangement with an official parity.
examples.zh: 历史示例展示了有官方平价的安排下公布的「官方下调本币平价」。

examples.en: The class compared the announced currency devaluation with an earlier decline under a floating exchange regime.
examples.zh: 同学们把公布的「官方下调本币平价」与更早在浮动汇率制度下出现的跌势作了比较。

collocations: analyse the effects of currency devaluation
compare a currency devaluation with depreciation

words.enDefinition: notes and coins issued and held outside the institutions excluded by the monetary statistic's stated definition

examples.en: Our data table separates currency in circulation from reserve balances held at the central bank.
examples.zh: 我们的数据表把「流通中货币」和央行持有的银行准备金余额分开列出。

examples.en: We checked whether the definition of currency in circulation in this series included cash held by banks.
examples.zh: 我们核查这个统计序列对「流通中货币」的定义是否包括银行持有的现金。

words.enDefinition: an arrangement seeking to maintain a currency at a specified rate or narrow range against an anchor currency or basket

examples.en: The model's currency peg set a target rate against a basket of currencies used by trading partners.
examples.zh: 模型中的「货币盯住安排」以贸易伙伴所用货币构成的一篮子为基准设定目标汇率。

examples.en: We compared the currency peg with a system allowing the exchange rate to move more freely.
examples.zh: 我们把「货币盯住安排」与允许汇率更自由变动的制度作了比较。

collocations: analyse pressure on a currency peg

words.enDefinition: an official increase in a currency's fixed or targeted value against its anchor

examples.en: The model's currency revaluation raised the official value of the local currency against the one it followed.
examples.zh: 模型中的「官方上调本币平价」提高了本币相对所盯住货币的官方价值。

examples.en: Our tutor used currency revaluation to distinguish a change in the official parity from ordinary daily trading movements.
examples.zh: 导师用「官方上调本币平价」区分官方平价变化与日常交易波动。

collocations: study the effects of currency revaluation

words.enDefinition: the difference between current account credits and debits for trade in goods and services and primary and secondary income

examples.en: The current account balance differed from the goods balance because the report also included income and services.
examples.zh: 「经常账户差额」与货物差额不同，因为报告也计入收入及服务。

examples.en: We checked which component accounted for most of the change in the current account balance that year.
examples.zh: 我们核查了哪个组成项目解释了当年「经常账户差额」的大部分变化。

collocations: explain a change in the current account balance

words.enDefinition: The actual prices prevailing in the period measured, used without adjustment for changes over time.

examples.en: The first column values each year's output at current prices in our fictional economy.
examples.zh: 第一列用「现价」计量虚构经济体各年的产出。

examples.en: We read both years at current prices before looking at the adjustment in the final column.
examples.zh: 查看最后一列的调整前，我们先看两个年度按「现价」计量的数值。

words.enDefinition: a trade arrangement removing duties on substantially all internal trade and applying substantially the same external duties or trade regulations

examples.en: The customs union in the example set a shared duty on goods arriving from economies outside the group.
examples.zh: 示例中的「关税同盟」为从集团外经济体进口的商品设定统一关税。

examples.en: We discussed how the customs union affected trade between its members and with neighbouring nonmember economies.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「关税同盟」怎样影响成员间贸易以及与邻近非成员经济体的贸易。

collocations: analyse the effects of a customs union

words.enDefinition: The part of movements in an economic series attributed to fluctuations around its underlying trend.

examples.en: The worksheet shows the cyclical component separately from the estimated trend in total production.
examples.zh: 练习表分别显示总产出的「周期成分」和估计趋势。

examples.en: The cyclical component turns positive when measured output moves above the underlying trend in our example.
examples.zh: 在示例里，实测产出超过长期趋势时，「周期成分」转正。

words.enDefinition: A business-cycle turning point at which an expansion ends and a contraction begins.

examples.en: The chart marks the cyclical peak just before the broad decline in the sample economy.
examples.zh: 图上在示例经济体普遍下滑前标出了「周期顶峰」。

examples.en: We compared the date of the cyclical peak with the date of the highest output reading.
examples.zh: 我们比较了「周期顶峰」所在的日期与最高产出读数所在的日期。

words.enDefinition: A business-cycle turning point at which a contraction ends and an expansion begins.

examples.en: The cyclical trough appears just before several measures of activity start rising in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中，多项经济活动指标回升前出现「周期谷底」。

examples.en: The tutor asked how the cyclical trough was located in the fictional monthly series.
examples.zh: 老师问是如何在虚构的月度序列中确定「周期谷底」的。

words.enDefinition: Unemployment associated with weak economic activity during a downturn

examples.en: The model shows cyclical unemployment among restaurant workers who lose jobs after overall spending falls.
examples.zh: 模型显示，总体支出下降后失去工作的餐饮业劳动者属于「周期性失业」。

examples.en: We separated cyclical unemployment from the unemployment that would remain after demand recovered.
examples.zh: 我们将「周期性失业」与需求恢复后仍会存在的失业分开。

words.zhGloss: 周期调整后的预算余额
words.enDefinition: Estimated budget balance after removing the temporary effects of economic fluctuations
acceptedZhAnswers: 周期调整后的预算余额

examples.en: The example uses a cyclically adjusted budget balance to separate weak tax receipts from other budget changes.
examples.zh: 该例使用「周期调整后的预算余额」，将税收收入因经济疲弱而减少的影响与其他预算变化分离。

examples.en: Our estimate of the cyclically adjusted budget balance changes when we revise assumed potential output.
examples.zh: 调整假定的潜在产出之后，我们对「周期调整后的预算余额」的估值也发生了变化。

collocations: calculate the cyclically adjusted budget balance
improve the cyclically adjusted budget balance

words.enDefinition: A set of recorded estimates as they appeared at a particular release date.

examples.en: We checked the data vintage before comparing the original growth estimate with the revised figure.
examples.zh: 我们先核对「数据发布版本」，再把最初公布的增长估计与修订值作比较。

examples.en: The worksheet labels the data vintage so readers know when its GDP figures were published.
examples.zh: 练习注明「数据发布版本」，让读者知道其 GDP 数据何时公布。

words.enDefinition: Loss of a stable anchor for longer-term expectations about price changes

examples.en: We discussed possible de-anchoring of inflation expectations after long-term survey forecasts moved away from the target.
examples.zh: 长期调查预测偏离目标后，我们讨论了「通胀预期脱锚」的可能性。

examples.en: The case study illustrates de-anchoring of inflation expectations after a series of unexpected price increases.
examples.zh: 案例展示了一连串意外涨价后出现的「通胀预期脱锚」。

collocations: risk of de-anchoring of inflation expectations
evidence of de-anchoring of inflation expectations

words.enDefinition: an exchange arrangement classified from observed policy and exchange rate behaviour rather than only from official announcements

examples.en: The de facto exchange rate regime was classified using how the currency actually moved in the example report.
examples.zh: 示例报告根据货币实际变动情况，对「实际汇率制度」进行了分类。

examples.en: We compared the de facto exchange rate regime with the arrangement officially described in the annual summary.
examples.zh: 我们把「实际汇率制度」和年度综述中正式说明的制度作了比较。

collocations: classify a de facto exchange rate regime
identify the de facto exchange rate regime
compare the de facto regime with the official arrangement

words.enDefinition: the exchange rate arrangement formally announced or reported by the authorities

examples.en: The table listed the de jure exchange rate regime using the country's official statement for the period.
examples.zh: 表格依照该国本期官方声明，列出「官方公布的汇率制度」。

examples.en: The tutor explained that the de jure exchange rate regime could differ from patterns visible in the data.
examples.zh: 导师说明，「官方公布的汇率制度」可能与数据中可见的实际走势不一致。

collocations: report a de jure exchange rate regime
identify the de jure exchange rate regime
compare de jure and observed exchange arrangements

words.enDefinition: Leftward curve shift reflecting fewer purchases at each price shown

examples.en: The worksheet shows a decrease in demand for printers after students switch to digital notes.
examples.zh: 习题显示，学生改用电子笔记后，打印机的「需求减少」。

examples.en: A decrease in demand can lower both price and quantity when the supply curve slopes upward.
examples.zh: 供给曲线向上倾斜时，「需求减少」可能同时降低价格和交易量。

words.enDefinition: Leftward curve shift reflecting fewer goods offered at each price shown

examples.en: The class graphed a decrease in supply for baked goods after a supplier raised flour prices.
examples.zh: 一家供应商提高面粉价格后，全班画图表示烘焙食品的「供给减少」。

examples.en: A decrease in supply for pears can lead to a higher market clearing price.
examples.zh: 梨的「供给减少」可能使市场出清价格上升。

words.enDefinition: a case where output grows by a smaller proportion than the common proportional increase in all inputs

examples.en: Our decreasing returns to scale example produced less than twice as much output after doubling the two inputs.
examples.zh: 在「规模报酬递减」的示例里，两种投入加倍后，产量没有达到两倍。

examples.en: We looked for decreasing returns to scale by scaling every input together across several points in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中，我们在几个不同点同时等比例增加各项投入，判断是否有「规模报酬递减」。

collocations: test for decreasing returns to scale

words.enDefinition: To adjust a series in current prices using a price index to obtain a series in real terms.

examples.en: We learned to deflate a nominal series before comparing the volume of production over time.
examples.zh: 我们先学会「对名义序列进行平减」，再比较不同时期的生产量。

examples.en: The worksheet asks us to deflate a nominal series using the index shown beside it.
examples.zh: 练习要求我们使用一旁列出的指数「对名义序列进行平减」。

collocations: deflate a nominal series with an index
deflate a nominal series for comparison
deflate a nominal series by sector

words.enDefinition: Lowest price that reduces the quantity demanded to zero in a model

examples.en: We found the demand choke price by setting ticket purchases to zero in the equation.
examples.zh: 我们把等式中的购票数量设为零，求出了「需求截断价格」。

examples.en: On our graph, the demand choke price is where the demand curve reaches the vertical axis.
examples.zh: 在我们的图里，「需求截断价格」对应需求曲线与纵轴的交点。

words.enDefinition: a graph showing the quantity buyers are willing and able to purchase at each possible price, holding other influences fixed

examples.en: Our demand curve slopes downward because buyers want more at lower prices.
examples.zh: 我们的「需求曲线」向下倾斜，因为价格越低，买家想买的就越多。

examples.en: Each point on the demand curve pairs a price with a planned purchase quantity.
examples.zh: 「需求曲线」上的每个点都对应一个价格和该价格下的计划购买量。

words.enDefinition: Amount of spendable balances people wish to hold under given conditions

examples.en: The model shows greater demand for money when households make more purchases each week.
examples.zh: 这个模型显示，家庭每周购买活动增加时「货币需求」变大。

examples.en: We compared the demand for money at two interest rates while holding income fixed.
examples.zh: 我们保持收入不变，比较了两种利率下的「货币需求」。

collocations: increase in the demand for money

words.enDefinition: Price growth driven by aggregate spending pressing against available productive capacity

examples.en: We modeled demand-pull inflation by increasing spending while keeping productive capacity unchanged.
examples.zh: 我们在产能不变的情况下增加支出，以模拟「需求拉动型通胀」。

examples.en: The example links demand-pull inflation to strong spending when factories are already busy.
examples.zh: 示例把工厂已经满负荷时的旺盛支出与「需求拉动型通胀」联系起来。

words.enDefinition: Table pairing possible prices with amounts buyers would buy at each

examples.en: We built a demand schedule for campus hoodies using the numbers from the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们用习题的数据编制了校园连帽衫的「需求表」。

examples.en: The first row of our demand schedule shows what buyers would purchase at ten dollars.
examples.zh: 我们「需求表」的第一行显示买家在价格为十美元时会买多少。

words.enDefinition: Factor besides the good's own price that changes purchases at given prices

examples.en: The lecturer treated hotter weather as a demand shifter for reusable water bottles.
examples.zh: 老师把天气变热视为可重复使用水瓶的「需求曲线移动因素」。

examples.en: Income is a demand shifter in the model because it affects purchases at unchanged prices.
examples.zh: 在这个模型中，收入是「需求曲线移动因素」，因为价格不变时它也会影响购买量。

words.enDefinition: Sudden change in the amounts buyers want at existing prices

examples.en: The festival created a positive demand shock for food stalls in the classroom simulation.
examples.zh: 在课堂模拟中，节庆活动给餐饮摊位带来了一次正向「需求冲击」。

examples.en: To show a negative demand shock, we moved the ticket demand curve to the left.
examples.zh: 为了表示负向「需求冲击」，我们把门票需求曲线向左移。

collocations: respond to a negative demand shock

words.enDefinition: A diagnostic for a jump in the distribution density of the running variable at the cutoff.

examples.en: The density continuity test checks whether example scores cluster unevenly just above and below the cutoff.
examples.zh: 「密度连续性检验」检查示例成绩在阈值上下一小段范围内的集中程度是否不均。

examples.en: We interpreted the density continuity test alongside the known rules for assigning scores in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们结合已知的评分规则解读「密度连续性检验」。

collocations: density continuity test at the cutoff

words.enDefinition: demand for labour arising from customers' demand for the goods or services that workers help produce

examples.en: The exercise illustrated derived demand for labour when growing demand for repairs led the shop to hire technicians.
examples.zh: 维修需求增长，店铺因而增聘技师，练习用这一变化说明「劳动的派生需求」。

examples.en: We used derived demand for labour to explain why fewer ticket sales could reduce the need for staff.
examples.zh: 我们用「劳动的派生需求」解释为什么门票销量减少可能降低用工需求。

collocations: estimate a shift in derived demand for labour

words.enDefinition: Inference that uses a specified assignment or sampling design as the source of uncertainty about an estimate.

examples.en: Design-based inference uses the known lottery assignment to quantify uncertainty in the simulated tutoring result.
examples.zh: 「基于设计的推断」利用已知的抽签分配机制量化模拟辅导结果的不确定性。

examples.en: The lesson explains how design-based inference reflects which groups actually entered the classroom lottery.
examples.zh: 课上说明「基于设计的推断」如何反映哪些组实际参加了课堂抽签。

words.enDefinition: the study of economic transformation, living conditions and policy challenges during development

examples.en: The development economics course compared improvements in household living conditions with changes in national income over time.
examples.zh: 「发展经济学」课程比较家庭生活条件的改善与国民收入随时间发生的变化。

examples.en: We used development economics readings to discuss why some rural households had difficulty accessing formal jobs.
examples.zh: 我们用「发展经济学」阅读资料讨论为何有些农村家庭难以进入正规就业岗位。

collocations: read a study in development economics

words.enDefinition: An allocation game in which one player chooses the division and the recipient cannot reject it.

examples.en: The dictator game let one student divide ten tokens without asking the other student to approve.
examples.zh: 「独裁者博弈」允许一名学生分配十枚代币，无需征得另一名学生同意。

examples.en: Our tutor compared the dictator game with a version in which the second player could reject.
examples.zh: 老师把「独裁者博弈」与第二位参与者可以拒绝提议的版本作了比较。

collocations: compare allocations in a dictator game
contrast a dictator game with an ultimatum game

words.enDefinition: A method that compares changes over time in a treated group with changes in a comparison group.

examples.en: Difference-in-differences compares the change in attendance at treated schools with the change at comparison schools.
examples.zh: 「双重差分法」把接受处理的学校与比较学校的出勤率变化进行比较。

examples.en: We used difference-in-differences under stated assumptions to estimate the effect of the simulated tutoring programme.
examples.zh: 我们在给定假设下，使用「双重差分法」估计模拟辅导项目的效应。

words.enDefinition: A difference in the rate or pattern of loss to follow-up across groups being compared.

examples.en: Differential attrition could occur if a smaller share of one group completes the final classroom survey.
examples.zh: 如果课堂调查中一个组完成末次问卷的学生比例较低，就可能出现「差异性流失」。

examples.en: We checked differential attrition before interpreting the final comparison between the two fictional study groups.
examples.zh: 我们先查「差异性流失」，再解读两个虚构研究组之间的最终比较。

words.enDefinition: a product buyers perceive as different from rival products in attributes such as design, location or quality

examples.en: The differentiated product appealed to customers who wanted a quiet workspace near the railway station in the example.
examples.zh: 示例中的「差异化产品」吸引了想在火车站附近找安静办公场地的顾客。

examples.en: We discussed how a differentiated product could face close substitutes even when no competitor matched every feature.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了即使没有竞争者能匹配所有特点，「差异化产品」为何仍可能面对接近的替代品。

collocations: analyse demand for a differentiated product

words.enDefinition: Declining willingness to give up another good as the first becomes plentiful

examples.en: The curve shows a diminishing marginal rate of substitution as the shopper gets more apples and fewer pears.
examples.zh: 随着购物者得到的苹果增多、梨减少，曲线反映出「边际替代率递减」。

examples.en: We saw a diminishing marginal rate of substitution when each extra cup justified giving up fewer biscuits.
examples.zh: 当人们愿意为多喝一杯茶而放弃的饼干越来越少时，就体现出「边际替代率递减」。

collocations: illustrate a diminishing marginal rate of substitution
assume a diminishing marginal rate of substitution
property of diminishing marginal rate of substitution

words.expression: diminishing marginal rate of technical substitution
words.lemma: diminishing marginal rate of technical substitution
words.enDefinition: the pattern in which additional units of one input replace progressively smaller amounts of another at the same output
acceptedEnVariants: diminishing marginal rate of technical substitution

examples.en: A diminishing marginal rate of technical substitution meant each additional worker replaced fewer machine hours along the curve.
examples.zh: 沿曲线增加一名工人所能替代的机器工时越来越少，体现了「边际技术替代率递减」。

examples.en: We drew a curved isoquant to illustrate a diminishing marginal rate of technical substitution in the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们在练习中画出一条弯曲的等产量曲线，以演示「边际技术替代率递减」。

collocations: illustrate a diminishing marginal rate of technical substitution
assume a diminishing marginal rate of technical substitution
an isoquant with a diminishing marginal rate of technical substitution

words.enDefinition: Pattern in which additional units give progressively smaller gains in satisfaction

examples.en: Our graph illustrates diminishing marginal utility as each additional cup adds less satisfaction.
examples.zh: 我们的图展示了「边际效用递减」，每多喝一杯带来的额外满足感都更少。

examples.en: The example shows diminishing marginal utility even though total satisfaction keeps rising with each serving.
examples.zh: 这个例子说明，尽管每多吃一份都会提高总满足感，仍然可能出现「边际效用递减」。

words.enDefinition: A pattern in which each extra unit of capital adds less output when other inputs stay fixed.

examples.en: Diminishing returns to capital mean that the third machine adds less output than the second in this example.
examples.zh: 示例说明「资本边际报酬递减」意味着第三台机器增加的产出少于第二台。

examples.en: The graph illustrates diminishing returns to capital by holding labour and technology constant throughout.
examples.zh: 图表始终固定劳动和技术水平，用来说明「资本边际报酬递减」。

collocations: evidence of diminishing returns to capital

words.enDefinition: income earned or payable within a direct investment relationship, including relevant dividends, reinvested earnings and interest under the reporting framework

examples.en: The exercise included reinvested earnings in direct investment income even though they were not paid out as cash.
examples.zh: 练习把再投资收益计入「直接投资收益」，尽管没有用现金支付收益。

examples.en: We located direct investment income in the primary income table before reading the example's investment transaction figures.
examples.zh: 我们在初次收入表中找到「直接投资收益」，再看示例里的投资交易数字。

words.enDefinition: The vector of payoffs the players receive if they fail to reach a bargain.

examples.en: We used the disagreement point to show what both clubs would receive without a shared booking.
examples.zh: 我们用「谈判破裂点」说明未达成共同预订时两个社团各能得到什么。

examples.en: Our tutor changed the disagreement point before recalculating how the shared time would be divided.
examples.zh: 老师先改变「谈判破裂点」，再重新计算共享时间会怎样分配。

collocations: compare offers with the disagreement point
set the disagreement point in a bargaining model

words.enDefinition: US Federal Reserve lending facility for eligible institutions posting acceptable collateral

examples.en: The US banking example uses the discount window to illustrate short-term central bank lending.
examples.zh: 美国银行业案例通过「贴现窗口」展示了央行短期放贷。

examples.en: Our reading compares the discount window with borrowing at a market interest rate.
examples.zh: 阅读材料将「贴现窗口」与按市场利率借款作了比较。

words.enDefinition: A payoff expressed in present terms by giving later rewards less weight than earlier rewards.

examples.en: We calculated a discounted payoff for the option that delivered most of its points later.
examples.zh: 我们为大部分积分较晚发放的选项计算了「折现收益」。

examples.en: The tutor compared an immediate payoff with the discounted payoff from waiting one more round.
examples.zh: 老师比较了立刻获得的收益与再等一轮所得的「折现收益」。

collocations: calculate total discounted payoff over several rounds

words.zhGloss: 因前景不佳而放弃求职者
words.enDefinition: US marginally attached people not currently searching because of poor job prospects
acceptedZhAnswers: 因前景不佳而放弃求职者

examples.en: The survey counted some respondents as discouraged workers after they stopped expecting suitable openings.
examples.zh: 调查将一些不再相信会有合适岗位的受访者归为「因前景不佳而放弃求职者」。

examples.en: Under the US definition, discouraged workers are outside the labor force unless they resume searching.
examples.zh: 按美国的定义，「因前景不佳而放弃求职者」在恢复求职前不计入劳动力人口。

collocations: discouraged workers outside the labor force

words.enDefinition: Deliberate changes in taxation or public spending through new policy decisions

examples.en: The lecture illustrates discretionary fiscal policy with a newly approved increase in public spending.
examples.zh: 课堂中新批准的公共支出增长是「主动财政政策」的一个例子。

examples.en: We contrasted discretionary fiscal policy with tax revenues changing automatically when household incomes fall.
examples.zh: 我们把「主动财政政策」与家庭收入下降时税收自动变化的情形作了比较。

words.enDefinition: the increase in long-run average cost as production expands beyond the relevant scale

examples.en: The diseconomies of scale in our example came from coordinating deliveries across too many separate workshops.
examples.zh: 示例中的「规模不经济」来自为过多分开的车间协调配送。

examples.en: We looked for diseconomies of scale on the upward-sloping part of the long-run average cost curve.
examples.zh: 我们在长期平均成本曲线的上升段找「规模不经济」。

collocations: explain a source of diseconomies of scale

words.enDefinition: higher cost from producing different outputs jointly than from providing each separately

examples.en: The sample bakery encountered diseconomies of scope because switching between products required costly cleaning and repeated setup.
examples.zh: 示例面包店切换产品时要付出较高的清洁费用并反复做准备，出现了「范围不经济」。

examples.en: We compared the joint costs with separate production costs to look for diseconomies of scope in our model.
examples.zh: 我们比较联合生产和分开生产的成本，判断模型中是否出现「范围不经济」。

words.enDefinition: Decline in a positive inflation rate while aggregate prices keep rising

examples.en: The chart shows disinflation when the annual price increase slows but stays positive.
examples.zh: 当年度价格涨幅放慢但仍为正时，图中显示的是「通胀放缓」。

examples.en: During disinflation, the price index in our example continued to move upward.
examples.zh: 在「通胀放缓」期间，例子中的价格指数仍继续上涨。

words.enDefinition: A tax that changes relative prices or incentives and can therefore alter economic decisions.

examples.en: The worksheet showed a distortionary tax changing which of two goods consumers chose in the model.
examples.zh: 练习表展示了「扭曲性税收」怎样改变模型中消费者在两种商品之间的选择。

examples.en: Our tutor compared a distortionary tax with a payment that did not depend on individual behaviour.
examples.zh: 老师把「扭曲性税收」与一项不取决于个人行为的缴款作了比较。

collocations: analyse responses to a distortionary tax
compare a distortionary tax with a fixed levy

words.enDefinition: How a policy's benefits or costs differ among people or groups.

examples.en: The report described the distributional impact of the fee by separating frequent users from occasional users.
examples.zh: 报告把常用者和偶尔使用者分开，说明收费的「分配影响」。

examples.en: We studied distributional impact even though the two options had the same total net benefit.
examples.zh: 尽管这两个选项具有同样的总净收益，我们仍研究了「分配影响」。

collocations: compare the distributional impacts of two policies

words.enDefinition: Factors applied to gains and losses of different groups to reflect an explicit welfare judgment.

examples.en: The worksheet used distributional weights to illustrate how equal payments could receive different importance in welfare analysis.
examples.zh: 练习表用「分配权重」说明，在福利分析里金额相同的付款怎样可能具有不同重要性。

examples.en: We recalculated the policy comparison using different distributional weights for the two hypothetical groups.
examples.zh: 我们对两个假设群体采用不同的「分配权重」，重新计算政策对比结果。

collocations: test the sensitivity to distributional weights

words.enDefinition: Production attributed to resident producer units of an economy, regardless of their owners' nationality.

examples.en: The worksheet counts the local factory's output as domestic production even when its owners live abroad.
examples.zh: 练习纸把本地工厂的产出归入「境内生产」，即使工厂所有者住在国外。

examples.en: We separated domestic production from imported goods before working through the expenditure example in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们先把「境内生产」与进口商品区分开，再做支出法示例。

words.enDefinition: the domestic price of one good expressed in units of another good or as a price ratio

examples.en: The domestic relative price of rice rose when rice became more expensive but wheat prices stayed unchanged.
examples.zh: 小麦价格不变而大米涨价时，大米的「国内相对价格」上升了。

examples.en: We found the domestic relative price from the slope of the budget line before comparing consumption bundles.
examples.zh: 我们根据预算线斜率求出「国内相对价格」，再比较消费组合。

collocations: compare domestic relative prices across economies
measure a change in the domestic relative price

words.enDefinition: the portion of exports' value created in the exporting economy through its own production activities

examples.en: The report calculated domestic value added in exports by subtracting the foreign value embedded in those exports.
examples.zh: 报告从出口价值扣除其中包含的国外增加值，计算「出口中的国内增加值」。

examples.en: We compared domestic value added in exports across industries that relied on very different shares of imported inputs.
examples.zh: 我们比较不同产业的「出口中的国内增加值」，这些产业对进口要素的依赖程度很不同。

collocations: estimate domestic value added in exports
report domestic value added in exports
compare domestic value added in exports across industries

words.zhGloss: 可通过支配关系求解的博弈
words.enDefinition: In the strict-dominance setting, a game with one strategy profile left after repeated elimination of dominated strategies.
acceptedZhAnswers: 可通过支配关系求解的博弈

examples.en: Our worksheet presented a dominance-solvable game with a single pair of choices remaining after the eliminations.
examples.zh: 练习表给出一个「可通过支配关系求解的博弈」，剔除之后只剩一对选择。

examples.en: The class checked whether the revised payoff matrix still described a dominance-solvable game.
examples.zh: 同学们检查了修改后的收益矩阵是否仍表示一种「可通过支配关系求解的博弈」。

words.enDefinition: a firm with enough market influence to set its own output or price while smaller competitors respond

examples.en: The dominant firm considered how competing suppliers would respond before choosing the price in our diagram.
examples.zh: 我们图中的「主导厂商」考虑其他供应商会怎样回应，再选定价格。

examples.en: We estimated the market demand available to a dominant firm after accounting for the output of smaller suppliers.
examples.zh: 计入较小供应商的产出之后，我们估计了留给「主导厂商」的市场需求。

collocations: analyse the pricing of a dominant firm
compare a dominant firm with smaller rivals

words.enDefinition: A sensitivity design that re-estimates a discontinuity after excluding observations nearest to the assignment cutoff.

examples.en: Donut regression discontinuity excludes the scores nearest the threshold in our simulated classroom study.
examples.zh: 在模拟课堂研究里，「环形断点回归」排除最靠近阈值的成绩。

examples.en: We compared donut regression discontinuity results with estimates using all scores near the fictional threshold.
examples.zh: 我们把「环形断点回归」结果与使用虚构阈值附近全部成绩的估计作了比较。

words.enDefinition: The error of including the same economic value more than once in a total.

examples.en: The production example avoids double counting by subtracting the value of flour used to make bread.
examples.zh: 生产示例扣除制作面包所用面粉的价值，以避免「重复计算」。

examples.en: We spotted double counting when the same final purchase appeared twice in the classroom total.
examples.zh: 看到同一笔最终购买在课堂总量里出现两次时，我们发现了「重复计算」。

words.enDefinition: Two recessionary downturns separated by a brief period of renewed growth.

examples.en: The hypothetical double-dip recession includes a brief rebound between two widely shared declines in activity.
examples.zh: 假设的「双底衰退」在两次普遍的经济活动下滑之间出现短暂反弹。

examples.en: We compared the figures before deciding whether the classroom example resembled a double-dip recession.
examples.zh: 判断课堂示例是否类似「双底衰退」之前，我们比较了相关数据。

words.enDefinition: Tendency for prices to fall when sellers compete for limited demand

examples.en: In our case study, unsold flowers put downward pressure on prices at the campus market.
examples.zh: 在我们的案例中，卖不掉的鲜花给校园市场带来了「价格下跌压力」。

examples.en: The diagram illustrates downward pressure on prices after more sellers enter the same small market.
examples.zh: 这张图展示了更多卖家进入同一个小市场后出现的「价格下跌压力」。

words.enDefinition: US policy goals of maximum employment and stable prices, considered together

examples.en: The Fed case uses the dual mandate to discuss employment alongside inflation.
examples.zh: 关于美联储的案例用「双重使命」说明为何把就业和通胀一同考虑。

examples.en: We compared decisions under a dual mandate with those under a price stability objective alone.
examples.zh: 我们比较了「双重使命」下的决策和只有物价稳定这一目标时的决策。

words.enDefinition: Perfect collinearity caused by including every indicator for a categorical variable together with an intercept.

examples.en: The dummy variable trap appears when the worksheet includes every school category and an intercept.
examples.zh: 练习把所有学校类别的指示变量和截距一并纳入时，出现了「虚拟变量陷阱」。

examples.en: We avoided the dummy variable trap by leaving one category out of the regression.
examples.zh: 我们在回归中省略一个类别，以避免「虚拟变量陷阱」。

words.enDefinition: An auction starting at a high announced price that falls until someone accepts it.

examples.en: In the Dutch auction, the displayed price fell until one participant accepted it for the sample book.
examples.zh: 在「荷兰式拍卖」中，显示价格不断下降，直到一位参与者接受该价格购买示例图书。

examples.en: We drew the price sequence for the Dutch auction before comparing it with the rising-price format.
examples.zh: 和价格上升的形式比较之前，我们先画出了「荷兰式拍卖」的价格序列。

collocations: accept the current price in a Dutch auction

words.enDefinition: broadening the industries or activities from which an economy obtains production, employment or income

examples.en: The policy example tracked economic diversification as several new manufacturing and service sectors began to grow.
examples.zh: 几个新的制造和服务行业开始增长时，政策示例跟踪了「经济多元化」。

examples.en: We discussed economic diversification after finding that the region still relied on one main source of revenue.
examples.zh: 发现该地区仍依赖一个主要收入来源后，我们讨论了「经济多元化」。

words.enDefinition: A business-cycle phase during which overall economic activity generally increases.

examples.en: The exercise shows economic expansion as production rises across several industries for many months.
examples.zh: 在练习中，多个行业的生产连续数月上升，表现为「经济扩张」。

examples.en: We considered which indicators support the classification of the later period as an economic expansion.
examples.zh: 我们研究了哪些指标支持将后面时段归为「经济扩张」。

words.enDefinition: A lasting effect of a temporary economic disturbance after its immediate cause has passed.

examples.en: The tutor used economic hysteresis to explain why potential production stayed lower after the temporary downturn.
examples.zh: 老师用「经济迟滞效应」解释了为何暂时下滑结束后，潜在产出仍处于较低水平。

examples.en: The example shows economic hysteresis through a lasting decline in investment after a brief contraction.
examples.zh: 示例中，短暂收缩后投资持续下降，反映了「经济迟滞效应」。

words.enDefinition: total revenue minus all explicit and implicit economic costs of using the firm's resources

examples.en: The economic profit fell after we included the earnings the owner could have received in another occupation.
examples.zh: 计入业主从事其他职业原本能获得的收入后，「经济利润」下降了。

examples.en: We compared economic profit for two producers that reported the same accounting profit but owned different assets.
examples.zh: 两家生产者报告的会计利润相同，但拥有的资产不同，我们比较了它们的「经济利润」。

collocations: account for opportunity costs when calculating economic profit

words.enDefinition: An effect large enough to matter in the economic context being studied.

examples.en: The seminar asks whether the small estimated wage difference represents an economically meaningful effect in this example.
examples.zh: 研讨课要求判断，示例中估计出的微小工资差异是否属于「具有经济意义的效应」。

examples.en: We judged whether the estimate represented an economically meaningful effect by comparing it with typical hourly pay.
examples.zh: 我们把估计值与典型小时工资比较，判断它是否代表「具有经济意义的效应」。

collocations: magnitude of an economically meaningful effect

words.enDefinition: a cost advantage from producing multiple outputs together rather than producing them separately

examples.en: We found economies of scope when one kitchen could prepare both menus more cheaply than two separate kitchens.
examples.zh: 一个厨房制作两套菜单的成本比两个厨房分开做更低，我们发现了「范围经济」。

examples.en: The producer benefited from economies of scope because the same delivery route could handle both kinds of orders.
examples.zh: 同一条配送线路可以送两种订单，生产者因此受益于「范围经济」。

words.enDefinition: Level near which additional policy rate cuts become impractical or ineffective

examples.en: The model reaches the effective lower bound before exploring other ways to loosen monetary policy.
examples.zh: 模型先达到「有效利率下限」，再探讨其他放松货币政策的方式。

examples.en: We discussed why estimates of the effective lower bound can differ across banking systems.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了为什么不同银行体系对「有效利率下限」的估计会不同。

collocations: policy at the effective lower bound

words.enDefinition: the proportional change in domestic value added caused by tariffs and related measures in the specified model

examples.en: The effective rate of protection fell when the imported input tariff increased and the output tariff stayed unchanged.
examples.zh: 进口投入品关税上升而产成品关税不变时，「有效保护率」下降。

examples.en: Our class calculated the effective rate of protection by comparing domestic value added with its free-trade level.
examples.zh: 同学们将国内增加值与自由贸易下的水平比较，以计算「有效保护率」。

collocations: calculate the effective rate of protection
interpret the effective rate of protection

words.enDefinition: Demand for which purchases change proportionally more than the own price

examples.en: In our example of elastic demand, a small price rise sharply reduces ticket purchases.
examples.zh: 在我们「富有弹性的需求」的例子中，价格小幅上涨就会使购票量急剧减少。

examples.en: The chart illustrates elastic demand because quantity changed much more in percentage terms.
examples.zh: 这张图展示了「富有弹性的需求」，因为数量的百分比变化大得多。

words.enDefinition: Supply for which the amount offered changes proportionally more than price

examples.en: The worksheet illustrates elastic supply because the quantity offered rises proportionally more than the price.
examples.zh: 习题用供给量增幅大于价格涨幅的情况来说明「富有弹性的供给」。

examples.en: In our example of elastic supply, a modest price increase brings many more bikes onto the market.
examples.zh: 在我们「富有弹性的供给」的例子中，价格小幅上升，就有更多自行车供应市场。

words.enDefinition: Number measuring the proportional response of one variable to another

examples.en: The elasticity coefficient lets us compare how purchases respond across products sold in different units.
examples.zh: 借助「弹性系数」，我们可以比较以不同单位销售的商品的购买量反应。

examples.en: We kept the sign of the elasticity coefficient when discussing whether products are substitutes.
examples.zh: 在讨论商品是否互为替代品时，我们保留了「弹性系数」的正负号。

words.enDefinition: A limit on total emissions covered by a policy over a specified period.

examples.en: The emissions cap determined how many allowances the classroom market could issue for the first period.
examples.zh: 「排放总量上限」决定了课堂市场在第一个时期可以发放多少配额。

examples.en: Our group lowered the emissions cap in the simulation and recalculated the number of available permits.
examples.zh: 我们组在模拟中降低了「排放总量上限」，并重新计算可用的配额数量。

words.enDefinition: A charge based on the amount of pollution an activity releases.

examples.en: The example applied an emissions charge to each unit that the simulated factories continued to release.
examples.zh: 例题对模拟工厂继续排放的每个单位实行「排放收费」。

examples.en: We compared an emissions charge with a rule that put a fixed limit on every factory.
examples.zh: 我们把「排放收费」与对每家工厂都设定固定上限的规定作了比较。

collocations: compare an emissions charge with a permit price

words.enDefinition: The interval over which covered emissions are assessed against the allowances required by a program.

examples.en: The simulation measured factory releases throughout the emissions compliance period before checking the allowances held.
examples.zh: 模拟记录整个「排放合规期」内各工厂的排放情况，再核查它们持有的配额。

examples.en: Our worksheet compared two policies using the same length of emissions compliance period for both.
examples.zh: 练习表对两种政策采用相同的「排放合规期」长度进行比较。

collocations: report emissions for a compliance period

words.enDefinition: Share of the reference population counted as employed in the survey

examples.en: The employment-to-population ratio fell when employment grew more slowly than the population used for comparison.
examples.zh: 当就业人数的增长慢于参照人口时，「就业人口比」下降了。

examples.en: The class compared the employment-to-population ratio for adults in two different age brackets.
examples.zh: 全班比较了两个年龄组成年人的「就业人口比」。

words.enDefinition: A condition in which a regressor is related to the model's unobserved error term.

examples.en: Endogeneity is possible when prior skills affect both training decisions and wages in our classroom example.
examples.zh: 课堂示例中，既往技能同时影响培训决定和实测工资时，可能存在「内生性」。

examples.en: The worksheet asks what kind of endogeneity the proposed instrument is intended to address.
examples.zh: 练习问的是拟议工具变量旨在处理哪种「内生性」。

words.enDefinition: A growth model in which mechanisms within the economy explain ongoing growth in output per person.

examples.en: The endogenous growth model links the creation of new ideas to the choices made within the economy.
examples.zh: 「内生增长模型」把新知识的形成与经济体内部的决策联系起来。

examples.en: We compared an endogenous growth model with one that takes technological progress as given.
examples.zh: 我们比较了「内生增长模型」和把技术进步视为给定因素的模型。

collocations: knowledge in an endogenous growth model

words.enDefinition: A regressor that is correlated with the disturbance in the equation being estimated.

examples.en: Training participation is an endogenous regressor if omitted motivation influences both participation and subsequent earnings.
examples.zh: 如果遗漏的积极性同时影响参与培训的决定和后续收入，培训参与就是「内生解释变量」。

examples.en: We labelled the endogenous regressor before writing the first equation in our classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 课堂练习中，我们先标出「内生解释变量」，再写下第一个方程。

words.enDefinition: Graph showing demand for one good as income varies at fixed prices

examples.en: We drew an Engel curve for bus trips with fares held constant across households.
examples.zh: 我们在各家庭面对的车费相同的情况下，绘制了公交出行的「恩格尔曲线」。

examples.en: The Engel curve slopes downward where rising income reduces purchases of the item.
examples.zh: 当收入提高、商品购买量减少时，「恩格尔曲线」向下倾斜。

collocations: Engel curve for a normal good

words.enDefinition: An open auction in which bids rise until the highest remaining bidder wins.

examples.en: The classroom English auction began with a low price and ended when only one bidder remained.
examples.zh: 课堂的「英式拍卖」从低价开始，只剩一名竞价者时结束。

examples.en: We compared an English auction with a demonstration where offers were written privately on cards.
examples.zh: 我们把「英式拍卖」与将报价私下写在卡片上的演示作了比较。

collocations: model an English auction as ascending bids

words.enDefinition: the way the set of firms in a market changes over time as producers join or leave

examples.en: The entry and exit dynamics in our model slowly changed the number of sellers after demand increased.
examples.zh: 需求增加后，模型的「企业进入与退出动态」逐步改变了卖家数量。

examples.en: We discussed entry and exit dynamics for the industry after switching from a short-run to a long-run model.
examples.zh: 从短期模型转为长期模型后，我们讨论该行业的「企业进入与退出动态」。

collocations: compare entry and exit dynamics across markets

words.enDefinition: A sequence of moves that occurs under the specified equilibrium strategies, including possible chance outcomes.

examples.en: On the equilibrium path, the second club accepted the proposed time in the first round.
examples.zh: 沿「均衡路径」，第二个社团会在第一轮接受提议的时段。

examples.en: We traced an equilibrium path through the tree after identifying which strategy each player would use.
examples.zh: 确定各参与者采用的策略后，我们沿博弈树追踪了一条「均衡路径」。

words.enDefinition: The payoff a player receives, or expects to receive, under an equilibrium strategy profile.

examples.en: We calculated each club's equilibrium payoff after finding the stable pair of room choices.
examples.zh: 找到稳定的教室选择组合之后，我们计算了各社团的「均衡收益」。

examples.en: The tutor compared the equilibrium payoff with what the same group earned when both teams cooperated.
examples.zh: 老师把「均衡收益」与两队都合作时同一小组的所得作了比较。

words.enDefinition: Price at which buyers and sellers plan to trade the same quantity

examples.en: We found the equilibrium price by setting the two quantity equations equal to each other.
examples.zh: 我们把两个数量方程设为相等，求出了「均衡价格」。

examples.en: With a larger harvest, our model predicts a lower equilibrium price for strawberries.
examples.zh: 草莓收成增加时，模型预测其「均衡价格」会下降。

words.enDefinition: Amount buyers want and sellers offer at the price that balances them

examples.en: The equilibrium quantity of notebooks rose after the supply curve shifted to the right.
examples.zh: 供给曲线向右移动后，笔记本的「均衡数量」增加了。

examples.en: We substituted the equilibrium price into the demand equation to find the equilibrium quantity.
examples.zh: 我们把均衡价格代入需求方程，求出了「均衡数量」。

words.enDefinition: Choosing or predicting one equilibrium when the same game allows several.

examples.en: The class discussed equilibrium selection because either shared booking time could be stable in the model.
examples.zh: 模型中的两个共同预订时段都可能是稳定的，全班因此讨论了「均衡选择」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether a prominent time on the timetable might influence equilibrium selection.
examples.zh: 老师问，日程表上显眼的时段是否会影响「均衡选择」。

words.enDefinition: Tendency of market conditions to return to equilibrium after a disturbance

examples.en: We discussed equilibrium stability by tracing what happens when price starts slightly too high.
examples.zh: 我们通过追踪价格起初略高时会发生什么，讨论了「均衡稳定性」。

examples.en: The model's adjustment rule matters when we examine equilibrium stability after a temporary disturbance.
examples.zh: 研究市场受短期扰动后的「均衡稳定性」时，模型采用的调整规则很重要。

words.enDefinition: Rule of equalizing marginal gains per unit of a shared resource

examples.en: The lecture applies the equimarginal principle when comparing extra satisfaction from the last dollars spent.
examples.zh: 课堂上老师用「等边际原理」比较花出去的最后几美元各带来的额外满足感。

examples.en: We used the equimarginal principle to explain how a shopper allocates spending across goods.
examples.zh: 我们用「等边际原理」解释购物者如何在各类商品之间分配支出。

words.enDefinition: A situation in which improving a specified measure of fairness can reduce overall economic efficiency, or vice versa.

examples.en: The seminar explored an equity-efficiency trade-off by comparing total welfare with the distribution of benefits.
examples.zh: 研讨课将总体福利与收益的分布作比较，探讨「公平与效率的权衡」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether the two policy options actually involved an equity-efficiency trade-off in this model.
examples.zh: 老师问，在这个模型中，两种政策选项是否真的涉及「公平与效率的权衡」。

collocations: discuss the equity-efficiency trade-off in a model

words.enDefinition: Money change at original prices equivalent to the price change's utility effect

examples.en: Our estimate of equivalent variation uses the old prices and the new satisfaction level.
examples.zh: 我们估算「等价变差」时，用的是旧价格和变动后的满足感水平。

examples.en: The instructor compared equivalent variation with the amount needed to restore satisfaction at new prices.
examples.zh: 老师把「等价变差」与按新价格恢复原有满足感所需的金额作了比较。

collocations: equivalent variation for a price increase

words.enDefinition: Survey asking workplaces about payroll jobs, earnings, or employee hours

examples.en: In the US establishment survey, two covered payroll jobs held by one worker are counted separately.
examples.zh: 在美国的「用人单位调查」中，同一名劳动者的两个有薪岗位分别计数。

examples.en: We used the establishment survey to compare payroll jobs at factories and retail stores.
examples.zh: 我们用「用人单位调查」比较工厂和零售门店的有薪岗位。

words.enDefinition: A model indexed by time relative to treatment that can estimate effects by period under stated assumptions.

examples.en: The event study specification allows the fitted attendance effects to differ across relative years in our example.
examples.zh: 示例中的「事件研究设定」允许拟合的出勤效应随相对年份而变化。

examples.en: We wrote an event study specification with indicators for the periods before and after tutoring.
examples.zh: 我们写出一套「事件研究设定」，加入辅导前后各期的指示变量。

words.enDefinition: Time measured relative to when a unit first experiences an event or begins treatment.

examples.en: Event time equals zero in the year when each fictional school first begins offering tutoring.
examples.zh: 各所虚构学校第一次开始辅导的那一年，「事件相对时间」等于零。

examples.en: We aligned the outcome series by event time so that the different starting years could be compared.
examples.zh: 我们按「事件相对时间」对齐结果序列，以便比较不同起始年份。

words.enDefinition: A regression coefficient associated with a particular period relative to treatment in an event study.

examples.en: The event-time coefficient for the first year after tutoring is positive in the simulated exercise.
examples.zh: 在模拟练习里，开始辅导后第一年的「事件相对时间系数」为正。

examples.en: We plotted each event-time coefficient with an interval to show the uncertainty around the estimate.
examples.zh: 我们为每个「事件相对时间系数」画出区间，展示估计的不确定性。

words.enDefinition: the prediction in a standard monopolistic competition model that firms produce below their minimum-average-cost output in long-run equilibrium

examples.en: The tutor drew the excess capacity theorem diagram with output left of the lowest average cost point.
examples.zh: 导师画出「过剩产能定理」的示意图，产量位于平均成本最低点的左侧。

examples.en: We discussed whether the excess capacity theorem applied before assuming a downward-sloping demand curve for each firm.
examples.zh: 给各厂商设定向下倾斜的需求曲线前，我们讨论「过剩产能定理」是否适用。

collocations: state the assumptions of the excess capacity theorem
test the implications of the excess capacity theorem

words.enDefinition: Amount by which intended purchases exceed offers at a given price

examples.en: Below the price where the curves meet, the graph shows excess demand for bike rentals.
examples.zh: 在两条曲线交点对应的价格以下，图上显示自行车租赁存在「超额需求」。

examples.en: Our worksheet records excess demand of twelve tickets at a price of five dollars.
examples.zh: 我们的习题记录了票价为五美元时存在十二张票的「超额需求」。

words.enDefinition: Amount by which offers exceed intended purchases at a given price

examples.en: At the listed price, the table shows excess supply of eight baskets of apples.
examples.zh: 表中显示，按所列价格计算，苹果有八篮的「超额供给」。

examples.en: The graph shows why excess supply arises when price exceeds the two curves' intersection price.
examples.zh: 这张图说明了为什么价格高于两条曲线交点对应的价格时会出现「超额供给」。

words.enDefinition: a rise in the value of a currency relative to another currency or a basket of currencies

examples.en: We observed exchange rate appreciation when the local currency bought more units of the foreign currency than before.
examples.zh: 当本币能买到更多单位的外币时，我们观察到「货币升值」。

examples.en: The tutor checked the quote convention before calling the currency's move exchange rate appreciation in the example.
examples.zh: 导师先核对报价口径，再把示例中的货币变动称为「货币升值」。

collocations: compare the effects of exchange rate appreciation

words.enDefinition: an announced or managed range within which an exchange rate is allowed to move under an arrangement

examples.en: The diagram showed a market rate moving within the exchange rate band defined for the hypothetical economy.
examples.zh: 图中显示市场汇率在为假想经济体设定的「汇率波动区间」内变化。

examples.en: We marked the upper and lower boundaries of the exchange rate band before reviewing the recorded rate.
examples.zh: 我们先标出「汇率波动区间」的上下界，再核查记录的汇率。

collocations: keep a currency within an exchange rate band

words.enDefinition: a fall in the value of a currency relative to another currency or a basket

examples.en: In the example, exchange rate depreciation meant that the local currency bought fewer units of the foreign currency.
examples.zh: 在示例中，「货币贬值」意味着本币可以兑换的外币单位变少。

examples.en: We discussed how exchange rate depreciation affected the local cost of imported inputs in the classroom model.
examples.zh: 我们讨论「货币贬值」如何影响课堂模型中进口投入要素的本币成本。

collocations: study the effects of exchange rate depreciation

words.enDefinition: the extent to which changes in exchange rates are reflected in import, producer or consumer prices

examples.en: The estimated exchange rate pass-through was incomplete because import prices moved by less than the currency did.
examples.zh: 进口价格变动幅度小于货币变动幅度，因此估计的「汇率传导」不完全。

examples.en: We compared exchange rate pass-through to border prices with the response of prices at local shops.
examples.zh: 我们比较了边境价格的「汇率传导」和当地商店价格的反应。

collocations: measure exchange rate pass-through to import prices
compare exchange rate pass-through across products

words.enDefinition: the arrangement governing how a currency's exchange rate is determined or managed

examples.en: The class compared each exchange rate regime before considering how the authorities might respond to external shocks.
examples.zh: 同学们比较了各「汇率制度」，再考虑主管机构可能怎样应对外部冲击。

examples.en: We read the report's description of the exchange rate regime before comparing currency movements across the two economies.
examples.zh: 在比较两个经济体的货币变动之前，我们先看报告对其「汇率制度」的说明。

words.enDefinition: The feasibility of preventing particular users from accessing a good or service.

examples.en: The classroom exercise used a ticketed stream to explain excludability for a service with many viewers.
examples.zh: 课堂练习用凭票观看的直播来说明一项有许多观看者的服务如何体现「排他性」。

examples.en: Our group considered excludability before classifying the two recreational facilities shown on the worksheet.
examples.zh: 我们组先考虑「排他性」，再把练习表上的两处休闲设施归类。

words.enDefinition: failure of a targeted programme to reach someone in its intended eligible group

examples.en: An exclusion error appeared when a household meeting the sample rules was absent from the list of recipients.
examples.zh: 符合示例规则的一户家庭未出现在领取名单上，因此出现一项「漏纳误差」。

examples.en: We estimated the exclusion error rate by dividing eligible nonrecipients by the total number of eligible households.
examples.zh: 我们用未领取款项的合资格家庭数除以合资格家庭总数，估算「漏纳误差」的发生率。

collocations: compare inclusion error and exclusion error

words.enDefinition: The assumption that an instrument can affect the outcome only by changing the treatment or endogenous regressor.

examples.en: The exclusion restriction would fail if a training offer improved scores through advice given before enrolment.
examples.zh: 如果培训邀请附带的报名指导能提高成绩，「排除限制」就不成立。

examples.en: We explained why the exclusion restriction matters before interpreting the example's instrumental variable estimate.
examples.zh: 解读示例的工具变量估计之前，我们先解释了「排除限制」为何重要。

words.enDefinition: Abrupt change in a factor determined outside the model being studied

examples.en: An unexpected frost was an exogenous shock in our model of the strawberry market.
examples.zh: 在我们的草莓市场模型中，一场突发霜冻是一次「外生冲击」。

examples.en: The exercise treats the river closure as an exogenous shock to the local ferry market.
examples.zh: 习题把河道关闭视为当地渡运市场受到的「外生冲击」。

words.enDefinition: Technological improvement whose rate is taken as given rather than explained by the growth model.

examples.en: The model assumes exogenous technological progress at a constant rate in the first classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 第一项课堂练习假设模型中的「外生技术进步」保持恒定速率。

examples.en: We discussed what exogenous technological progress means for interpreting the results of that model.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「外生技术进步」对理解该模型结果意味着什么。

words.enDefinition: Variation in a variable that is unrelated to the unobserved determinants relevant to the comparison.

examples.en: The simulated lottery provides exogenous variation in access to extra study sessions in our exercise.
examples.zh: 在练习中，模拟抽签为参加额外学习小组的机会提供了「外生变动」。

examples.en: We considered whether the timetable rule could generate exogenous variation for the hypothetical comparison.
examples.zh: 我们研究该时间表规则能否为假设比较产生「外生变动」。

collocations: use exogenous variation in a study

words.enDefinition: A positive gap that occurs when actual output exceeds potential output in a macroeconomic model.

examples.en: The diagram shows an expansionary gap where short-run output exceeds the estimated long-run sustainable level.
examples.zh: 短期产出超过估计的长期可持续水平时，图上显示「扩张性产出缺口」。

examples.en: The class identified an expansionary gap by comparing the equilibrium point with the potential output line.
examples.zh: 全班把均衡点与潜在产出线相比较，找到了「扩张性产出缺口」。

words.zhGloss: 预期扩展的菲利普斯曲线
words.enDefinition: Model relating inflation to expected inflation, economic slack, and supply disturbances
acceptedZhAnswers: 预期扩展的菲利普斯曲线

examples.en: The expectations-augmented Phillips curve in our notes adds expected inflation to the basic model.
examples.zh: 我们笔记里的「预期扩展的菲利普斯曲线」在基本模型中加入了预期通胀。

examples.en: Our expectations-augmented Phillips curve exercise separates expected inflation from the effect of a temporary supply shock.
examples.zh: 关于「预期扩展的菲利普斯曲线」的习题将预期通胀和短期供给冲击的影响分开了。

words.enDefinition: The probability-weighted average payoff from the possible outcomes of a choice or strategy.

examples.en: We calculated the expected payoff for each plan using the probabilities listed in the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们用练习中列出的概率计算每个方案的「期望收益」。

examples.en: The tutor asked which plan had a higher expected payoff against the other team's random choice.
examples.zh: 老师问，面对另一队随机选择时，哪个方案的「期望收益」更高。

words.enDefinition: measuring GDP by adding final consumption, gross capital formation and exports, then subtracting imports

examples.en: The expenditure approach in our lesson adds final purchases and then deducts imported goods and services.
examples.zh: 课堂上的「支出法」先加总最终购买支出，再扣除进口货物和服务。

examples.en: The exercise uses the expenditure approach to organize the household, investment, and trade data.
examples.zh: 练习使用「支出法」整理住户、投资和贸易数据。

collocations: calculate GDP using the expenditure approach

words.enDefinition: Minimum attainable spending needed for specified satisfaction at given prices

examples.en: We evaluated the expenditure function at the new prices while keeping the target unchanged.
examples.zh: 我们在目标不变的情况下，代入新价格求出了「支出函数」值。

examples.en: The expenditure function gives the cost of reaching the target rather than the goods chosen.
examples.zh: 「支出函数」给出达到目标所需的成本，所选商品由需求函数给出。

words.enDefinition: Choosing the least expensive bundle that reaches a specified utility level

examples.en: Our expenditure minimization exercise fixes satisfaction and asks how little a shopper can spend.
examples.zh: 我们的「支出最小化」练习固定满足感水平，然后问购物者最低可以花多少钱。

examples.en: We used expenditure minimization to compare the cheapest baskets that reached the same target.
examples.zh: 我们通过「支出最小化」比较达到同一目标所需的最低成本商品组合。

words.enDefinition: a revision of the spending shares used as weights for categories in a consumer price index

examples.en: The expenditure weight update gave several household services a larger share because families' spending patterns had changed.
examples.zh: 由于家庭支出结构改变，「支出权重更新」提高了若干住户服务项目的权重。

examples.en: Our tutor compared the expenditure weight update with a change to the index's reference period.
examples.zh: 导师将「支出权重更新」与改变指数参考期的做法作了比较。

collocations: compare inflation before and after an expenditure weight update

words.enDefinition: Setting later premiums or contributions partly according to past reported losses or claims.

examples.en: The hypothetical plan used experience rating, so past repair claims affected the prices shown for later periods.
examples.zh: 假设计划采用「按历史赔付情况定价」，因此历史维修索赔影响后续期间的价格。

examples.en: Our class compared experience rating with a simple model where each group paid the same price.
examples.zh: 全班把「按历史赔付情况定价」与各组支付相同价格的简单模型作了比较。

collocations: discuss incentive effects of experience rating

words.enDefinition: The points or other rewards a participant earns under the rules of an experiment.

examples.en: We calculated the experimental payoff from the tokens still held by each participant at the end.
examples.zh: 我们根据结束时各参与者仍持有的代币，计算了「实验收益」。

examples.en: The worksheet explained how the experimental payoff changed when the shared fund returned additional points.
examples.zh: 练习表解释了共享基金返还额外积分时，「实验收益」会怎样改变。

collocations: record the experimental payoff for each participant

words.enDefinition: A specific condition assigned to participants so its effect can be compared with other conditions.

examples.en: One experimental treatment showed previous contributions before participants made their next choice in the game.
examples.zh: 一种「实验处理条件」在参与者作出下一次博弈选择前展示此前的出资。

examples.en: Our tutor described the experimental treatment that changed the matching rule between rounds of the exercise.
examples.zh: 老师介绍了在练习各轮之间改变配对规则的「实验处理条件」。

words.enDefinition: the extent to which an economy's export value is dominated by a small number of products or destinations

examples.en: The export concentration measure increased after the main destination bought a much larger share of the country's exports.
examples.zh: 主要目的地购买了该国更大份额的出口品后，「出口集中度」指标上升了。

examples.en: We compared export concentration by product with the concentration of exports across several partner markets.
examples.zh: 我们比较按产品计算的「出口集中度」与按多个贸易伙伴市场计算的集中程度。

words.enDefinition: broadening the set of products or destinations that contribute to an economy's exports

examples.en: The development report measured export diversification by comparing the number and relative size of different export categories.
examples.zh: 发展报告通过对比各类出口的数量及相对规模，衡量「出口多元化」。

examples.en: We discussed whether entering two new markets would improve export diversification without introducing a new product.
examples.zh: 我们讨论在不推出新产品的情况下，进入两个新市场是否能促进「出口多元化」。

words.enDefinition: financial support linked to exporting goods or services under the programme or policy being described

examples.en: The simplified export subsidy increased the amount producers received per unit they sold abroad in the model.
examples.zh: 在模型中，简化的「出口补贴」提高了生产者每单位海外销售收到的金额。

examples.en: We calculated the public spending associated with the export subsidy in the sample policy exercise.
examples.zh: 我们在示例政策练习中计算了「出口补贴」对应的公共支出。

collocations: estimate spending on an export subsidy
model responses to an export subsidy

words.enDefinition: a graph of the amount offered abroad at different prices, often domestic supply minus domestic demand

examples.en: The export supply curve showed larger quantities offered abroad at higher prices in our exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中，「出口供给曲线」显示世界价格较高时，可供应国外的商品更多。

examples.en: We formed the export supply curve by subtracting domestic purchases from what local firms produced at each price.
examples.zh: 我们在各个价格下用本地厂商总产量减去国内购买量，得到「出口供给曲线」。

collocations: match export supply with import demand

words.enDefinition: A game representation specifying move order, available actions, information, chance events and final payoffs.

examples.en: The extensive-form game showed who chose first and what the second team could observe.
examples.zh: 「扩展式博弈」展示谁先选，以及第二队能观察到什么。

examples.en: We converted the proposed room exchange into an extensive-form game before analysing the later choices.
examples.zh: 我们先把拟议的教室互换表示为「扩展式博弈」，再分析后续选择。

collocations: represent an extensive-form game as a tree

words.enDefinition: the creation or loss of trade links involving new products, trading firms or partner markets

examples.en: New destinations contributed to the extensive margin of trade even though sales to existing importers did not change.
examples.zh: 虽然销往现有进口商的销量没变，但新增目的地推动了「贸易的拓展边际」。

examples.en: The report tracked the extensive margin of trade by counting previously unserved destinations for each product.
examples.zh: 报告按产品统计先前未覆盖的目的地，以跟踪「贸易的拓展边际」。

collocations: measure the extensive margin of trade
increase exports at the extensive margin of trade
distinguish the extensive margin of trade from sales growth

words.enDefinition: A benefit of an activity received by people outside the decision or transaction that created it.

examples.en: The case counted an external benefit when shade from a restored garden cooled the neighbouring walkway.
examples.zh: 修复后的花园为邻近步道遮阳降温，案例把这计作一项「外部收益」。

examples.en: Our tutor separated the external benefit from the benefit received by people who attended the workshop.
examples.zh: 老师把「外部收益」和工作坊参加者自身获得的收益分开。

collocations: an external benefit to nearby households

words.enDefinition: A cost of an activity borne by people other than the decision-makers or parties to the transaction.

examples.en: The worksheet included an external cost for the extra cleaning needed in the streets around the festival.
examples.zh: 练习表计入了节庆周边街道需要额外清洁所产生的一项「外部成本」。

examples.en: We added the external cost to the producer's own cost when comparing the two activities.
examples.zh: 比较两项活动时，我们把「外部成本」加到了生产者自行承担的成本上。

collocations: an external cost borne by residents

words.enDefinition: an effect on others that the decision-maker does not bear or receive through the prices and payments attached to the activity

examples.en: The class identified an externality when noise from deliveries disturbed people who were not buying anything.
examples.zh: 配送发出的噪声打扰了没有购买商品的人，全班把它识别为「外部性」。

examples.en: Our worksheet asked which externality might result from planting trees near the shared campus path.
examples.zh: 练习表问，在校园公共小径旁种树可能产生哪种「外部性」。

words.enDefinition: relative availability of a production factor in one economy compared with another under the chosen measure

examples.en: We compared factor abundance using the ratio of capital to labour, because the countries differed in size.
examples.zh: 由于国家规模不同，我们用资本与劳动的比率比较「要素丰裕性」。

examples.en: The instructor used factor abundance to explain the trade pattern expected in the simplified two-country model.
examples.zh: 讲师借助「要素丰裕性」解释简化的两国模型所预期的贸易格局。

collocations: relate factor abundance to export specialisation

words.enDefinition: the productive resources available to an economy, such as its labour, land or capital

examples.en: The trade model gave each region a different factor endowment while assuming they used identical production methods.
examples.zh: 贸易模型给各地区设定不同「要素禀赋」，同时假定生产方法相同。

examples.en: We compared the factor endowment of a labour-rich region with that of a region rich in capital.
examples.zh: 我们比较劳动力丰富地区与资本丰富地区的「要素禀赋」。

words.enDefinition: Rate on unsecured overnight loans in the US federal funds market

examples.en: We plotted the federal funds rate to compare it with the target range in the example.
examples.zh: 我们绘制了「联邦基金利率」，将它与示例中的目标区间作比较。

examples.en: The notes connect the federal funds rate to overnight lending among eligible US financial institutions.
examples.zh: 讲义将「联邦基金利率」与符合条件的美国金融机构之间的隔夜拆借联系起来。

collocations: target range for the federal funds rate

words.enDefinition: US Federal Reserve committee responsible for monetary policy decisions including rate targets

examples.en: We read the Federal Open Market Committee statement to identify the arguments for holding rates steady.
examples.zh: 我们阅读「联邦公开市场委员会」的声明，找出维持利率不变的理由。

examples.en: The lesson compares a Federal Open Market Committee decision with the market's earlier expectations for rates.
examples.zh: 课堂将「联邦公开市场委员会」的一项决定与市场先前的利率预期作了比较。

words.enDefinition: Statistical inference in settings with too few independent clusters for usual large-cluster approximations to be reliable.

examples.en: Few-cluster inference matters in the exercise because only six fictional schools could receive the offer.
examples.zh: 练习里只有六所虚构学校有机会收到邀请，所以「少聚类推断」很重要。

examples.en: The tutor covered few-cluster inference to explain why many students cannot replace many independent schools here.
examples.zh: 老师用「少聚类推断」解释为什么在这里，增加学生人数无法替代增加独立学校的数量。

words.enDefinition: the external account recording transactions in financial assets and liabilities between residents and nonresidents

examples.en: The financial account recorded a resident firm's purchase of a bond issued by a nonresident company.
examples.zh: 「金融账户」记录居民厂商购买非居民公司发行债券的交易。

examples.en: We used the financial account to distinguish new investment transactions from changes in the value of existing holdings.
examples.zh: 我们借助「金融账户」区分新投资交易与现有持有资产的价值变动。

collocations: record a transaction in the financial account

words.enDefinition: A game with finitely many players and finitely many pure strategies for each player.

examples.en: We treated the classroom exercise as a finite game because each club had only three possible plans.
examples.zh: 我们将课堂练习视为「有限博弈」，因为每个社团只有三个可能计划。

examples.en: Our tutor enumerated the possible outcomes of the finite game before examining each player's best choice.
examples.zh: 老师先列出了「有限博弈」的各种可能结果，再考察每位参与者的最佳选择。

collocations: analyse a finite game in strategic form

words.enDefinition: the difference between an estimator's expected value at the given finite sample size and the parameter it is estimating

examples.en: The simulation reveals finite-sample bias by averaging the estimates over many draws of ten observations.
examples.zh: 模拟对许多各含十个观测值的样本所得估计取平均，从而显示「有限样本偏误」。

examples.en: We discussed why finite-sample bias can be present even for an estimator that is consistent.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了为什么估计量即使具有一致性，也可能存在「有限样本偏误」。

words.enDefinition: A game repeating its stage game a known finite number of times.
