examples.en: We compared the isocost slope in the two diagrams to see how the relative input prices differed.
examples.zh: 我们比较两张图中的「等成本线斜率」，了解投入要素的相对价格如何不同。

collocations: compare the isocost slope with the isoquant slope

words.enDefinition: a set of isoquants showing feasible input combinations for several levels of output

examples.en: The isoquant map placed the curve for higher output farther from the origin in our example.
examples.zh: 在示例中，「等产量曲线图」把较高产量的曲线画在离原点更远的位置。

examples.en: We used an isoquant map to see how the required input combinations changed as output increased.
examples.zh: 我们用「等产量曲线图」查看产量提高时所需的投入组合怎样变化。

collocations: interpret output changes on an isoquant map

words.expression: iterated elimination of strictly dominated strategies
words.lemma: iterated elimination of strictly dominated strategies
words.zhGloss: 反复剔除被严格支配策略
words.enDefinition: Repeatedly removing strictly dominated strategies and reassessing remaining options in the reduced game.
acceptedZhAnswers: 反复剔除被严格支配策略
acceptedEnVariants: iterated elimination of strictly dominated strategies

examples.en: We used iterated elimination of strictly dominated strategies to simplify the classroom game one step at a time.
examples.zh: 我们用「反复剔除被严格支配策略」逐步简化课堂博弈。

examples.en: The tutor illustrated iterated elimination of strictly dominated strategies by crossing out rows, then checking the remaining columns.
examples.zh: 老师先划去若干行，再检查剩下的列，以说明「反复剔除被严格支配策略」。

collocations: apply iterated elimination of strictly dominated strategies
solve a game by iterated elimination of strictly dominated strategies
explain iterated elimination of strictly dominated strategies

words.enDefinition: a pattern in which the trade balance initially worsens after depreciation before improving as quantities adjust

examples.en: The tutor illustrated the J-curve effect with a model where import prices changed before quantities could respond.
examples.zh: 导师用一个进口价格先变、数量随后作出反应的模型演示了「J 曲线效应」。

examples.en: The report tested for a J-curve effect by comparing trade balances across several quarters after the currency moved.
examples.zh: 报告比较汇率变动后几个季度的贸易差额，以检验是否存在「J 曲线效应」。

collocations: explain the timing of the J-curve effect

words.enDefinition: Share of unemployed people moving into employment during a specified period

examples.en: The quarterly job-finding rate rose when more unemployed respondents reported starting a job.
examples.zh: 随着更多失业受访者报告已入职，季度「求职成功率」上升了。

examples.en: The exercise calculates the job-finding rate among those unemployed at the start of June.
examples.zh: 习题计算的是六月初处于失业状态的人群的「求职成功率」。

words.enDefinition: Process linking workers seeking jobs with employers offering suitable openings

examples.en: The model treats job matching as a process that can take several weeks.
examples.zh: 模型把「岗位匹配」看作一个可能需要几周的过程。

examples.en: Better information may improve job matching in a town with many unfilled vacancies.
examples.zh: 在空缺岗位很多的小镇，更充分的信息可能改善「岗位匹配」。

words.enDefinition: US ratio of job openings to employment plus job openings

examples.en: Our US labor report places the job openings rate above the chart of actual hiring.
examples.zh: 我们的美国劳动力报告将「职位空缺率」放在实际招聘人数图表的上方。

examples.en: We reproduced the job openings rate using both occupied jobs and open positions in the denominator.
examples.zh: 我们将已有人任职的岗位和空缺岗位都纳入分母，重算出了「职位空缺率」。

words.enDefinition: Frequency of workers leaving existing employment relative to a defined workforce

examples.en: Our model raised the job separation rate while keeping the rate of successful job searches fixed.
examples.zh: 我们的模型在求职成功率不变的情况下提高了「离职率」。

examples.en: The instructor calculated the job separation rate from the number who left and the employment base.
examples.zh: 老师用离职人数和就业人数基数算出了「离职率」。

words.enDefinition: Equal-satisfaction contour with a sharp bend where the exchange rate changes abruptly

examples.en: The kinked indifference curve bends where the numbers of left and right gloves match.
examples.zh: 左右手手套数量相等的地方，就是「有折点的无差异曲线」的转折处。

examples.en: At the bend of a kinked indifference curve, the usual tangency rule may fail.
examples.zh: 在「有折点的无差异曲线」的转折处，通常的相切规则可能不适用。

collocations: slope of a kinked indifference curve
optimum on a kinked indifference curve

words.enDefinition: People classified as either employed or unemployed under the survey's definitions

examples.en: The survey's labor force includes both people with jobs and people classified as unemployed.
examples.zh: 调查中的「劳动力人口」既包括有工作的人，也包括归类为失业的人。

examples.en: If more residents start looking for work, the measured labor force may grow.
examples.zh: 如果更多居民开始找工作，统计中的「劳动力人口」可能会增加。

words.enDefinition: Share of the reference population that is employed or officially unemployed

examples.en: Our chart shows the labor force participation rate rising even though employment barely changed.
examples.zh: 我们的图表显示，尽管就业人数几乎没有变化，「劳动力参与率」仍有所上升。

examples.en: We used the survey's population count to calculate the labor force participation rate for that year.
examples.zh: 我们用该调查的人口统计值计算当年的「劳动力参与率」。

collocations: calculate the labor force participation rate
labor force participation rate by age

words.enDefinition: Available labor capacity that current employment and hours do not use

examples.en: We looked for labor market slack among both unemployed people and workers wanting more hours.
examples.zh: 我们从失业者和想获得更多工时的劳动者中寻找「劳动力市场闲置」的迹象。

examples.en: The report pairs lower vacancies with other signs of labor market slack in the example.
examples.zh: 该报告在示例中列出空缺岗位减少及其他「劳动力市场闲置」的迹象。

words.enDefinition: Extent to which vacancies are plentiful relative to available jobseekers

examples.en: We measured labor market tightness using the number of vacancies for each unemployed person.
examples.zh: 我们用每名失业者对应的岗位空缺数衡量「劳动力市场紧俏度」。

examples.en: Our chart shows greater labor market tightness during the months when vacancies rose and unemployment fell.
examples.zh: 我们的图表显示，在岗位空缺增加、失业减少的几个月，「劳动力市场紧俏度」更高。

words.enDefinition: Movement of workers into and out of positions over a period

examples.en: The labor turnover figures showed frequent hiring and departures despite little net employment change.
examples.zh: 「人员流动」数据显示，尽管净就业变化很小，招聘和离职都很频繁。

examples.en: We compared labor turnover across industries while holding the reporting period constant.
examples.zh: 我们使用同一统计期，比较各行业的「人员流动」。

words.enDefinition: Unused labor capacity including unemployment and some forms of insufficient employment

examples.en: The class compared two measures of labor underutilization from the same employment report.
examples.zh: 全班比较了同一份就业报告中的两项「劳动力利用不足」指标。

examples.en: Our exhibit uses labor underutilization to include both joblessness and some unmet demand for hours.
examples.zh: 我们的展示用「劳动力利用不足」来涵盖失业和部分未获满足的工时需求。

words.enDefinition: the units of labour used for each unit of capital in a production method

examples.en: The labour-capital ratio rose when the producer kept its equipment and paid for more staffing hours.
examples.zh: 生产者保留原有设备，同时增加有薪工时，「劳动资本比」随之上升。

examples.en: We compared the labour-capital ratio of two techniques that produced the same number of finished bags.
examples.zh: 我们比较了能做出相同成品包数量的两种生产方法的「劳动资本比」。

words.enDefinition: The mix of measured characteristics of workers, such as education and experience, used to analyse labour input.

examples.en: The labour composition measure changes when the fictional industry employs a different mix of experienced workers.
examples.zh: 虚构行业内不同经验的劳动者占比发生变化时，「劳动构成」指标也发生变化。

examples.en: Our worksheet records changes in labour composition separately from changes in the number of hours.
examples.zh: 练习纸分别记录「劳动构成」变动和工时变动。

words.enDefinition: a graph of how much labour employers choose at each wage under the stated market and production conditions

examples.en: The labour demand curve shifted right when the competitive firms received a higher price for their output.
examples.zh: 完全竞争厂商能以更高价格卖出产品后，「劳动需求曲线」右移。

examples.en: We traced the labour demand curve while holding the price of the firm's equipment unchanged in the exercise.
examples.zh: 在练习中，我们保持厂商设备价格不变，描出「劳动需求曲线」。

words.enDefinition: the reliance of a production method on labour relative to other inputs such as capital

examples.en: The workshop's labour intensity fell after it installed equipment that could handle some of the manual sorting.
examples.zh: 车间安装能承担一部分人工分拣的设备后，「劳动密集程度」下降了。

examples.en: We compared labour intensity across two methods that used very different amounts of equipment per worker.
examples.zh: 我们比较了人均设备量差别很大的两种方法的「劳动密集程度」。

words.enDefinition: Output per unit of labour input, commonly measured per hour worked.

examples.en: Labour productivity rises in the example because each hour worked produces more units of output.
examples.zh: 示例中，每工时产量增多，因此「劳动生产率」提高。

examples.en: The class compared labour productivity across two industries using the same measure of hours worked.
examples.zh: 全班用同一工时指标比较了两个行业的「劳动生产率」。

words.enDefinition: A measure that tends to change after shifts in broader economic activity have already occurred.

examples.en: The lagging economic indicator begins to rise two months after the fictional economy begins recovering.
examples.zh: 虚构经济体开始复苏两个月后，「滞后经济指标」才开始上升。

examples.en: The worksheet asks why a lagging economic indicator cannot identify the turning point in advance.
examples.zh: 练习问的是为什么「滞后经济指标」不能提前确定转折点。

collocations: changes in a lagging economic indicator

words.enDefinition: an economy whose trade decisions are substantial enough to affect world prices or global markets in the model

examples.en: The large open economy could influence the world price because it accounted for much of global demand.
examples.zh: 这个「大型开放经济体」占全球需求的很大一部分，因此能影响世界价格。

examples.en: We compared a large open economy with an importer that purchased too little to change world prices.
examples.zh: 我们把「大型开放经济体」与购买量小到无法改变世界价格的进口方作了比较。

collocations: analyse policy in a large open economy
compare a large open economy with a small one

words.enDefinition: Principle that higher prices usually reduce purchases when other factors stay fixed

examples.en: The law of demand explains why a higher price usually means fewer notebooks are purchased.
examples.zh: 「需求定律」解释了为什么价格越高，人们通常买的笔记本越少。

examples.en: To illustrate the law of demand, we changed the smoothie price while keeping income fixed.
examples.zh: 为了说明「需求定律」，我们调整了冰沙的价格，同时保持收入不变。

collocations: exception to the law of demand

words.enDefinition: the tendency for successive units of a variable input eventually to add less output when other inputs stay fixed

examples.en: The law of diminishing marginal returns explained why extra workers contributed less once the bench became crowded.
examples.zh: 「边际报酬递减规律」解释了为什么工作台拥挤后，再增聘工人所带来的产量更少。

examples.en: We illustrated the law of diminishing marginal returns by adding workers while holding the number of ovens constant.
examples.zh: 我们维持烤炉台数不变、逐步增聘工人，以说明「边际报酬递减规律」。

collocations: illustrate the law of diminishing marginal returns
apply the law of diminishing marginal returns
an example of the law of diminishing marginal returns

words.enDefinition: Principle that higher prices generally encourage more selling, other things equal

examples.en: Our example illustrates the law of supply by showing how bakeries respond to higher bread prices.
examples.zh: 我们用面包店对面包涨价的反应来说明「供给定律」。

examples.en: Under the law of supply, sellers normally offer more when only their selling price rises.
examples.zh: 根据「供给定律」，当只有售价上涨时，卖家通常愿意多卖一些。

collocations: consistent with the law of supply

words.enDefinition: Employer-initiated job separations grouped together in US labor turnover reports

examples.en: The US table reports layoffs and discharges separately from people who resign on their own.
examples.zh: 美国统计表将「裁员和解雇」与自愿辞职分开列报。

examples.en: Our group compared layoffs and discharges in manufacturing and retail using the same monthly release.
examples.zh: 我们小组用同一份月报比较了制造业和零售业的「裁员和解雇」数据。

words.enDefinition: A measure that tends to change before the corresponding turning points in broader economic activity.

examples.en: The leading economic indicator starts to fall before total production turns down in our example.
examples.zh: 示例中，总产出转为下降之前，「先行经济指标」已经开始下降。

examples.en: We compared two years of a leading economic indicator with the later movements in output.
examples.zh: 我们用两年的「先行经济指标」与之后的产出变化作比较。

words.enDefinition: improving productivity through accumulated experience performing production tasks

examples.en: To estimate learning by doing, the group compared production times across batches of identical items.
examples.zh: 为估算「干中学」的效果，小组比较了生产多批相同产品的耗时。

examples.en: The model separated learning by doing from the lower input prices the firm negotiated over time.
examples.zh: 模型将「干中学」与厂商后来谈到的更低投入要素价格区分开。

collocations: measure the gains from learning by doing

words.enDefinition: a set of input amounts that achieves a given output while minimising total input expense

examples.en: The least-cost input combination changed when rented machine hours became cheaper but the wage stayed the same.
examples.zh: 机器租用工时降价而工资不变时，「成本最低的投入组合」变了。

examples.en: We found the least-cost input combination by comparing the feasible points shown on the target isoquant.
examples.zh: 我们比较目标等产量曲线上的可行点，找到了「成本最低的投入组合」。

collocations: calculate the expense of a least-cost input combination

words.enDefinition: A sensitivity check that re-estimates a result after removing each cluster in turn.

examples.en: Our leave-one-cluster-out check asks whether the estimated attendance change depends heavily on one fictional school.
examples.zh: 我们的「逐簇剔除检查」考察出勤率的估计变化是否高度依赖某一所虚构学校。

examples.en: We plotted the leave-one-cluster-out check results after repeating the analysis without each school in turn.
examples.zh: 我们依次剔除每所学校、重做分析，然后绘出「逐簇剔除检查」结果。

words.enDefinition: a fixed-proportions production function in which output is limited by the smallest effective input quantity

examples.en: The Leontief production function made extra tool sets unproductive unless the number of trained operators also increased.
examples.zh: 在「列昂惕夫生产函数」下，若受训操作员人数没有增加，多出的工具套装不会提高产量。

examples.en: We drew the right-angled isoquant implied by the Leontief production function used in our example.
examples.zh: 我们画出了示例「列昂惕夫生产函数」所对应的直角等产量曲线。

collocations: derive isoquants from a Leontief production function

words.enDefinition: a measure of pricing power calculated as price minus marginal cost, divided by price

examples.en: The Lerner index was zero in our competitive example because price matched the producer's marginal cost.
examples.zh: 竞争示例中，价格等于生产者的边际成本，因此「勒纳指数」为零。

examples.en: We compared the Lerner index for two hypothetical suppliers at their respective prices and marginal costs.
examples.zh: 我们根据两家假想供应商各自的价格和边际成本，比较它们的「勒纳指数」。

words.enDefinition: A model specification in which the outcome stays in levels and the regressor of interest is logged.

examples.en: The level-log specification records test scores in points and takes the logarithm of study hours.
examples.zh: 「水平—对数设定」用分数表示测试成绩，并对学习时数取对数。

examples.en: The tutor asked how to interpret a ten percent change in hours under the level-log specification.
examples.zh: 老师问，在「水平—对数设定」下应如何解释学习时数变动百分之十。

words.enDefinition: Equation whose quantity demanded changes by equal amounts for equal price changes

examples.en: Our linear demand function gives a drop of two purchases for each dollar added to price.
examples.zh: 我们的「线性需求函数」显示，价格每涨一美元，购买量减少两件。

examples.en: The tutor used a linear demand function on the interval where predicted quantity stays positive.
examples.zh: 在预测需求量保持为正的区间内，辅导老师采用了「线性需求函数」。

words.enDefinition: a linear regression for a binary outcome, with fitted values estimating probabilities that can fall outside zero to one

examples.en: The linear probability model describes how the fitted chance of completing the course changes with attendance.
examples.zh: 「线性概率模型」描述课程完成的拟合概率如何随出勤变化。

examples.en: We noticed that the linear probability model gave one fitted value above one in the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们注意到练习中的「线性概率模型」有一个拟合值大于一。

words.enDefinition: Equation whose quantity supplied changes by equal amounts for equal price changes

examples.en: We fitted a linear supply function to the example quantities at the three positive prices.
examples.zh: 我们根据三个正价格对应的示例数量拟合了「线性供给函数」。

examples.en: With our linear supply function, each dollar of extra price adds the same number of tickets.
examples.zh: 按我们的「线性供给函数」，价格每增加一美元，增加的供票量都相同。

words.enDefinition: Preference for holding easily spendable balances instead of less liquid assets

examples.en: The example links stronger liquidity preference to greater uncertainty about upcoming household expenses.
examples.zh: 例子把更强的「流动性偏好」与未来家庭开支的不确定性增大联系起来。

examples.en: We used liquidity preference theory to explain the model's downward-sloping demand for money.
examples.zh: 我们用「流动性偏好」理论解释模型中向下倾斜的货币需求曲线。

words.enDefinition: The average causal effect for units whose treatment status changes with the instrument, under suitable identification assumptions.

examples.en: The local average treatment effect describes the students who participate only when offered tutoring in our example.
examples.zh: 示例中的「局部平均处理效应」针对只有获得邀请才会参加辅导的学生。

examples.en: We explained why the local average treatment effect need not describe every student in the simulation.
examples.zh: 我们解释了为什么「局部平均处理效应」未必适用于模拟中的每名学生。

collocations: identify a local average treatment effect
estimate a local average treatment effect
interpret a local average treatment effect

words.enDefinition: the treatment effect identified at the assignment cutoff under the assumptions of the particular regression discontinuity design

examples.en: The local effect at the cutoff concerns students near eligibility in the simulated tutoring example.
examples.zh: 在模拟辅导示例中，「阈值处局部效应」针对接近资格门槛的学生。

examples.en: We discussed why the local effect at the cutoff need not apply to students far away.
examples.zh: 我们讨论「阈值处局部效应」为什么未必适用于得分离阈值很远的学生。

collocations: estimate a local effect at the cutoff
interpret the local effect at the cutoff
report a local effect at the cutoff

words.enDefinition: A straight-line model estimated using observations near a chosen target value, often with distance-based weights.

examples.en: The local linear fit uses scores close to the cutoff in the simulated tutoring data.
examples.zh: 「局部线性拟合」使用模拟辅导数据中接近阈值的成绩。

examples.en: We estimated a local linear fit on each side to compare their values at the cutoff.
examples.zh: 我们在阈值两侧分别进行「局部线性拟合」，以比较两侧在阈值处的数值。

words.enDefinition: Preferences where a better option exists arbitrarily close to any bundle

examples.en: We assumed locally nonsatiated preferences and looked near a bundle well inside the budget region.
examples.zh: 我们假定「局部非饱和偏好」成立，并在一个离预算边界较远的组合附近寻找更好的选择。

examples.en: Under locally nonsatiated preferences, spending less than the budget cannot give the best affordable bundle.
examples.zh: 在「局部非饱和偏好」下，支出低于预算的组合不可能是最优的可负担组合。

collocations: utility representation for locally nonsatiated preferences

words.enDefinition: A model specification in which the outcome is logged and the regressor of interest stays in levels.

examples.en: The log-level specification uses the log of hourly wages and records schooling in years.
examples.zh: 「对数—水平设定」使用小时工资的对数，受教育程度用年数表示。

examples.en: We interpreted the log-level specification by comparing wages for workers one year apart in schooling.
examples.zh: 我们比较受教育年限相差一年的劳动者工资，以解释「对数—水平设定」。

words.enDefinition: A model specification in which both the outcome and the regressor of interest are logged.

examples.en: The log-log specification uses logarithms for both wages and accumulated study hours in the worksheet.
examples.zh: 练习的「双对数设定」对工资和累计学习时数都取对数。

examples.en: In this log-log specification, the slope measures the fitted elasticity of one variable with respect to another.
examples.zh: 在这个「双对数设定」中，斜率衡量一个变量相对另一个变量的拟合弹性。

words.enDefinition: The sustainable total output an economy can produce once wages and other prices have adjusted.

examples.en: The long-run aggregate supply line is vertical at potential output in our introductory classroom diagram.
examples.zh: 入门课示意图中的「长期总供给」线在潜在产出处垂直。

examples.en: The sample economy's long-run aggregate supply increases when the model assumes higher productive capacity.
examples.zh: 模型假设生产能力提高时，示例经济体的「长期总供给」增加。

words.enDefinition: a graph of the lowest attainable average cost at each output level when all inputs may be adjusted

examples.en: The long-run average cost curve showed the cheapest plant size at each planned output in our model.
examples.zh: 「长期平均成本曲线」显示模型中各计划产量所对应的最低成本厂房规模。

examples.en: The tutor traced the long-run average cost curve beneath the alternatives available at different plant sizes.
examples.zh: 导师沿各种厂房规模所对应曲线的下包络，描出了「长期平均成本曲线」。

collocations: derive a long-run average cost curve
move along the long-run average cost curve
locate the minimum of the long-run average cost curve

words.enDefinition: an equilibrium where competitive firms have adjusted their inputs and entry or exit no longer creates further change

examples.en: In long-run competitive equilibrium, the model's identical firms earned just enough to cover all their economic costs.
examples.zh: 在「长期竞争均衡」下，模型中的同质厂商收入恰好覆盖全部经济成本。

examples.en: We marked long-run competitive equilibrium after showing how additional firms changed the price and total quantity supplied.
examples.zh: 演示新增厂商如何改变价格和总供给量后，我们标出了「长期竞争均衡」。

collocations: compare adjustment paths to long-run competitive equilibrium

words.enDefinition: Proportional responsiveness measured over a longer period allowing more complete adjustments

examples.en: The researchers estimated long-run elasticity after households had time to change how they commuted.
examples.zh: 研究人员等到各家庭有时间改变通勤方式后，才估算「长期弹性」。

examples.en: The discussion compared long-run elasticity across industries that can expand capacity at different speeds.
examples.zh: 课堂讨论比较了能够以不同速度扩大产能的行业的「长期弹性」。

words.enDefinition: the decision whether to stop taking part in a market when all production commitments can be changed

examples.en: The long-run exit decision depended on whether the expected price would cover all costs after the lease ended.
examples.zh: 「长期退出决策」取决于租约到期后预期的售价能否覆盖所有成本。

examples.en: We compared a long-run exit decision with temporarily closing a stall while its rent remained due.
examples.zh: 我们将「长期退出决策」与仍须付租金时暂时关停摊位的情形作了比较。

collocations: compare a long-run exit decision with a short-run shutdown

words.enDefinition: the relation between market price and total output once firms can adjust capacity and enter or exit

examples.en: The long-run industry supply changed when the model allowed additional shops to rent space in the same district.
examples.zh: 模型允许更多商店在同一区域租用场地时，「行业长期供给」改变了。

examples.en: We compared long-run industry supply under constant input costs and under rising demand for scarce locations.
examples.zh: 我们比较要素成本不变和稀缺地点需求上升两种情形下的「行业长期供给」。

collocations: explain the shape of long-run industry supply

words.enDefinition: A position in the aggregate demand and supply model where actual output equals potential output after prices adjust.

examples.en: The diagram shows long-run macroeconomic equilibrium where the price adjustment leaves output at its potential level.
examples.zh: 示意图显示价格调整后产出处于潜在水平的「长期宏观经济均衡」。

examples.en: The class compared long-run macroeconomic equilibrium before and after the hypothetical increase in productive capacity.
examples.zh: 全班比较假设生产能力提高前后的「长期宏观经济均衡」。

collocations: long-run macroeconomic equilibrium in the model

words.enDefinition: a graph of the additional cost of expanding output when the firm is free to adjust all inputs

examples.en: The long-run marginal cost curve reflected changes in capacity as output increased in our model.
examples.zh: 在我们的模型里，「长期边际成本曲线」反映了产量增加时产能也能变化。

examples.en: We derived the long-run marginal cost curve from the least total cost at nearby output levels.
examples.zh: 我们根据相邻几个产量水平的最低总成本，推导出「长期边际成本曲线」。

collocations: derive the long-run marginal cost curve
interpret a long-run marginal cost curve
compare long-run and short-run marginal cost curves

words.enDefinition: Vertical curve in the standard model after inflation expectations fully adjust

examples.en: In the textbook model, the long-run Phillips curve passes through the natural unemployment rate.
examples.zh: 在教科书模型中，「长期菲利普斯曲线」经过自然失业率所对应的位置。

examples.en: We drew a vertical long-run Phillips curve after allowing expectations to adjust fully in the model.
examples.zh: 允许模型中的预期充分调整后，我们画了一条垂直的「长期菲利普斯曲线」。

collocations: position of the long-run Phillips curve

words.enDefinition: Unemployment lasting at least the duration specified in the reporting framework

examples.en: The US long-term unemployment series groups people who have been unemployed for at least twenty-seven weeks.
examples.zh: 美国「长期失业」数据把已失业至少二十七周的人归为一类。

examples.en: Our class compared two reports that used different thresholds for long-term unemployment.
examples.zh: 全班比较了两份采用不同「长期失业」判定门槛的报告。

words.enDefinition: choosing the feasible decision with the smallest economic loss when all available options lead to a loss

examples.en: The model used loss minimisation to compare producing a small quantity with temporarily closing the workshop.
examples.zh: 模型通过「亏损最小化」比较少量生产与暂时关闭车间。

examples.en: We discussed loss minimisation after the exercise showed that every available output decision led to a loss.
examples.zh: 练习显示所有可选产量决策都会亏损后，我们讨论了「亏损最小化」。

collocations: choose an output for loss minimisation

words.enDefinition: a tax payment fixed independently of the taxpayer's choices in the model

examples.en: The classroom model used a lump-sum tax that was unchanged when a household altered its purchases.
examples.zh: 课堂模型采用「定额总付税」，即使家庭改变购买选择，税额也不变。

examples.en: We compared a lump-sum tax with a charge applied to each transaction in the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们把「定额总付税」与练习中对每笔交易征收的税作了比较。

collocations: compare a lump-sum tax with a per-unit tax
raise revenue through a lump-sum tax

words.enDefinition: Product whose demand increases more than proportionally when buyers' income rises

examples.en: Our data treat weekend trips as a luxury good because trip counts rise proportionally more than income.
examples.zh: 我们的数据将周末旅行归为「奢侈品」，因为旅行次数的增幅大于收入的增幅。

examples.en: A luxury good in the model is classified by its response to income changes.
examples.zh: 在模型中，「奢侈品」是根据需求对收入变化的反应来分类的。

words.enDefinition: a general term for a floating exchange arrangement in which authorities also intervene at their discretion

examples.en: The classroom example used a managed float where the currency usually moved with market conditions during the year.
examples.zh: 课堂示例采用「管理浮动汇率制度」，一年内该货币大多随市场状况变动。

examples.en: We compared a managed float with occasional intervention and a peg targeting a published exchange rate.
examples.zh: 我们比较了偶尔有干预的「管理浮动汇率制度」和盯住已公布汇率的安排。

collocations: compare a managed float with a peg

words.enDefinition: The additional cost of reducing pollution by one more unit.

examples.en: We compared marginal abatement cost across two factories before explaining who reduced more emissions in the simulation.
examples.zh: 解释模拟中谁减排更多之前，我们比较了两家工厂的「边际减排成本」。

examples.en: The graph showed marginal abatement cost rising as the least expensive reductions were used first.
examples.zh: 图上显示，最便宜的减排措施先用完后，「边际减排成本」会上升。

collocations: draw a marginal abatement cost curve
compare marginal abatement costs across firms

words.enDefinition: The additional deadweight loss per additional unit of tax revenue raised by a small tax increase.

examples.en: The worksheet estimated marginal excess burden by comparing the extra welfare loss with the extra revenue raised.
examples.zh: 练习表把额外福利损失与新增税收收入比较，估算「边际超额负担」。

examples.en: Our tutor compared marginal excess burden for two small changes in the course's tax model.
examples.zh: 老师比较了课程税收模型中两项小幅调整的「边际超额负担」。

collocations: compare the marginal excess burden of two taxes

words.enDefinition: a graph showing the extra total expenditure from buying an additional unit of an input at each quantity

examples.en: In the single-wage model, the marginal expenditure curve lay above supply because extra hires also raised existing wages.
examples.zh: 在统一工资模型中，增聘也会提高现有员工的工资，所以「边际支出曲线」位于供给曲线上方。

examples.en: We read the marginal expenditure curve before choosing the employment level for the example's single employer.
examples.zh: 为示例中的单一雇主选定用工水平前，我们读取了「边际支出曲线」。

collocations: compare a marginal expenditure curve with the supply curve

words.enDefinition: The additional benefit received by third parties when one more unit of an activity takes place.

examples.en: The exercise estimated marginal external benefit from the extra shade one more tree provided to neighbouring houses.
examples.zh: 练习估算了再种一棵树为周边住宅增加树荫所带来的「边际外部收益」。

examples.en: We counted the marginal external benefit separately from the extra benefit enjoyed by the person planting the tree.
examples.zh: 我们把「边际外部收益」与种树人自己获得的额外收益分开计算。

collocations: include marginal external benefit in a welfare comparison

words.enDefinition: The additional cost imposed on third parties by one more unit of an activity.

examples.en: The model's marginal external cost was higher for a delivery on the busy street during quiet hours.
examples.zh: 模型中，同样在繁忙街道上配送，若赶上居民休息时段，「边际外部成本」会更高。

examples.en: We estimated marginal external cost for one additional trip before calculating the corresponding social cost.
examples.zh: 我们先估算多一次出行的「边际外部成本」，再计算对应的社会成本。

collocations: plot the marginal external cost curve
include marginal external cost in the calculation

words.enDefinition: The additional benefit a decision-maker receives from consuming or undertaking one more unit.

examples.en: The marginal private benefit was the extra value a participant received from attending one more session.
examples.zh: 「边际私人收益」是参加者多参加一场活动所获得的额外价值。

examples.en: Our tutor measured marginal private benefit before counting any benefits received by people outside the workshop.
examples.zh: 老师先测量「边际私人收益」，再计入工作坊之外的人所获得的收益。

collocations: draw the marginal private benefit curve
compare marginal private benefit with marginal social benefit

words.enDefinition: The extra cost that a decision-maker bears from producing or undertaking one more unit.

examples.en: The marginal private cost included the materials and labour needed to make one more sample basket.
examples.zh: 「边际私人成本」包括多做一个样品篮子所需的材料和人工。

examples.en: We compared marginal private cost with the additional cost that the same unit imposed on neighbours.
examples.zh: 我们将「边际私人成本」与这一个单位给邻居带来的额外成本作比较。

collocations: draw the marginal private cost curve
compare marginal private cost with marginal social cost

words.enDefinition: a graph showing how the marginal product of an input changes with the amount of that input

examples.en: The marginal product curve bent down after additional staff began sharing the same preparation area.
examples.zh: 新增员工开始共用同一准备区后，「边际产量曲线」向下弯折。

examples.en: We plotted the marginal product curve using the increases in output shown in the production table.
examples.zh: 我们用生产表中列出的产量增量绘制「边际产量曲线」。

collocations: find the peak of a marginal product curve

words.enDefinition: additional output from increasing one input by a unit, or the rate of change for a continuous input

examples.en: The marginal product of another worker was low because all the packing tables were already in use.
examples.zh: 打包台已全部占用，再增加一名工人的「边际产量」很低。

examples.en: We compared the marginal product at different staffing levels while keeping oven capacity fixed in the example.
examples.zh: 示例里我们固定烤炉容量，比较不同用工水平下的「边际产量」。

collocations: measure the marginal product of an input
compare marginal product across input levels

words.enDefinition: the change in output per additional unit of physical capital when other inputs are held constant

examples.en: The marginal product of capital measured the extra output from adding a machine without changing staffing.
examples.zh: 「资本的边际产量」衡量保持人员不变、增加一台机器带来的额外产出。

examples.en: The tutor asked whether the marginal product of capital changed when the plant had three machines.
examples.zh: 导师问，工厂拥有三台机器时，「资本的边际产量」是否发生变化。

collocations: estimate the marginal product of capital
compare the marginal product of capital across plants
plot the marginal product of capital

words.enDefinition: the change in output per additional unit of labour when other input amounts are held constant

examples.en: The marginal product of labour declined after the fourth worker joined the already crowded preparation area.
examples.zh: 第四名工人加入本来就拥挤的准备区后，「劳动的边际产量」下降了。

examples.en: We calculated the marginal product of labour using output changes at a fixed number of packing tables.
examples.zh: 打包台台数固定时，我们根据产量变化计算「劳动的边际产量」。

collocations: calculate the marginal product of labour
compare the marginal product of labour with the wage
plot the marginal product of labour

words.enDefinition: Rate of trading one good for another locally at unchanged satisfaction

examples.en: The marginal rate of substitution measures how much tea she gives up for another biscuit here.
examples.zh: 在这里，「边际替代率」衡量她愿意为再得到一块饼干放弃多少茶。

examples.en: At this point, the marginal rate of substitution is the absolute slope of the indifference curve.
examples.zh: 在这一点，「边际替代率」等于无差异曲线斜率的绝对值。

collocations: calculate the marginal rate of substitution
marginal rate of substitution between goods

words.enDefinition: the rate at which one input can replace another while output is held constant along an isoquant

examples.en: The marginal rate of technical substitution fell as the firm moved toward using more labour along the isoquant.
examples.zh: 厂商沿等产量曲线增加劳动用量时，「边际技术替代率」下降了。

examples.en: We calculated the marginal rate of technical substitution from two marginal products in the smooth example.
examples.zh: 在使用平滑曲线的示例中，我们根据两项边际产量求出「边际技术替代率」。

collocations: calculate the marginal rate of technical substitution
compare the marginal rate of technical substitution with relative input prices
interpret the marginal rate of technical substitution

words.enDefinition: the additional revenue per extra unit sold, or the derivative of total revenue for continuous output

examples.en: Marginal revenue was below price because the seller lowered the price on all units to sell more.
examples.zh: 卖家为增加销量调低了所有单位的价格，因此「边际收益」低于售价。

examples.en: We calculated marginal revenue from the difference between the table's receipts for two consecutive quantities sold.
examples.zh: 我们用表中相邻两种销量对应的销售收入之差，计算「边际收益」。

collocations: compare marginal revenue with marginal cost
equate marginal revenue and marginal cost

words.enDefinition: a graph showing marginal revenue at each quantity of output sold

examples.en: The marginal revenue curve lay below the single-price demand curve in the linear example drawn in class.
examples.zh: 在线性课堂示例里，「边际收益曲线」位于采用统一价格的需求曲线下方。

examples.en: We used the marginal revenue curve to locate the quantity where another sale would reduce total revenue.
examples.zh: 我们根据「边际收益曲线」找出再多卖一单位就会减少总收益的销量位置。

collocations: find where the marginal revenue curve crosses zero

words.enDefinition: the additional revenue generated by using one more unit of an input, holding other inputs fixed

examples.en: The marginal revenue product of an additional worker fell as the producer approached the limits of its equipment.
examples.zh: 生产者接近设备产能上限时，再雇一名工人的「边际收益产品」下降了。

examples.en: We estimated marginal revenue product from the change in receipts when one more hour of labour was added.
examples.zh: 我们用增加一小时人工后销售收入的变化估算「边际收益产品」。

collocations: compare marginal revenue product with marginal expenditure
plot the marginal revenue product curve

words.enDefinition: The total extra benefit to everyone from one more unit, including private and external benefits.

examples.en: The worksheet added the participant's extra benefit to the spillover to calculate marginal social benefit.
examples.zh: 练习表把参加者的额外收益和外溢收益相加，计算「边际社会收益」。

examples.en: We compared marginal social benefit with marginal social cost for one additional workshop place.
examples.zh: 我们比较了增加一个工作坊名额的「边际社会收益」和边际社会成本。

collocations: plot the marginal social benefit curve
compare marginal social benefit with marginal social cost

words.enDefinition: The total extra cost to everyone from one more unit, including private and external costs.

examples.en: We added the firm's extra expense and the neighbours' extra damage to obtain marginal social cost.
examples.zh: 我们将企业多付的费用与邻居额外承受的损害相加，得到「边际社会成本」。

examples.en: The graph placed marginal social cost above marginal private cost because extra production created noise.
examples.zh: 图上的「边际社会成本」高于边际私人成本，因为额外生产会产生噪声。

collocations: draw the marginal social cost curve
compare marginal social cost with the benefit of another unit

words.enDefinition: Change in satisfaction from consuming one more unit, other consumption fixed

examples.en: We calculated the marginal utility of a third peach from the two utility totals.
examples.zh: 我们根据两项总效用计算了吃第三个桃子的「边际效用」。

examples.en: In the model, the marginal utility of another snack fell after lunch.
examples.zh: 在模型中，午饭后再吃一份零食的「边际效用」下降了。

words.enDefinition: Additional satisfaction from one more unit divided by that unit's price

examples.en: We compared the marginal utility per dollar of coffee with the same ratio for tea.
examples.zh: 我们比较了咖啡与茶的「每美元边际效用」。

examples.en: The table includes marginal utility per dollar for snacks that cost different amounts at the café.
examples.zh: 这张表列出了咖啡馆里各种不同价格零食的「每美元边际效用」。

words.enDefinition: Largest amount someone would pay for one additional unit of something

examples.en: The class found the marginal willingness to pay for a third apple using the demand graph.
examples.zh: 全班用需求图求出了买第三个苹果的「边际支付意愿」。

examples.en: His marginal willingness to pay dropped after the first serving because he was already less hungry.
examples.zh: 吃完第一份后，他没那么饿了，因此「边际支付意愿」下降了。

words.enDefinition: in the US CPS, people outside the labour force who want and are available for work and searched within the past year but outside the recent four-week window

examples.en: The US table lists marginally attached workers separately because they have not searched recently.
examples.zh: 美国统计表单列「边缘劳动力」，因为这些人近期没有寻找工作。

examples.en: In the US example, marginally attached workers searched sometime in the past year and still wanted work.
examples.zh: 在美国示例中，「边缘劳动力」过去一年内曾经求职，现在仍想工作。

words.enDefinition: A policy tool using prices or tradable rights to change incentives rather than prescribing every action.

examples.en: The worksheet used a market-based instrument to let firms choose how to reduce their own emissions.
examples.zh: 练习表用「市场型政策工具」，让企业自行选择怎样减少本企业的排放。

examples.en: Our tutor compared a market-based instrument with a fixed rule applying to all the simulated firms.
examples.zh: 老师把「市场型政策工具」和适用于所有模拟企业的一条固定规则作了比较。

collocations: choose a market-based instrument for a policy model

words.enDefinition: Graph of how much all buyers together would buy at each price

examples.en: To draw the market demand curve, we added each student's purchases at the same price.
examples.zh: 为了绘制「市场需求曲线」，我们把同一价格下每名学生的购买量加起来。

examples.en: Our market demand curve included visitors as well as students because both groups bought festival tickets.
examples.zh: 我们的「市场需求曲线」既包含学生也包含访客，因为两类人都会买节庆门票。

collocations: slope of the market demand curve

words.enDefinition: Situation in which buyers and sellers intend to trade different amounts

examples.en: At the posted price, the difference between planned purchases and sales signals market disequilibrium.
examples.zh: 按标示价格，计划购买量和计划销售量之间的差额意味着「市场非均衡」。

examples.en: Our graph illustrates market disequilibrium by showing two different quantities at the same price.
examples.zh: 我们的图在同一个价格下标出两个不同数量，展示了「市场非均衡」。

words.enDefinition: Situation where buyers' planned purchases match sellers' planned sales at prevailing prices

examples.en: The example reaches market equilibrium when both sides want to trade thirty bus passes.
examples.zh: 当双方都想交易三十张公交通票时，这个例子就达到「市场均衡」。

examples.en: We marked market equilibrium where the two curves met on the grain market graph.
examples.zh: 我们在粮食市场图上两条曲线相交的位置标出了「市场均衡」。

words.enDefinition: A situation in which market choices do not lead to an efficient allocation of resources.

examples.en: The class identified a market failure when the factory's prices ignored costs borne by nearby residents.
examples.zh: 工厂的售价忽略了附近居民承担的成本，全班把这一情形识别为「市场失灵」。

examples.en: Our tutor used the flood warning example to show why market failure can leave services underprovided.
examples.zh: 老师用洪水预警例子说明，「市场失灵」为什么可能导致服务供给不足。

collocations: explain the source of market failure

words.enDefinition: A market where buyers cannot distinguish quality reliably, so lower-quality goods may drive out higher-quality ones.

examples.en: The seminar used a market for lemons to explain how good bicycles could disappear from the listings.
examples.zh: 研讨课用「柠檬市场」解释优质自行车为什么可能从商品列表中消失。

examples.en: Our group asked whether independent inspections could change the outcome in the example market for lemons.
examples.zh: 我们组问，独立检验能否改变例题中「柠檬市场」的结果。

collocations: evidence of a market for lemons

words.enDefinition: Output sold or intended for sale at prices that substantially influence how much producers offer and buyers demand.

examples.en: The baker's bread counts as market output because the shop sells it at economically significant prices.
examples.zh: 面包店以会显著影响供需的价格出售面包，因此计为「市场产出」。

examples.en: In the example, market output includes the repairs that customers pay the local workshop to perform.
examples.zh: 在示例中，顾客付费请本地维修点提供的维修服务属于「市场产出」。

words.enDefinition: the ability of a buyer or seller to influence market terms such as the price it pays or charges

examples.en: The producer had market power in the example because buyers considered its specialised service difficult to replace.
examples.zh: 在示例中，买家认为该生产者的专业服务难以替代，因此它具有「市场势力」。

examples.en: We discussed why closer substitutes could reduce a firm's market power without increasing the number of sellers.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了为何即使卖家数量不增加，更接近的替代品也可能削弱厂商的「市场势力」。

collocations: compete with a firm possessing market power

words.enDefinition: the competitive organisation of a market, including the number and size of firms and the nature of their products

examples.en: The market structure differed between the farm example with many sellers and the example with one utility.
examples.zh: 农场示例有许多卖家，公用事业示例只有一家，两者的「市场结构」不同。

examples.en: We examined market structure before deciding whether the model firm could influence the price it charged.
examples.zh: 判断模型厂商能否影响自己所收的价格前，我们先研究「市场结构」。

words.enDefinition: Graph of amounts all sellers together would offer at each price

examples.en: The market supply curve combines what all five bakeries would offer at each possible price.
examples.zh: 「市场供给曲线」汇总了五家面包店在每个可能价格下的供给量。

examples.en: For our sketch, the market supply curve now includes output from the new bakery downtown.
examples.zh: 我们画的「市场供给曲线」现在也包含市中心那家新面包店的产量。

words.enDefinition: In a lemons model, progressive withdrawal of higher-quality sellers as expected quality and prices fall.

examples.en: The simulation showed market unraveling after the withdrawal of good bicycles lowered buyers' willingness to pay.
examples.zh: 优质自行车退出后，买家的支付意愿下降，模拟展示了由此发生的「市场瓦解」。

examples.en: Our class discussed whether independent quality checks would slow market unraveling in the practice model.
examples.zh: 全班讨论了独立质量检查能否减缓练习模型中的「市场瓦解」。

collocations: assess the risk of market unraveling

words.enDefinition: the amount by which a price exceeds the marginal cost of producing the good

examples.en: The instructor compared markup over marginal cost for two firms with different degrees of demand responsiveness.
examples.zh: 讲师比较了两家具有不同需求响应程度的厂商的「高于边际成本的加价」。

examples.en: We calculated the markup over marginal cost by subtracting the extra production cost from the listed unit price.
examples.zh: 我们从所列单位价格扣除额外生产成本，计算「高于边际成本的加价」。

collocations: calculate the markup over marginal cost
compare markup over marginal cost across products

words.enDefinition: in a standard initially balanced trade model, depreciation improves the trade balance if the absolute import and export demand elasticities sum to more than one

examples.en: The tutor used the Marshall-Lerner condition to explain why responsiveness of both import and export quantities mattered.
examples.zh: 导师用「马歇尔勒纳条件」说明，进口和出口数量的响应程度为何都重要。

examples.en: We checked the assumptions behind the Marshall-Lerner condition before interpreting the two elasticities in our worksheet.
examples.zh: 解读练习表里的两个弹性之前，我们核查了「马歇尔勒纳条件」所依赖的假设。

collocations: state the assumptions of the Marshall-Lerner condition

words.enDefinition: Quantities that maximize satisfaction at given prices and a given income

examples.en: We derived Marshallian demand by choosing the best bundle within a fixed weekly allowance.
examples.zh: 我们在每周零花钱固定的条件下选择最优组合，推导出「马歇尔需求」。

examples.en: Our Marshallian demand changes when the student's income changes even though prices stay fixed.
examples.zh: 尽管价格保持不变，该学生的收入变化时，我们算出的「马歇尔需求」仍会变化。

words.enDefinition: A two-player game where one player benefits when choices match and the other benefits when they differ.

examples.en: We played matching pennies with two marked cards and kept score using classroom points.
examples.zh: 我们用两张有标记的卡片玩「硬币匹配博弈」，用课堂积分记分。

examples.en: The tutor used matching pennies to show why no pair of fixed actions was stable.
examples.zh: 老师用「硬币匹配博弈」说明为什么不存在稳定的固定行动组合。

collocations: use matching pennies to illustrate mixed strategies

words.enDefinition: A set of contracts offered together so participants can choose terms that suit their own circumstances.

examples.en: The model offered a menu of contracts that differed in their upfront fees and repair coverage.
examples.zh: 模型提供一套「合同选项组合」，各选项的前期费用与维修保障范围不同。

examples.en: The tutor asked why one menu of contracts might attract people with different expected usage levels.
examples.zh: 老师问，为什么一套「合同选项组合」可能吸引预期使用量各不相同的人。

collocations: choose from a menu of contracts

words.enDefinition: a proposed pattern in which economies reaching middle-income levels struggle to sustain progress toward high-income levels

examples.en: The course discussed the middle-income trap while noting that researchers use different thresholds and periods to define it.
examples.zh: 课程讨论了「中等收入陷阱」，同时指出研究人员用不同门槛和时段界定它。

examples.en: We compared proposed explanations for the middle-income trap after reading about changing productivity in several industries.
examples.zh: 阅读数个行业生产率变化的资料后，我们比较了「中等收入陷阱」的几种解释。

collocations: compare explanations for the middle-income trap

words.enDefinition: Calculation method that uses the average of endpoints as the percentage base

examples.en: Our class used the midpoint method to calculate elasticity between the two prices.
examples.zh: 我们班用「中点法」计算了两个价格之间的弹性。

examples.en: With the midpoint method, reversing which observation comes first leaves the elasticity estimate unchanged.
examples.zh: 使用「中点法」时，把两个观测值的顺序颠倒，弹性估计值仍然不变。

words.enDefinition: the lowest average total cost attainable over the feasible output levels for the stated cost curve

examples.en: The curve's minimum average total cost gave the lowest break-even price available to the perfectly competitive firm.
examples.zh: 曲线的「最低平均总成本」给出了完全竞争厂商可达到的最低盈亏平衡价格。

examples.en: We compared minimum average total cost across three plants before discussing which size was cheapest at its optimum.
examples.zh: 讨论哪种规模在各自最优产量下最省成本之前，我们比较了三个工厂的「最低平均总成本」。

collocations: locate minimum average total cost on the curve
compare price with minimum average total cost

words.enDefinition: the smallest output level at which long-run average cost reaches its minimum

examples.en: The minimum efficient scale was the first output level on the flat bottom of the long-run cost curve.
examples.zh: 长期平均成本曲线的底部为平段，进入平段的第一个产量就是「最小有效规模」。

examples.en: We compared the minimum efficient scale with estimated market demand in the example involving many small buyers.
examples.zh: 我们在涉及大量小买家的示例中，把「最小有效规模」与估计的市场需求作了比较。

collocations: compare minimum efficient scale with market size

words.enDefinition: Income from an unincorporated household enterprise that combines returns to the owner's labour and business.

examples.en: The tutor uses a family shop to illustrate mixed income from both work and ownership.
examples.zh: 老师用家庭经营的小店说明同时来自劳动和经营的「混合收入」。

examples.en: The example records mixed income because the owner's labour earnings cannot be separated from the business surplus.
examples.zh: 示例记录为「混合收入」，因为无法把业主的劳动收入和业务盈余分开。

words.enDefinition: A probability distribution over a player's pure strategies.

examples.en: We described a mixed strategy that assigned equal probabilities to the two complete plans on the worksheet.
examples.zh: 我们描述了一种「混合策略」，为练习表上的两个完整方案分配相等的概率。

examples.en: The tutor compared the expected payoffs from each mixed strategy in the classroom game.
examples.zh: 老师比较了课堂博弈中各种「混合策略」的期望收益。

collocations: choose probabilities for a mixed strategy

words.enDefinition: A Nash equilibrium in which players use probability distributions over pure strategies and at least one genuinely randomizes.

examples.en: The tutor derived a mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium for a game with no stable pair of pure choices.
examples.zh: 老师为一个没有稳定纯策略组合的博弈推导了「混合策略纳什均衡」。

examples.en: We verified the mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium by checking that neither team gained from changing its probabilities.
examples.zh: 我们检查了两队都不能靠单独改变概率而获益，以验证「混合策略纳什均衡」。

collocations: calculate probabilities for a mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium

words.enDefinition: The declared choice of variables, functional relationships, and assumptions used in an econometric model.

examples.en: We described the model specification before reporting the estimated relationship between schooling and pay in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们先说明「模型设定」，再报告受教育程度与工资的估计关系。

examples.en: The second model specification includes a term for prior experience that the first version leaves out.
examples.zh: 第二种「模型设定」纳入了第一版省略的既往经验项。

words.enDefinition: Statistical measure grouping together specified types of money and liquid balances

examples.en: The lecture explains why the monetary aggregate includes some accounts and excludes others.
examples.zh: 课堂解释了「货币总量指标」为什么纳入某些账户而排除其他账户。

examples.en: We chose the same monetary aggregate before comparing money growth across the two periods.
examples.zh: 比较两个时期的货币增长之前，我们选定了同一个「货币总量指标」。

words.enDefinition: Measure combining currency in circulation with banks' reserves at the central bank

examples.en: Our table gives the monetary base separately from the broader measures that include customer deposits.
examples.zh: 我们的统计表把「基础货币」与包括客户存款的较广义指标分开列出。

examples.en: An increase in bank reserves raised the monetary base in the classroom accounting example.
examples.zh: 在课堂的会计示例中，银行准备金增加使「基础货币」增加。

words.enDefinition: Shift toward a policy stance intended to support spending and borrowing

examples.en: The textbook scenario uses monetary easing to illustrate a possible response to weaker demand.
examples.zh: 教材情景用「货币政策宽松」举例说明需求转弱时的一种可能应对方式。

examples.en: We compared the effects of monetary easing after fast and slow changes in lending rates.
examples.zh: 我们比较了贷款利率快速和缓慢调整时「货币政策宽松」的效果。

words.enDefinition: Process through which policy decisions affect financial conditions, activity, and inflation

examples.en: We drew a diagram of monetary policy transmission starting with a rise in policy rates.
examples.zh: 我们绘制了以政策利率上调开始的「货币政策传导」图。

examples.en: The article explains why monetary policy transmission can be faster in some credit markets.
examples.zh: 文章解释了为什么「货币政策传导」在某些信贷市场可能更快。

words.enDefinition: Shift toward a more restrictive policy stance intended to restrain demand

examples.en: The model traces monetary tightening from higher policy rates to softer demand for credit.
examples.zh: 模型追踪了「货币政策收紧」如何从政策利率上涨传导到信贷需求转弱。

examples.en: Our exercise asks why monetary tightening may influence inflation only after a delay.
examples.zh: 习题问，为什么「货币政策收紧」可能要过一段时间才影响通胀。

words.enDefinition: an arrangement in which participating economies share a currency and normally a common monetary policy

examples.en: The two member economies in the example used the same currency after they joined the monetary union.
examples.zh: 示例中的两个成员经济体加入「货币联盟」后，使用同一货币。

examples.en: We discussed how a monetary union affects exchange between its members and transactions with countries outside it.
examples.zh: 我们讨论「货币联盟」怎样影响成员间交易以及与联盟外国家的交易。

collocations: study monetary policy within a monetary union

words.enDefinition: Textbook condition where desired money holdings equal the amount supplied

examples.en: Our model reaches money market equilibrium where the supply of money equals desired holdings.
examples.zh: 在我们的模型中，货币供给量等于所需持有量时达到「货币市场均衡」。

examples.en: We redrew the money market equilibrium diagram after changing the assumed level of income.
examples.zh: 修改收入水平假设后，我们重新画了「货币市场均衡」图。

words.enDefinition: Ratio of a chosen money stock to the monetary base

examples.en: The worksheet compares the money multiplier under different assumptions about cash and excess reserves.
examples.zh: 习题比较了对现金及超额准备金作出不同假设时的「货币乘数」。

examples.en: In this example, the money multiplier is smaller because households hold more cash.
examples.zh: 在这个例子中，家庭持有更多现金，所以「货币乘数」更小。

words.enDefinition: Stock of money available under the specific aggregate definition being used

examples.en: The lecture compares two measures of the money supply that include different deposits.
examples.zh: 课堂比较了两种纳入不同存款类别的「货币供给量」指标。

examples.en: We examined how the reported money supply changed after a shift between account types.
examples.zh: 我们研究了存款在账户类型之间转移后，公布的「货币供给量」如何变化。

words.enDefinition: Resources spent observing or verifying how another party performs its responsibilities.

examples.en: The worksheet included a monitoring cost for the time spent checking whether the agreed work was complete.
examples.zh: 练习表把检查约定工作是否完成所花时间计入一项「监督成本」。

examples.en: We compared the monitoring cost with the benefit of avoiding errors in the hypothetical arrangement.
examples.zh: 我们把「监督成本」与假设安排中因避免错误而获得的收益作了比较。

collocations: compare a monitoring cost with expected benefits

words.enDefinition: a market structure with many firms, differentiated products and relatively free entry and exit

examples.en: We studied monopolistic competition using several cafés that differed in location, menu and other features valued by customers.
examples.zh: 我们用几家在位置、菜单及顾客看重的其他特点上各不相同的咖啡馆学习「垄断竞争」。

examples.en: Under monopolistic competition, new sellers reduced sales for existing varieties in our simplified long-run exercise.
examples.zh: 在简化的长期练习中，「垄断竞争」下新增卖家减少了现有产品品种的销量。

collocations: analyse an industry under monopolistic competition
compare monopolistic competition with perfect competition

words.enDefinition: the total surplus lost when a monopoly reduces mutually beneficial trades relative to an efficient quantity

examples.en: The tutor shaded monopoly deadweight loss between demand and marginal cost for units the seller did not supply.
examples.zh: 导师把卖家未供应的那些单位在需求线和边际成本线之间的「垄断无谓损失」涂上阴影。

examples.en: We compared monopoly deadweight loss with the producer's profit to see why the two measures differed.
examples.zh: 我们将「垄断无谓损失」与生产者利润比较，了解两项指标为什么不同。

collocations: shade monopoly deadweight loss on a graph
compare monopoly deadweight loss across cases

words.enDefinition: the quantity chosen by the monopoly seller given its demand, costs and objective

examples.en: The monopoly output was lower than the competitive quantity under the two curves used in class.
examples.zh: 在课堂给定的需求和边际成本曲线下，「垄断产量」低于竞争产量。

examples.en: We calculated monopoly output before using the demand curve to find the price consumers would pay.
examples.zh: 我们先计算「垄断产量」，再用需求曲线找出消费者愿意支付的价格。

collocations: compare monopoly output with competitive output
find the price associated with monopoly output

words.enDefinition: setting prices in a market with one seller of the product and no close substitutes within the model

examples.en: The lesson compared monopoly pricing with the outcome from several identical suppliers selling the same service.
examples.zh: 这节课比较了「垄断定价」与多个相同供应者销售同一服务时的结果。

examples.en: We used monopoly pricing to explain why the model's supplier considered how its price affected total sales.
examples.zh: 我们用「垄断定价」说明模型里的供应商为何考虑价格对总销量的影响。

collocations: compare monopoly pricing with competitive pricing

words.enDefinition: the economic profit earned by the sole seller under the demand and cost conditions being analysed

examples.en: The monopoly profit changed after higher production costs were entered into the classroom model of one service provider.
examples.zh: 在课堂的单一服务供应商模型中输入更高生产成本后，「垄断利润」改变了。

examples.en: We shaded monopoly profit between price and average total cost over the quantity actually sold in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中，我们按实际销量把售价与平均总成本之间的「垄断利润」区域涂上阴影。

collocations: compare monopoly profit across cost assumptions

words.enDefinition: the single buyer in a market under the monopsony model

examples.en: The monopsonist faced an upward supply curve because higher purchase prices drew more sellers into the market.
examples.zh: 「买方垄断者」面临向上倾斜的供给曲线，因为更高买价会吸引更多卖家进入市场。

examples.en: We compared the quantity a monopsonist bought with the amount purchased in the two-buyer version of the model.
examples.zh: 我们把「买方垄断者」的购买量与双买方模型中的购买量作了比较。

collocations: estimate the purchases of a monopsonist
compare a monopsonist with competing buyers

words.zhGloss: 具有买方势力的劳动力市场
words.enDefinition: a labour market in which employers face upward-sloping labour supply and can influence wages through hiring decisions
acceptedZhAnswers: 具有买方势力的劳动力市场

examples.en: Our monopsonistic labour market example showed how a long commute reduced the options available to job seekers.
examples.zh: 「具有买方势力的劳动力市场」示例显示，通勤时间长会减少求职者的可选岗位。

examples.en: The model compared wages in a monopsonistic labour market with those in a competitive labour market.
examples.zh: 模型比较了「具有买方势力的劳动力市场」与竞争性劳动力市场中的工资。

collocations: compare wages in a monopsonistic labour market

words.enDefinition: a market structure with one buyer for the input or product under consideration

examples.en: The lesson used a town with only one crop buyer to explain how monopsony affected the farmers.
examples.zh: 课堂用只有一家农作物收购商的小镇解释「买方垄断」如何影响农民。

examples.en: Our model compared monopsony with a case where several employers competed for the same pool of workers.
examples.zh: 模型比较了「买方垄断」与多个雇主争聘同一批劳动者的情形。

collocations: model a labour market under monopsony

words.enDefinition: Preferences never ranking more of a good lower, with other amounts unchanged

examples.en: Under strict monotonic preferences, one extra apple makes the original bundle more desirable.
examples.zh: 在严格「单调偏好」下，多加入一个苹果会让原组合更受偏好。

examples.en: The graph illustrates weak monotonic preferences where an extra apple leaves satisfaction unchanged.
examples.zh: 该图展示了一种弱「单调偏好」，多一个苹果也不会改变满足感。

words.enDefinition: Percentage change in the price index compared with the previous month

examples.en: Our chart uses month-over-month inflation to show how quickly prices changed from April to May.
examples.zh: 我们的图用「环比通胀」展示了四月到五月的价格变动速度。

examples.en: The month-over-month inflation figure rose while the twelve-month inflation rate fell in the exercise.
examples.zh: 在习题中，「环比通胀」读数上升，而十二个月通胀率下降。

words.enDefinition: A change in incentives or behavior when another party bears some consequences and cannot readily observe the behavior.

examples.en: The exercise considered moral hazard when repair costs were shared but daily care could not be monitored.
examples.zh: 练习考虑了分摊维修费用、又无法观察日常养护时可能出现的「道德风险」。

examples.en: Our tutor used moral hazard to discuss why coverage might change maintenance effort in the classroom model.
examples.zh: 老师用「道德风险」讨论为什么在课堂模型中，获得保障可能改变维护投入。

collocations: distinguish moral hazard from adverse selection

words.enDefinition: the tariff applicable under most-favoured-nation treatment, apart from rates under permitted preferential arrangements

examples.en: The report listed the most-favoured-nation tariff beside the lower rate applied under a bilateral trade agreement.
examples.zh: 报告将「最惠国关税」与双边贸易协定下适用的较低税率并排列出。

examples.en: We compared the most-favoured-nation tariff across categories of manufactured goods in the published example table.
examples.zh: 我们用公开示例表比较各类制成品的「最惠国关税」。

collocations: check the most-favoured-nation tariff for a category

words.enDefinition: under WTO rules and applicable exceptions, extending a trade advantage granted to one trading partner to other members

examples.en: The tutor distinguished most-favoured-nation treatment across partners from the treatment of imported and domestic products within a market.
examples.zh: 导师区分了贸易伙伴之间的「最惠国待遇」和同一市场里进口产品与本国产品所受的待遇。

examples.en: We discussed how most-favoured-nation treatment applied to the duty schedules in our simplified WTO classroom case.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「最惠国待遇」如何适用于简化的 WTO 课堂案例中的关税表。

collocations: compare most-favoured-nation treatment with national treatment

words.expression: movement along the aggregate demand curve
words.lemma: movement along the aggregate demand curve
words.enDefinition: A change in output demanded caused by a change in the price level with other conditions held fixed.
acceptedEnVariants: movement along the aggregate demand curve

examples.en: The movement along the aggregate demand curve follows a price change without an underlying spending shift.
examples.zh: 总体价格变化使图上的对应点「沿总需求曲线移动」，而支出倾向未发生改变。

examples.en: We used an arrow to mark movement along the aggregate demand curve on the diagram.
examples.zh: 我们在示意图上用箭头标记「沿总需求曲线移动」的方向。

collocations: show movement along the aggregate demand curve
explain movement along the aggregate demand curve
movement along the aggregate demand curve after a price change

words.enDefinition: shortfalls experienced across several dimensions of wellbeing or basic living conditions

examples.en: The table showed overlapping indicators of multidimensional deprivation in schooling and access to safe water.
examples.zh: 该表显示了教育与安全用水方面相互重叠的「多维匮乏」指标。

examples.en: We discussed multidimensional deprivation after noticing that similar incomes coexisted with very different levels of service access.
examples.zh: 发现收入相近的群体享受服务的水平却非常不同后，我们讨论了「多维匮乏」。

words.enDefinition: a poverty indicator combining deprivations across several domains such as health, education and living conditions

examples.en: The multidimensional poverty measure recorded some households as deprived because they lacked access to several essential services.
examples.zh: 由于缺乏多项基本服务，「多维贫困指标」将部分家庭记录为面临匮乏。

examples.en: We compared the multidimensional poverty measure with the income-based rate for the same communities in class.
examples.zh: 我们在课堂上将「多维贫困指标」与同一批社区按收入测算的比率作了比较。

words.enDefinition: Output relative to a combined measure of multiple production inputs, commonly labour and capital.

examples.en: The worksheet estimates multifactor productivity using an output series and combined measures of labour and capital.
examples.zh: 练习使用产出序列及劳动和资本的合并指标估计「多要素生产率」。

examples.en: We discussed why a rise in multifactor productivity may reflect several changes in the economy.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了为什么「多要素生产率」上升可能反映经济中的多种变化。

words.enDefinition: Two or more distinct equilibrium strategy profiles in the same game.

examples.en: The scheduling example had multiple equilibria because the clubs could coordinate on either of two days.
examples.zh: 排期例题存在「多个均衡」，因为两个社团在两天中的哪一天都可以协调一致。

examples.en: We checked the payoff matrix for multiple equilibria after changing the points awarded for sharing equipment.
examples.zh: 我们改变共用设备获得的积分之后，核查收益矩阵里是否有「多个均衡」。

words.enDefinition: A regression model with more than one explanatory variable for the same outcome.

examples.en: The multiple regression model includes prior grades and attendance when relating study hours to test scores.
examples.zh: 「多元回归模型」分析学习时数与测试成绩的关系时，同时纳入先前成绩和出勤率。

examples.en: We compared a multiple regression model with one that included only attendance in the classroom example.
examples.zh: 在课堂示例中，我们比较了「多元回归模型」和只纳入出勤率的模型。

words.enDefinition: An outcome in which both players choose the cooperative action.

examples.en: Mutual cooperation gave both clubs extra workshop time in the first case on the worksheet.
examples.zh: 练习表的第一个案例中，「双方合作」让两个社团都得到更多工作坊时间。

examples.en: We compared mutual cooperation with the outcome where only one team helped maintain the shared space.
examples.zh: 我们将「双方合作」与只有一队协助维护共享空间的结果作比较。

collocations: compare mutual cooperation with mutual defection
reach mutual cooperation in a repeated game

words.enDefinition: An outcome in which both players choose the noncooperative action.

examples.en: Mutual defection left the shared project without any tokens from either team in the exercise.
examples.zh: 在练习里，「双方背叛」意味着共享项目没有得到任一队的代币。

examples.en: Our tutor asked why mutual defection could be stable even though cooperation helped both clubs.
examples.zh: 老师问，虽然合作对两个社团都有利，「双方背叛」为什么可能保持稳定。

collocations: compare the payoffs under mutual defection

words.enDefinition: Unemployment rate at which inflation neither accelerates nor slows within a model

examples.en: The class estimated the NAIRU from a model relating unemployment to changes in inflation.
examples.zh: 全班利用一个把失业与通胀变化联系起来的模型，估算「非加速通胀失业率」。

examples.en: Two different sets of assumptions produced different estimates of the NAIRU in our exercise.
examples.zh: 在练习中，两套不同假设得出了不同的「非加速通胀失业率」估值。

words.enDefinition: Money measure emphasizing currency and balances available for relatively immediate spending

examples.en: The report describes narrow money as the more readily spendable portion of the measure.
examples.zh: 报告将「狭义货币」称为该指标中较容易直接用于支出的部分。

examples.en: Our cross-country table defines narrow money separately for each economy in the comparison.
examples.zh: 我们的跨国统计表分别给出参与比较的各经济体对「狭义货币」的定义。

words.enDefinition: in the two-player symmetric model, the feasible individually rational outcome maximising the product of both players' gains over disagreement

examples.en: The tutor used the Nash bargaining solution to divide the gains from a joint studio booking.
examples.zh: 老师用「纳什谈判解」分配共同预订工作室所获得的收益。

examples.en: We recalculated the Nash bargaining solution after one club gained access to another room.
examples.zh: 一个社团获准使用另一间教室后，我们重新计算了「纳什谈判解」。

collocations: compare a Nash bargaining solution across disagreement points

words.enDefinition: A strategy profile in which no player can gain by changing strategy alone.

examples.en: The class found a Nash equilibrium where neither club benefited from changing its own booking choice.
examples.zh: 全班找到了一个「纳什均衡」，在该组合中两个社团都无法靠单独改变时段选择获益。

examples.en: We tested each possible Nash equilibrium by keeping one team's choice fixed while checking the other's options.
examples.zh: 我们固定一队的选择、检查另一队的选项，以检验每个可能的「纳什均衡」。

words.enDefinition: A table from the national accounts presenting measures such as output, income, or expenditure.

examples.en: The national accounts table separates household spending from the government's consumption of goods and services.
examples.zh: 「国民账户表」把住户支出与政府的货物和服务消费分列。

examples.en: We read the national accounts table to find the source of the investment figure.
examples.zh: 我们查阅「国民账户表」，找到投资数据的来源。

words.enDefinition: a poverty threshold defined for a particular country according to its own measurement criteria

examples.en: The survey measured the share of households below the national poverty line specified in the accompanying notes.
examples.zh: 调查统计低于附注所指定「国家贫困线」的家庭占比。

examples.en: We checked how the national poverty line was adjusted for local living costs in the example report.
examples.zh: 我们核查了示例报告如何按当地生活成本调整「国家贫困线」。

collocations: measure poverty at the national poverty line

words.enDefinition: in applicable trade rules, treating qualifying foreign products, services or suppliers no less favourably than comparable domestic ones as specified

examples.en: The class used national treatment to compare taxes on imported goods with those on comparable domestic goods.
examples.zh: 同学们用「国民待遇」比较进口品和可比本国产品所缴的税。

examples.en: We checked the scope of national treatment before interpreting the sample provision on access for service suppliers.
examples.zh: 解读有关服务供应商准入的示例条款之前，我们核查了「国民待遇」的适用范围。

collocations: review the scope of national treatment

words.enDefinition: A study using a naturally occurring rule or event that creates a comparison resembling an experiment.

examples.en: The lesson treats the simulated eligibility change as a natural experiment under a stated assignment assumption.
examples.zh: 课程在给定分配假设下，把模拟的资格变动当作「自然实验」。

examples.en: We discussed whether the change in classroom schedules could support a credible natural experiment.
examples.zh: 我们讨论课堂时间表的变动能否支持一个可信的「自然实验」。

words.enDefinition: a market situation where one producer can supply the relevant total demand at lower cost than multiple producers

examples.en: The course used a shared water network to illustrate a natural monopoly with unusually high fixed infrastructure costs.
examples.zh: 课程用共用供水网络说明固定基础设施成本特别高的「自然垄断」。

examples.en: We checked whether natural monopoly remained a credible description after the expected market demand increased.
examples.zh: 预计市场需求增大后，我们检验「自然垄断」是否仍是合理的描述。

collocations: analyse pricing in a natural monopoly

words.enDefinition: a market where efficient firm size is sufficiently large relative to demand that only a few firms can operate efficiently

examples.en: Our tutor illustrated natural oligopoly with an industry where each efficient plant served a large share of demand.
examples.zh: 导师用单个高效工厂能满足很大一部分需求的行业演示「自然寡头结构」。

examples.en: We checked whether the industry would still have a natural oligopoly if its minimum efficient scale declined.
examples.zh: 我们核查最小有效规模降低后，该行业是否仍会形成「自然寡头结构」。

collocations: explain the emergence of a natural oligopoly
compare natural oligopoly with natural monopoly

words.enDefinition: Unemployment rate consistent with normal labor adjustment absent cyclical demand weakness

examples.en: Faster job matching lowered the natural rate of unemployment in the model used for class.
examples.zh: 在课堂所用的模型中，岗位匹配加快降低了「自然失业率」。

examples.en: We compared observed unemployment with an estimate of the natural rate of unemployment in the exercise.
examples.zh: 在习题中，我们把观测到的失业率和估计的「自然失业率」作了比较。

collocations: estimate the natural rate of unemployment
changes in the natural rate of unemployment
model the natural rate of unemployment

words.enDefinition: Product whose demand increases less than proportionally when buyers' income rises

examples.en: The exercise calls basic groceries a necessity good because purchases rise less than income.
examples.zh: 习题把基本食品称为「必需品」，因为购买量的增幅小于收入的增幅。

examples.en: We used the income data to decide whether soap was a necessity good in the model.
examples.zh: 我们用收入数据判断肥皂在该模型中是不是「必需品」。

words.enDefinition: An uncompensated cost imposed on others who are not directly involved in the activity.

examples.en: The example treated delivery noise as a negative externality because it disturbed nearby residents at night.
examples.zh: 例题把配送噪声视为「负外部性」，因为它夜间打扰了附近居民。

examples.en: We discussed a negative externality from litter that remained after customers took their food away.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了顾客带走食物后留下的垃圾所造成的一种「负外部性」。

words.enDefinition: a drop in total output when the amount of a particular input is increased with other inputs fixed

examples.en: The negative marginal product meant that adding another worker actually reduced output in the overcrowded stall.
examples.zh: 「负的边际产量」表示，在这个过于拥挤的摊位上增加一名工人反而降低产量。

examples.en: We identified negative marginal product where the total output curve sloped downward as staffing rose further.
examples.zh: 人数继续增加而总产量曲线下降时，我们识别出「负的边际产量」。

words.enDefinition: GDP minus consumption of fixed capital during the accounting period.

examples.en: Net domestic product is below GDP in the worksheet because fixed assets lose value through use.
examples.zh: 由于固定资产在使用中贬值，练习纸上的「国内生产净值」低于 GDP。

examples.en: We calculated net domestic product after reading the separate estimate of fixed capital consumption.
examples.zh: 我们查阅单独估算的固定资本消耗后，算出了「国内生产净值」。

collocations: measure net domestic product per person

words.enDefinition: the BPM6 balancing item reflecting discrepancies among separately measured parts of the balance of payments

examples.en: The BPM6 table showed net errors and omissions after combining estimates drawn from several statistical sources.
examples.zh: BPM6 表格汇总来自多个统计来源的估计后，列示了「净误差与遗漏」。

examples.en: The tutor explained why net errors and omissions could not automatically be attributed to one particular transaction category.
examples.zh: 导师说明，为什么不能直接把「净误差与遗漏」归因于某个特定交易类别。

collocations: review the size of net errors and omissions

words.enDefinition: an economy exporting more than it imports in a specified good, sector or total trade measure

examples.en: The example economy became a net exporter of fruit even though it still imported some varieties.
examples.zh: 示例经济体成为水果的「净出口方」，尽管它仍进口某些品种。

examples.en: We checked trade records to see whether the region was a net exporter of machinery.
examples.zh: 我们用进出口记录判断该地区是否为机械产品的「净出口方」。

collocations: compare a net exporter with a net importer

words.enDefinition: an economy importing more than it exports in a specified good, sector or total trade measure

examples.en: The country remained a net importer of fuel despite selling a small amount to a neighbouring market.
examples.zh: 这个国家向邻近市场出售少量燃料，但仍是燃料的「净进口方」。

examples.en: Our chart changed when the example region went from being a net importer to exporting more grain.
examples.zh: 示例地区从粮食「净进口方」变为出口多于进口时，我们的图也随之改变。

words.enDefinition: residents' stock of external financial assets minus their stock of external financial liabilities at a given time

examples.en: The net international investment position stayed negative because foreign liabilities still exceeded external assets in the example.
examples.zh: 示例中，对外负债仍超过对外资产，因此「净国际投资头寸」保持为负。

examples.en: We calculated the net international investment position before comparing the economies' external assets net of liabilities.
examples.zh: 比较各经济体扣除对外负债后的对外资产前，我们计算了「净国际投资头寸」。

collocations: calculate the net international investment position
report a net international investment position
explain a change in the net international investment position

words.enDefinition: the balancing amount after current income, spending and capital transactions, showing funds available to others or needed from them

examples.en: The worksheet shows net lending or borrowing for each sector after recording its capital transactions.
examples.zh: 练习纸在记录各部门的资本交易后，列出它们的「净贷出或净借入」。

examples.en: We read net lending or borrowing as negative for the sector that needs external funds.
examples.zh: 需要外部资金的部门，其「净贷出或净借入」数据为负。

collocations: net lending or borrowing by sector

words.enDefinition: Gross national income less consumption of fixed capital over the same period.

examples.en: We calculated net national income by deducting fixed capital consumption from the sample gross figure.
examples.zh: 我们从示例总额中扣除固定资本消耗，算出「国民净收入」。

examples.en: The slide compares net national income for two fictional countries with similar levels of gross income.
examples.zh: 幻灯片比较两个总收入水平相近的虚构国家的「国民净收入」。

words.enDefinition: Taxes on products less subsidies on those products in the national accounts.

examples.en: The sample table adds net taxes on products to convert basic-price value added to market-price GDP.
examples.zh: 示例表加上「产品税净额」，将按基本价格计量的增加值换算为按市场价格计量的 GDP。

examples.en: We checked where net taxes on products appear between the industry totals and final GDP figure.
examples.zh: 我们查阅「产品税净额」在行业总量和最终 GDP 数据之间的列示位置。

words.enDefinition: Gross value added after deducting consumption of fixed capital.

examples.en: The example subtracts the wear on the equipment before reporting the workshop's net value added.
examples.zh: 报告维修点的「净增加值」前，示例扣除设备损耗。

examples.en: Our table compares net value added across industries with different amounts of fixed capital use.
examples.zh: 我们的表格对比固定资本消耗量不同的各行业的「净增加值」。

words.enDefinition: An increase in overall welfare relative to a baseline once relevant benefits and costs are included.

examples.en: The exercise found a net welfare gain after comparing reduced noise damage with the cost of abatement.
examples.zh: 练习把减少的噪声损害和治理成本比较后，发现存在「净福利增益」。

examples.en: We calculated the net welfare gain against the baseline chosen for the classroom policy comparison.
examples.zh: 我们按课堂政策对比中选定的基准计算了「净福利增益」。

collocations: compare net welfare gains across policies

words.enDefinition: an estimated interest rate consistent with output at potential and stable inflation over the relevant horizon

examples.en: Our model uses a neutral interest rate to judge whether the policy rate restrains activity.
examples.zh: 模型用「中性利率」来判断政策利率是否抑制经济活动。

examples.en: The reading discusses why the neutral interest rate must be inferred instead of observed directly.
examples.zh: 阅读材料讨论了为什么「中性利率」需要推断，无法直接观测。

collocations: uncertainty around the neutral interest rate

words.enDefinition: Units that do not receive treatment during the observed period and serve as a comparison group.

examples.en: The never-treated comparison group contains schools without a tutoring programme during the entire classroom study.
examples.zh: 「始终未处理比较组」由课堂研究期间一直没有辅导项目的学校组成。

examples.en: We used the never-treated comparison group as a reference when estimating effects for the earliest cohort.
examples.zh: 估计最早批次的效应时，我们参考了「始终未处理比较组」。

words.enDefinition: The assumption that future treatment does not affect outcomes before the designated start of treatment.

examples.en: The no anticipation assumption would fail if students changed attendance before the scheduled start of tutoring.
examples.zh: 如果学生在辅导计划开始前就改变出勤情况，「无预期效应假设」就不成立。

examples.en: Our study design states the no anticipation assumption next to the programme's announced start date.
examples.zh: 我们的研究设计在项目宣布的开始日期旁写明「无预期效应假设」。

collocations: violation of the no anticipation assumption

words.enDefinition: an index combining exchange rates against multiple partners' currencies using specified weights without relative price adjustment

examples.en: The nominal effective exchange rate reflected movements against several currencies instead of the rate against just one partner.
examples.zh: 「名义有效汇率」反映相对多种货币的变动，涵盖的范围超过单一伙伴的汇率。

examples.en: We read the weighting note before comparing the nominal effective exchange rate indexes published for two economies.
examples.zh: 比较两个经济体公布的「名义有效汇率」指数前，我们先看了权重说明。

collocations: calculate a nominal effective exchange rate
report the nominal effective exchange rate
compare changes in nominal effective exchange rates

words.enDefinition: GDP measured using the prices prevailing in the period when production occurs.

examples.en: Nominal GDP rises in the first example because prices increase while the volume of output stays unchanged.
examples.zh: 第一个例子中，产出量保持不变，价格上涨使「名义国内生产总值」提高。

examples.en: We compared nominal GDP across two years before applying any adjustment for changing prices.
examples.zh: 进行价格变动调整之前，我们比较了两个年度的「名义国内生产总值」。

words.enDefinition: Tendency of wages measured in money to adjust slowly, especially downward

examples.en: The model assumes nominal wage rigidity because existing hourly contracts reset only once a year.
examples.zh: 现有的计时工资合同每年只调整一次，因此模型假定存在「名义工资刚性」。

examples.en: We compared nominal wage rigidity with a model where wages immediately respond to demand changes.
examples.zh: 我们把「名义工资刚性」与工资立即响应需求变化的模型作了比较。

words.enDefinition: The property by which chained monetary estimates for components need not sum to the corresponding total.

examples.en: Non-additivity explains why the published real components do not sum exactly to total GDP in our example.
examples.zh: 「不可加总性」解释了示例里已公布的各项实际值为何加起来不完全等于 GDP 总额。
