examples.en: We distinguished the regression disturbance from the numerical error computed after fitting the sample model.
examples.zh: 我们区分了「回归扰动项」和拟合样本模型后计算出的数值误差。

words.enDefinition: the constant in a regression equation, giving the fitted value when the nonconstant model terms equal zero

examples.en: The regression intercept gives predicted wages when every regressor is zero in the simplified example.
examples.zh: 在简化示例中，各解释变量都为零时，「回归截距」给出预测工资。

examples.en: We discussed whether the regression intercept had a meaningful interpretation given the range of schooling.
examples.zh: 考虑到受教育年限的取值范围，我们讨论了「回归截距」是否具有实际含义。

words.enDefinition: A situation in which regulation is unduly influenced to serve regulated or other special interests.

examples.en: The fictional case examined regulatory capture after the agency consistently prioritised the interests of regulated firms.
examples.zh: 虚构案例分析了「监管俘获」，其中机构一贯将受监管企业的利益放在优先位置。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how regulatory capture might change which costs were counted in the classroom model.
examples.zh: 老师问，「监管俘获」可能怎样改变课堂模型将哪些成本纳入计算。

collocations: identify a risk of regulatory capture
discuss the effects of regulatory capture

words.enDefinition: A rule setting a requirement that an activity, product or process must meet.

examples.en: The classroom case compared a regulatory standard for noise with a fee based on the level of noise.
examples.zh: 课堂案例比较了噪声「监管标准」和按噪声水平收取的费用。

examples.en: We asked whether the regulatory standard in the model applied to output or to the production process.
examples.zh: 我们问，模型中的「监管标准」是针对产品还是针对生产过程。

collocations: compare a regulatory standard with a market incentive

words.enDefinition: poverty measured relative to the standard of living or income distribution in the same society

examples.en: The model defined relative poverty using a threshold set as a share of the national median income.
examples.zh: 模型用相当于全国收入中位数一定比例的门槛定义「相对贫困」。

examples.en: We compared relative poverty in two periods after checking how the threshold changed when median income increased.
examples.zh: 我们检查收入中位数提高时门槛怎样变化，再比较两个时期的「相对贫困」。

words.enDefinition: A sampling design that draws separate cross-sectional samples over time without following the same units.

examples.en: The repeated cross-section surveys new workers each year instead of following the same people over time.
examples.zh: 「重复横截面」每年调查新的一批劳动者，没有持续跟踪同一批人。

examples.en: We used repeated cross-section data to compare average outcomes across the two districts over time.
examples.zh: 我们使用「重复横截面」数据，比较两个地区的平均结果随时间的变化。

words.enDefinition: A game formed by playing the same underlying stage game on multiple occasions.

examples.en: The class used a repeated game to see whether two teams would keep sharing equipment over time.
examples.zh: 全班用「重复博弈」查看两队是否会一直共用设备。

examples.en: We compared the decisions in a repeated game with the ones made in a single round.
examples.zh: 我们把「重复博弈」中的决定与只进行一轮时的决定作了比较。

collocations: compare a repeated game with a single round

words.enDefinition: An arrangement in which past behaviour affects trust and future transactions, giving participants incentives to maintain quality.

examples.en: The case included a reputation mechanism in which past transactions affected how much buyers trusted each seller.
examples.zh: 案例包含一种「声誉机制」，其中过去的交易会影响买家对各卖家的信任。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether the reputation mechanism still mattered when sellers expected only one transaction.
examples.zh: 老师问，当卖家预计只会发生一次交易时，「声誉机制」是否仍然重要。

collocations: a reputation mechanism based on reviews

words.enDefinition: buying in a lower-price market and reselling in a higher-price market to profit from the price gap

examples.en: The classroom model tested whether resale arbitrage would narrow the price difference between the two buyer groups.
examples.zh: 课堂模型检验「转售套利」是否会缩小两个买方群体之间的价差。

examples.en: We discussed why resale arbitrage was easier for a physical textbook than for an individual swimming lesson.
examples.zh: 我们讨论为什么实体教材比一对一游泳课更容易发生「转售套利」。

collocations: account for resale arbitrage in a model

words.enDefinition: Rule specifying reserves banks must maintain against certain liabilities under a framework

examples.en: The textbook model assumes a reserve requirement tied to a specified group of deposits.
examples.zh: 教材模型假定「法定准备金要求」与指定类别的存款有关。

examples.en: We compared two banking frameworks with different ways of setting the reserve requirement.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两种以不同方式设定「法定准备金要求」的银行制度。

words.enDefinition: A household, business, or other institutional unit with its main economic interest in an economy's territory.

examples.en: The worksheet asks whether the local branch qualifies as a resident institutional unit in the example.
examples.zh: 练习题要求判断示例中的本地分支机构是否属于「常住机构单位」。

examples.en: The accounts record the household as a resident institutional unit under the stated assumptions.
examples.zh: 在给定假设下，账户将该住户记录为「常住机构单位」。

collocations: resident institutional unit in the accounts

words.enDefinition: the demand left for a particular firm at each price after subtracting the quantity supplied by competitors

examples.en: The residual demand facing the large supplier fell when the smaller firms offered more output at each price.
examples.zh: 较小厂商在各价格下提供更多产量后，大供应商面临的「剩余需求」下降了。

examples.en: We calculated residual demand at each listed price by subtracting rival supply from the total market demand.
examples.zh: 我们在各给定价格下，用市场总需求扣除竞争者供给，求出「剩余需求」。

collocations: estimate residual demand facing a firm

words.enDefinition: A model in which specified conditions are imposed on the coefficients or available terms.

examples.en: The restricted model sets both schooling interaction coefficients to zero in the instructor's example.
examples.zh: 在老师的示例中，「受约束模型」将两个教育交互项的系数都设为零。

examples.en: We fitted the restricted model before comparing it with one that allows those coefficients to vary.
examples.zh: 我们先拟合「受约束模型」，再把它与允许相应系数变化的模型比较。

collocations: compare a restricted model with its unrestricted counterpart

words.enDefinition: how output changes when all production inputs are multiplied by the same factor

examples.en: The tutor measured returns to scale by doubling labour and equipment together in the production example.
examples.zh: 导师在生产示例中同时将劳动和设备用量加倍，以衡量「规模报酬」。

examples.en: We compared returns to scale for two production functions using the same proportional change in both inputs.
examples.zh: 我们将两种投入同时按相同比例改变，比较两个生产函数的「规模报酬」。

collocations: classify a production function by its returns to scale

words.enDefinition: Inference about someone's rankings drawn from choices among the options they could afford

examples.en: The revealed preference argument uses Mira's purchase and the other basket she could afford.
examples.zh: 「显示偏好」的推理用到了米拉的实际购买选择和她买得起的另一篮商品。

examples.en: We used revealed preference to learn what the shopper favored without asking for ratings.
examples.zh: 我们用「显示偏好」了解购物者更喜欢什么，省去了请她打分的环节。

words.enDefinition: Under standard independent private-value assumptions with risk-neutral bidders, formats with the same allocation rule and lowest-type payoff yield equal expected revenue.

examples.en: The revenue equivalence theorem linked two auction formats under the assumptions written on our worksheet.
examples.zh: 按照练习表所列的假设，「收益等价定理」将两种拍卖形式联系起来。

examples.en: Our tutor asked why risk neutrality mattered for the revenue equivalence theorem in the simple example.
examples.zh: 老师问，在这个简单例题中，风险中性为什么对「收益等价定理」重要。

collocations: check the assumptions of the revenue equivalence theorem

words.enDefinition: A reform designed to keep government revenue unchanged relative to a specified baseline.

examples.en: The classroom case designed a revenue-neutral reform but found different households would pay different amounts afterward.
examples.zh: 课堂案例设计了「税收收入中性的改革」，但发现改革后各家庭的缴款额会发生不同变化。

examples.en: We compared receipts before and after the revenue-neutral reform to check the total in the model.
examples.zh: 我们对比「税收收入中性的改革」前后的收入，以核查模型中的合计。

collocations: compare two options for revenue-neutral reform
test assumptions in a revenue-neutral reform

words.enDefinition: A situation in which the supposed outcome influences the variable proposed as its cause.

examples.en: Reverse causality is possible if better expected wages affect workers' decisions to seek further training.
examples.zh: 如果更高的预期工资影响劳动者是否寻求进一步培训，就可能存在「反向因果」。

examples.en: The class considered reverse causality before interpreting the observed association between grades and tutoring hours.
examples.zh: 全班先考虑「反向因果」，再解释成绩与辅导时数的观测关联。

words.enDefinition: a trade model explaining specialisation through differences in relative production productivity, commonly with labour as the only input

examples.en: The Ricardian trade model used different labour requirements for making the same goods in the two economies.
examples.zh: 「李嘉图贸易模型」为两经济体生产同类商品设置了不同的劳动需求量。

examples.en: We used the Ricardian trade model to see why absolute productivity did not determine export patterns by itself.
examples.zh: 我们用「李嘉图贸易模型」说明为何仅凭绝对生产率无法决定出口格局。

collocations: derive trade patterns in a Ricardian trade model

words.enDefinition: In a symmetric two-action coordination game, the equilibrium with a strategy that pays more against equal mixing.

examples.en: Both choosing the smaller room formed the risk-dominant equilibrium because that choice paid more against equal mixing.
examples.zh: 双方都选小教室构成「风险占优均衡」，因为当对方以相同概率选择两个选项时，选小教室的期望收益更高。

examples.en: Our tutor checked the risk-dominant equilibrium by assuming the other club was equally likely to choose either option.
examples.zh: 老师假定另一社团选择两个选项的概率各半，据此核查「风险占优均衡」。

collocations: compare a risk-dominant equilibrium with a payoff-dominant one
explain a risk-dominant equilibrium with a matrix

words.enDefinition: Combining potential losses across participants so that individual losses are shared by the group.

examples.en: The model illustrated risk pooling by sharing the cost of unexpected repairs across several participating workshops.
examples.zh: 模型将意外维修成本分摊给几家参加的工场，以说明「风险共担」。

examples.en: Our tutor used risk pooling to explain why average costs could be more predictable than individual costs.
examples.zh: 老师用「风险共担」解释为什么平均成本可能比个人成本更可预测。

words.enDefinition: The property that one person's use reduces the amount or quality available for others.

examples.en: The example showed rivalry in consumption because one person taking a book left fewer for everyone else.
examples.zh: 有人取走一本书，给其他人留下的书就少一本，例题以此展示「消费竞争性」。

examples.en: We discussed how crowding might create rivalry in consumption at an otherwise quiet shared facility.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了拥挤如何在原本清静的共享设施中产生「消费竞争性」。

collocations: compare cases with different rivalry in consumption

words.enDefinition: An analysis that tests whether a substantive conclusion persists under a reasonable change in the method or data.

examples.en: The robustness check uses a different comparison school to see whether the main pattern persists.
examples.zh: 「稳健性检查」使用另一所比较学校，看看主要模式是否仍然存在。

examples.en: We described each robustness check alongside the assumptions it changes in the classroom report.
examples.zh: 我们在课堂报告说明每项「稳健性检查」以及它改变的假设。

words.enDefinition: An approximation that divides 70 by a constant annual growth percentage to estimate the doubling time in years.

examples.en: The rule of 70 puts the doubling time near thirty-five years at two percent annual growth.
examples.zh: 年增长率为百分之二时，用「70 法则」估算出的翻倍时间约为三十五年。

examples.en: We used the rule of 70 to compare approximate doubling times for two constant growth rates.
examples.zh: 我们用「70 法则」比较两个恒定增长率各自对应的大致翻倍时间。

collocations: estimate doubling time using the rule of 70

words.enDefinition: criteria used to determine the country or territory a good is treated as originating from for trade purposes

examples.en: The textbook used rules of origin to explain why the final assembly location did not always determine origin.
examples.zh: 教材用「原产地规则」说明为什么最终装配地点有时无法决定原产地。

examples.en: We compared rules of origin for two model agreements covering goods assembled from parts made in several countries.
examples.zh: 我们比较两个范例协定的「原产地规则」，涉及用多国零件组装的商品。

collocations: apply rules of origin in an example
compare rules of origin across agreements

words.enDefinition: A score or measured quantity whose position relative to a threshold governs treatment assignment or its probability.

examples.en: The running variable is the initial test score used to decide eligibility for simulated tutoring.
examples.zh: 「驱动变量」是决定学生有无模拟辅导资格的初始测试成绩。

examples.en: We plotted the running variable on the horizontal axis of the classroom discontinuity graph.
examples.zh: 我们把「驱动变量」画在课堂断点图的横轴上。

words.enDefinition: movement of people from rural areas to urban areas to live, work or pursue other opportunities

examples.en: The study tracked rural-urban migration after new jobs became available in the nearby town in the example.
examples.zh: 示例中附近城镇出现新岗位后，研究跟踪了「农村向城市迁移」。

examples.en: We compared rural-urban migration with daily commuting when discussing how the survey counted permanent moves.
examples.zh: 讨论调查怎样统计永久性搬迁时，我们把「农村向城市迁移」和日常通勤作了比较。

words.enDefinition: Cumulative output loss associated with lowering inflation by one percentage point

examples.en: We estimated the sacrifice ratio from lost output during a modeled decline in inflation.
examples.zh: 我们根据模型中通胀下降期间的产出损失估算了「牺牲率」。

examples.en: The lecture compared the sacrifice ratio under two assumptions about how quickly expectations adjust.
examples.zh: 课堂在两种不同的预期调整速度假设下，比较了「牺牲率」。

words.enDefinition: Bias that arises when inclusion in the analysed sample depends on factors related to the outcome or its determinants.

examples.en: Sample selection bias may arise when wages are observed only for employed participants in the example.
examples.zh: 示例只观测到在职参与者的工资，这可能产生「样本选择偏误」。

examples.en: We considered sample selection bias before interpreting results from the smaller group with recorded outcomes.
examples.zh: 我们先考虑「样本选择偏误」，再解读有记录结果的较小组得出的结果。

words.enDefinition: A value giving an observation its intended contribution to an estimate, often accounting for unequal selection or response.

examples.en: The sample weight for each fictional worker reflects the survey design used in our exercise.
examples.zh: 每名虚构劳动者的「样本权重」反映了练习中的调查抽样设计。

examples.en: We applied a sample weight before estimating the mean wage from the classroom survey records.
examples.zh: 我们先应用「样本权重」，再根据课堂调查记录估计平均工资。

words.enDefinition: At an interior efficient quantity of a pure public good, the sum of individual marginal benefits equals marginal cost.

examples.en: The tutor used the Samuelson condition to find the efficient amount of lighting in a classroom model.
examples.zh: 老师用「萨缪尔森条件」求课堂模型中的有效照明量。

examples.en: Our worksheet applied the Samuelson condition by comparing combined extra benefits with the cost of another unit.
examples.zh: 练习表把合计额外收益与再增加一个单位的成本比较，应用了「萨缪尔森条件」。

collocations: derive the Samuelson condition for a public good

words.enDefinition: A salient choice that can help players coordinate without direct agreement.

examples.en: The main entrance served as a Schelling point in the classroom example about meeting without messages.
examples.zh: 在不发消息碰面的课堂例题里，正门充当了「谢林焦点」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked why the clock tower might become a Schelling point for both groups.
examples.zh: 老师问，钟楼为什么可能成为两个小组的「谢林焦点」。

collocations: discuss how a Schelling point emerges

words.enDefinition: Actions by a less-informed party to learn about or distinguish types that are privately known.

examples.en: The classroom buyers used screening when they asked a neutral inspector to assess the bicycles.
examples.zh: 课堂模型中的买家请中立检验员评估自行车，借此进行「筛选」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how screening would work if buyers could offer sellers two different contract options.
examples.zh: 老师问，如果买家能给卖家提供两种合同选择，「筛选」会如何发挥作用。

collocations: use screening to learn about quality

words.enDefinition: A test or choice arranged to reveal information about participants whose types are not directly observable.

examples.en: The exercise used a repair record check as a screening device in the modelled bicycle market.
examples.zh: 练习把维修记录核查用作自行车市场模型的一种「筛选机制」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked when a choice between two contracts might work as a screening device.
examples.zh: 老师问，让人从两种合同中选择何时能起到「筛选机制」的作用。

words.enDefinition: An auction in which bidders submit offers without seeing other bids before the bidding deadline.

examples.en: In the sealed-bid auction, students wrote their offers before looking at anyone else's card.
examples.zh: 在「密封出价拍卖」中，学生先写下报价，之后才能看其他人的卡片。

examples.en: The tutor used a sealed-bid auction to compare two different rules for determining payment.
examples.zh: 老师用「密封出价拍卖」比较两种确定付款金额的规则。

collocations: submit an offer in a sealed-bid auction
compare bids in a sealed-bid auction

words.enDefinition: The removal of recurring within-year patterns from a series to make changes easier to compare.

examples.en: Seasonal adjustment helps separate recurring holiday purchases from other movements in quarterly spending in our example.
examples.zh: 「季节调整」有助于区分示例季度支出中反复出现的节日购物和其他变化。

examples.en: We read the notes on seasonal adjustment before interpreting movements between the two adjacent quarters.
examples.zh: 我们先读「季节调整」说明，再解读相邻两个季度之间的变动。

words.enDefinition: Joblessness linked to recurring changes in labor demand during the year

examples.en: The town's seasonal unemployment rises after the summer visitors leave and hotels reduce staffing.
examples.zh: 夏季游客离开、酒店缩减用工后，小镇的「季节性失业」上升了。

examples.en: We discussed seasonal unemployment before comparing tourism employment from January and July.
examples.zh: 比较一月和七月的旅游业就业情况之前，我们讨论了「季节性失业」。

words.enDefinition: Consumer price index adjusted to remove estimated recurring seasonal price movements

examples.en: We read the seasonally adjusted CPI to compare the index with the previous month.
examples.zh: 我们用「季调消费者价格指数」与前一个月作比较。

examples.en: In the table, the seasonally adjusted CPI rose less sharply than the unadjusted measure.
examples.zh: 统计表中的「季调消费者价格指数」涨幅小于未经调整的指标。

collocations: monthly change in seasonally adjusted CPI

words.enDefinition: offering pricing options that vary with quantity or product version so buyers select an option themselves

examples.en: The exercise illustrated second-degree price discrimination using different per-unit prices for small and large bundles.
examples.zh: 练习给大、小组合设定不同的单位价格，以说明「二级价格歧视」。

examples.en: We modelled second-degree price discrimination with a menu that customers could choose from without revealing their preferences directly.
examples.zh: 我们用一组方案模拟「二级价格歧视」，顾客无需直接透露自己的偏好就能选方案。

collocations: compare second-degree price discrimination with group pricing

words.enDefinition: A benefit from acting later, such as being able to respond to the first player's observable choice.

examples.en: The second-mover advantage came from seeing the first group's preference before suggesting another workshop time.
examples.zh: 「后行动者优势」来自先看到第一组的偏好，再提议另一个工作坊时段。

examples.en: The tutor asked whether the second-mover advantage disappeared when the earlier choice was hidden.
examples.zh: 老师问，先前的选择被隐藏时，「后行动者优势」是否消失。

collocations: compare outcomes with a second-mover advantage

words.enDefinition: a single-item auction in which the highest bidder wins and pays the second-highest bid

examples.en: The second-price auction awarded the book to the highest bidder but charged the second-highest offer.
examples.zh: 「第二价格拍卖」把书给出价最高者，但按第二高的报价收费。

examples.en: The tutor used a second-price auction to show why the winning bid need not equal the payment.
examples.zh: 老师用「第二价格拍卖」说明为什么获胜报价不一定等于付款金额。

collocations: record payment in a second-price auction
compare a second-price auction with a first-price one

words.enDefinition: the BPM6 current account category for current transfers between residents and nonresidents

examples.en: The BPM6 secondary income account recorded cross-border household gifts without an associated purchase of goods.
examples.zh: BPM6「二次收入账户」记录跨境家庭赠款，这些款项没有对应的商品购买。

examples.en: We traced a current transfer in the table to the secondary income account of the reporting economy.
examples.zh: 我们将表中的一项经常转移追溯到报告经济体的「二次收入账户」。

collocations: record a transfer in the secondary income account

words.enDefinition: the fraction of total employment accounted for by a specified sector

examples.en: The sectoral employment share of manufacturing rose even though employment in agriculture also increased in absolute terms.
examples.zh: 尽管农业就业人数绝对值也增加，制造业的「部门就业占比」仍然上升。

examples.en: We tracked each sectoral employment share before explaining how the composition of work had changed over time.
examples.zh: 解释工作构成怎样随时间变化前，我们跟踪了各「部门就业占比」。

collocations: report changes in sectoral employment shares

words.enDefinition: The process by which units receive, seek, or choose a treatment, potentially creating systematic group differences.

examples.en: Selection into treatment occurs when the more motivated fictional students are likelier to enrol in tutoring.
examples.zh: 虚构学生中，积极性较高者更可能报名辅导，这体现了「进入处理组的选择」。

examples.en: We described selection into treatment before comparing the groups' scores in the classroom case.
examples.zh: 在课堂案例中，我们先说明「进入处理组的选择」，再比较各组得分。

words.zhGloss: 基于可观测变量的选择
words.enDefinition: The assumption that after conditioning on observed characteristics, treatment assignment is independent of relevant potential outcomes.
acceptedZhAnswers: 基于可观测变量的选择

examples.en: Selection on observables assumes the measured characteristics account for systematic treatment selection in the example.
examples.zh: 在示例中，「基于可观测变量的选择」假设实测特征足以解释处理分配中的系统性选择。

examples.en: We discussed whether selection on observables was plausible given the limited information about prior achievement.
examples.zh: 鉴于掌握的既往成绩信息有限，我们讨论了「基于可观测变量的选择」是否可信。

words.enDefinition: People sorting themselves among options according to preferences or information they privately hold.

examples.en: The model relied on self-selection because participants knew which of the two options suited them better.
examples.zh: 模型依靠「自我选择」，因为参加者知道两个选项哪个更适合自己。

examples.en: We discussed how self-selection could reveal differences that the organiser could not observe directly.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「自我选择」如何揭示组织者无法直接观察到的差异。

words.enDefinition: The part of a tax borne by sellers, measured per unit by the reduction in the price they retain.

examples.en: The seller tax burden reflected the drop in the amount each seller kept per sale.
examples.zh: 「卖方税负」反映了卖家从每笔销售中留存金额的下降。

examples.en: Our tutor found the seller tax burden by comparing the seller's net price with the original price.
examples.zh: 老师比较卖方实收净价与原价，求出了「卖方税负」。

collocations: compare the seller tax burden across markets
identify the seller tax burden on a graph

words.enDefinition: the proportional change in one variable per unit change in another, represented locally by a log-level slope

examples.en: The semi-elasticity links one more year of schooling to an approximate percentage change in fitted wages.
examples.zh: 「半弹性」把受教育年限多一年与拟合工资的近似百分比变化联系起来。

examples.en: We used the semi-elasticity to interpret the schooling term in a model with log wages.
examples.zh: 我们用「半弹性」解读对数工资模型里的受教育程度项。

words.enDefinition: An equilibrium in which different types choose distinguishable actions that reveal information about them.

examples.en: The model showed a separating equilibrium because higher and lower quality sellers chose different offers.
examples.zh: 质量较高和较低的卖家给出不同报价，因此模型显示「分离均衡」。

examples.en: Our worksheet asked which choices buyers could observe in the proposed separating equilibrium for used bicycles.
examples.zh: 练习表问，在假设的二手自行车「分离均衡」下，买家可以观察到哪些选择。

words.enDefinition: a sequentially rational assessment consistent with a limit of completely mixed strategy profiles and the corresponding Bayesian beliefs

examples.en: Our tutor illustrated sequential equilibrium by considering small positive probabilities for all available moves.
examples.zh: 老师通过给所有可选行动考虑很小的正概率来说明「序贯均衡」。

examples.en: The worksheet checked which beliefs could arise in the limit before confirming the sequential equilibrium.
examples.zh: 练习表先核查哪些信念能在取极限时出现，再确认「序贯均衡」。

collocations: test beliefs for consistency in a sequential equilibrium

words.enDefinition: A game where players make their decisions in an ordered sequence.

examples.en: The booking model became a sequential-move game once the clubs were assigned different decision times.
examples.zh: 给各社团安排不同的决策时间后，预订模型变为「序贯行动博弈」。

examples.en: We traced the moves in the sequential-move game before deciding which plans the players would use.
examples.zh: 判断各参与者将采用哪些计划之前，我们先追踪了「序贯行动博弈」中的行动。

words.enDefinition: Optimality of a player's plan from each information set onward, given its beliefs and the other players' strategies.

examples.en: Our tutor checked sequential rationality even at decisions the proposed strategies would never reach.
examples.zh: 即使某些决策点按拟议策略永远不会到达，老师也核查了「序贯理性」。

examples.en: The worksheet asked whether the later response satisfied sequential rationality under the beliefs shown.
examples.zh: 练习表问，在所示信念下，后期回应是否满足「序贯理性」。

collocations: check sequential rationality at each information set

words.enDefinition: Dependence between a unit's disturbances across periods in a model with a time dimension.

examples.en: Serial correlation in errors occurs when a school's unmeasured attendance shocks persist across years in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中，一所学校未测量的出勤冲击跨年持续时，就存在「误差的序列相关」。

examples.en: The tutor discussed serial correlation in errors before explaining why the original uncertainty estimates might be too small.
examples.zh: 老师先讲「误差的序列相关」，再解释原来的不确定性估计为何可能过小。

collocations: allow for serial correlation in errors
serial correlation in errors over time

words.enDefinition: A discontinuity in a statistical series caused by a change in how the measure is defined or produced.

examples.en: The series break marks the year when the statistical office changed its industry coverage.
examples.zh: 「序列断点」标出统计机构改变行业统计覆盖范围的年份。

examples.en: The chart uses a dotted line to indicate the series break between the two estimates.
examples.zh: 图表用点线标明两组估计之间的「序列断点」。

words.enDefinition: Rate of price increase for services in the price measure

examples.en: We tracked services inflation separately to see how rents and restaurant prices changed.
examples.zh: 我们单独追踪「服务通胀」，以了解房租和餐厅价格如何变动。

examples.en: The briefing showed services inflation remaining positive even when prices for many goods fell.
examples.zh: 简报显示，即使许多商品的价格下跌，「服务通胀」仍为正。

words.enDefinition: The influence of expected future interactions on a player's willingness to cooperate now.

examples.en: The tutor introduced the shadow of the future when the same teams expected to meet again.
examples.zh: 原来的队伍预计还会继续碰面时，老师介绍了「未来的影子」。

examples.en: We discussed whether the shadow of the future changed how the clubs shared the studio today.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「未来的影子」是否改变了各社团当天共用工作室的做法。

collocations: explain the shadow of the future
discuss the shadow of the future
a longer shadow of the future

words.enDefinition: A discontinuity design in which treatment status changes deterministically across the assignment cutoff.

examples.en: Sharp regression discontinuity applies in the example because every eligible student receives tutoring and nobody else does.
examples.zh: 示例适合「精确断点回归」，因为每名符合资格的学生都接受辅导，其余学生均不参加。

examples.en: We started with sharp regression discontinuity before studying a less strictly enforced eligibility rule in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们先学习「精确断点回归」，再看执行较灵活的资格规则。

words.enDefinition: A change in the amount supplied at each price level due to a change in production conditions.

examples.en: The diagram shows a leftward shift in short-run aggregate supply after input costs rise unexpectedly.
examples.zh: 投入成本意外上升后，图中「短期总供给曲线移动」的方向是向左。

examples.en: We labelled the shift in short-run aggregate supply before reading the new output and price levels.
examples.zh: 我们在图上标明「短期总供给曲线移动」后，再读新的产出和价格水平。

collocations: leftward shift in short-run aggregate supply
rightward shift in short-run aggregate supply
illustrate a shift in short-run aggregate supply

words.enDefinition: Total output supplied at different price levels while some wages or other input prices adjust gradually.

examples.en: Short-run aggregate supply slopes upward under the stated assumptions in our classroom model of output.
examples.zh: 在给定假设下，课堂产出模型中的「短期总供给」曲线向上倾斜。

examples.en: We shifted short-run aggregate supply left in the diagram after raising production costs in the example.
examples.zh: 提高示例中的生产成本后，我们把图中的「短期总供给」曲线向左移动。

words.enDefinition: a graph of average cost at different output levels when at least one input is fixed

examples.en: The short-run average cost curve used one workshop size while the number of completed orders could vary.
examples.zh: 「短期平均成本曲线」假定车间规模固定，而完工订单数量可以变化。

examples.en: We drew another short-run average cost curve for the larger building shown in the practice exercise.
examples.zh: 我们为练习里较大的楼宇另画了一条「短期平均成本曲线」。

collocations: draw a short-run average cost curve
read a short-run average cost curve
compare short-run average cost curves for two plants

words.enDefinition: Proportional responsiveness measured over a period that limits time for adjustment

examples.en: The case compares short-run elasticity for bus trips among students with different commute options.
examples.zh: 案例比较了拥有不同通勤选择的学生对公交出行的「短期弹性」。

examples.en: In our example, the short-run elasticity is small because buyers cannot easily change plans this week.
examples.zh: 在我们的例子中，「短期弹性」较小，因为买家这周不容易改变计划。

words.enDefinition: The combination of output and price level where aggregate demand equals short-run aggregate supply.

examples.en: Short-run macroeconomic equilibrium occurs where the two curves cross in the classroom output diagram.
examples.zh: 课堂产出图上，两条曲线相交处达到「短期宏观经济均衡」。

examples.en: We marked the new short-run macroeconomic equilibrium after moving the demand curve in the example.
examples.zh: 我们移动了示例中的需求曲线后，标出新的「短期宏观经济均衡」。

words.enDefinition: a graph of the extra cost of producing additional output when at least one input is fixed

examples.en: The short-run marginal cost curve rose after extra orders required increasingly expensive overtime at the same workshop.
examples.zh: 同一车间接到额外订单后必须付出越来越高的加班成本，「短期边际成本曲线」随之上升。

examples.en: We read the short-run marginal cost curve to find the cost of producing the next finished item.
examples.zh: 我们读取「短期边际成本曲线」，找出再生产一件成品的成本。

collocations: draw a short-run marginal cost curve
read a short-run marginal cost curve
derive the short-run marginal cost curve from total cost

words.enDefinition: a model relation between inflation and unemployment or other slack measures with expectations and supply conditions held fixed

examples.en: We moved along the short-run Phillips curve while keeping expectations and supply conditions fixed.
examples.zh: 我们保持预期和供给条件不变，沿「短期菲利普斯曲线」移动。

examples.en: The diagram shifts the short-run Phillips curve upward after workers expect faster price increases.
examples.zh: 当劳动者预期价格上涨更快时，示意图中的「短期菲利普斯曲线」向上移动。

collocations: movement along the short-run Phillips curve

words.enDefinition: a relationship between variable inputs and feasible output when at least one other input is fixed

examples.en: The short-run production function showed how extra workers affected output while the number of machines stayed fixed.
examples.zh: 「短期生产函数」显示机器台数固定时，增加工人怎样影响产量。

examples.en: We drew the short-run production function after selecting a particular workshop size for the first part.
examples.zh: 为第一部分选定一个车间规模后，我们画出了「短期生产函数」。

words.enDefinition: the decision to stop current production when revenue cannot cover avoidable operating costs, given fixed commitments

examples.en: The short-run shutdown rule explained why the example's shop could keep producing despite reporting an overall loss.
examples.zh: 「短期停产规则」解释了为什么示例中的商店即使整体亏损也可能继续生产。

examples.en: We applied the short-run shutdown rule by comparing the revenue from opening with the costs it could avoid.
examples.zh: 我们比较营业所得收入和可以避免的成本，以应用「短期停产规则」。

collocations: compare the short-run shutdown rule with long-run exit

words.enDefinition: a graph of quantities supplied at different prices when some inputs and the set of producers are held fixed

examples.en: The short-run supply curve showed output adjustments while the number of firms and their plant sizes stayed fixed.
examples.zh: 「短期供给曲线」显示厂商数量和工厂规模固定时的产量调整。

examples.en: We drew a short-run supply curve before allowing entry of new producers in the next part of class.
examples.zh: 我们先画「短期供给曲线」，到下一部分课程再允许新生产者进入。

collocations: read a price from a short-run supply curve

words.enDefinition: a graph of total production cost for different output levels in a period when some input is fixed

examples.en: The short-run total cost curve started above zero because the workshop still paid rent without producing anything.
examples.zh: 车间没有产出时仍要付房租，所以「短期总成本曲线」从零以上起步。

examples.en: We compared two points on the short-run total cost curve to calculate the cost of increased production.
examples.zh: 我们比较「短期总成本曲线」上的两点，计算增产所需的成本。

collocations: plot a short-run total cost curve
measure the slope of the short-run total cost curve

words.enDefinition: in a standard competitive short-run model, the price below which producing cannot cover avoidable variable costs

examples.en: The sample firm's shutdown price corresponded to the minimum of its average variable cost curve in class.
examples.zh: 课堂中，示例厂商的「停产价格」对应其平均变动成本曲线的最低点。

examples.en: We marked the shutdown price below the break-even level because rent had to be paid either way.
examples.zh: 无论生产与否都要付租金，因此我们把「停产价格」标在盈亏平衡价格下方。

collocations: compare prices with the shutdown price

words.enDefinition: Observable actions by a better-informed party that convey information to a less-informed party.

examples.en: The used goods exercise modelled signaling when sellers provided verified inspection reports about their products.
examples.zh: 二手商品练习将卖家提供经核实的检验报告作为「信号传递」来建模。

examples.en: Our tutor distinguished signaling by sellers from screening initiated by buyers in the classroom case.
examples.zh: 老师区分了课堂案例中卖家进行的「信号传递」和买家发起的筛选。

words.enDefinition: Bias that arises when variables jointly determine each other, making a regressor correlated with the disturbance.

examples.en: The example shows simultaneity bias when firms and workers jointly determine both wages and hours.
examples.zh: 示例中，企业和劳动者共同决定工资和工时，从而出现「联立性偏误」。

examples.en: We distinguished simultaneity bias from a case in which an important background variable was simply omitted.
examples.zh: 我们把「联立性偏误」与单纯遗漏一个重要背景变量的情况区分开。

words.enDefinition: A game in which players make the relevant choices without observing one another's current moves beforehand.

examples.en: The simultaneous-move game required each team to submit its preferred time without seeing the other submission.
examples.zh: 「同时行动博弈」要求各队在看不到对方提交内容时提交自己偏好的时段。

examples.en: Our tutor compared a simultaneous-move game with a version where the second club could observe the first.
examples.zh: 老师把「同时行动博弈」与第二个社团能观察第一个社团选择的版本作了比较。

words.enDefinition: Changes in two or more modeled curves or schedules at once

examples.en: We drew simultaneous shifts to show both a bumper harvest and an increase in demand.
examples.zh: 我们画出两条曲线「同时移动」，反映收成增加和需求上升。

examples.en: The question about simultaneous shifts asks why we cannot determine the change in market price.
examples.zh: 关于曲线「同时移动」的题目问，为什么我们无法确定市场价格的变化方向。

collocations: simultaneous shifts in supply and demand

words.enDefinition: Rate of change in affordable quantities between goods along the spending boundary

examples.en: The slope of the budget line equals the negative price ratio in our two-good model.
examples.zh: 在我们的两种商品模型中，「预算线斜率」等于价格比的相反数。

examples.en: We recalculated the slope of the budget line when only the price of lunches rose.
examples.zh: 只有午餐价格上涨时，我们重新计算了「预算线斜率」。

collocations: calculate the slope of the budget line
change the slope of the budget line
interpret the slope of the budget line

words.enDefinition: Formula splitting a demand response into substitution and purchasing power effects

examples.en: The lecture applied the Slutsky equation to separate two reasons coffee purchases might change.
examples.zh: 课堂上老师用「斯勒茨基方程」把咖啡购买量可能变化的两个原因分开。

examples.en: We used the Slutsky equation to express the total response to a price change.
examples.zh: 我们用「斯勒茨基方程」表示需求对价格变化的总反应。

collocations: decompose changes using the Slutsky equation

words.enDefinition: an economy open to international transactions and treated as too small to affect relevant world prices in the model

examples.en: The lesson treated the region as a small open economy that took the outside price as given.
examples.zh: 课堂把该地区视为接受外部市场价格的「小型开放经济体」。

examples.en: We assumed a small open economy before analysing how an import tax would affect local purchases.
examples.zh: 分析进口税怎样影响当地购买量前，我们采用了「小型开放经济体」假设。

collocations: assume the country is a small open economy

words.enDefinition: Comparing the benefits and costs of an action for society, including effects outside the immediate transaction.

examples.en: The class used social cost-benefit analysis to compare a quieter delivery schedule with the original one.
examples.zh: 全班用「社会成本收益分析」比较降噪后的配送时段与原来的安排。

examples.en: Our tutor included effects on nearby residents in the social cost-benefit analysis of the classroom proposal.
examples.zh: 老师在课堂方案的「社会成本收益分析」中计入了对附近居民的影响。

collocations: document assumptions in a social cost-benefit analysis

words.enDefinition: The emissions level that balances marginal damage and marginal abatement cost at an interior social optimum.

examples.en: We located the socially efficient emissions level where the marginal damage and marginal abatement cost curves met.
examples.zh: 我们在边际损害曲线和边际减排成本曲线相交处找到「社会有效排放水平」。

examples.en: The tutor asked why the socially efficient emissions level in the example was greater than zero.
examples.zh: 老师问，例题中的「社会有效排放水平」为什么大于零。

collocations: calculate the socially efficient emissions level
locate the socially efficient emissions level
compare actual emissions with the socially efficient emissions level

words.enDefinition: The quantity that maximizes net social benefits, where marginal social benefit equals marginal social cost at an interior optimum.

examples.en: We found the socially efficient quantity where marginal social benefit and marginal social cost crossed.
examples.zh: 我们在边际社会收益和边际社会成本相交处找到「社会有效数量」。

examples.en: The market produced more than the socially efficient quantity after ignoring the cost of nearby noise.
examples.zh: 市场忽略了给周边造成的噪声成本，产量因此超过「社会有效数量」。

collocations: compare market output with the socially efficient quantity

words.enDefinition: A model in which saving, population growth, and technology help explain capital and output over time.

examples.en: The Solow growth model links investment and depreciation to the capital stock in our lesson.
examples.zh: 课堂上，「索洛增长模型」把投资和折旧与资本存量联系起来。

examples.en: We traced the effects of a higher saving rate in the simple Solow growth model.
examples.zh: 我们观察了简单「索洛增长模型」中储蓄率上升的影响。

collocations: steady state of the Solow growth model

words.enDefinition: The portion of measured output growth left after subtracting growth contributions attributed to capital and labour.

examples.en: The Solow residual remains positive after the measured capital and labour contributions are subtracted in class.
examples.zh: 课堂示例中，扣除测得的资本和劳动贡献后，「索洛余值」仍为正。

examples.en: The tutor explained that the Solow residual can include changes beyond technical improvement alone.
examples.zh: 老师解释说，「索洛余值」反映的变化可能不限于技术进步。

words.zhGloss: 阈值附近的选择性分布
words.enDefinition: Nonrandom placement of units on either side of a cutoff, for example through influence over the running variable.
acceptedZhAnswers: 阈值附近的选择性分布

examples.en: The class discussed whether sorting around the cutoff could make the two groups systematically different.
examples.zh: 全班讨论「阈值附近的选择性分布」会不会让两组存在系统差异。

examples.en: The worksheet asks what patterns might suggest sorting around the cutoff in the simulated records.
examples.zh: 练习要求判断模拟记录中的哪些模式可能提示「阈值附近的选择性分布」。

collocations: signs of sorting around the cutoff

words.enDefinition: a trade model with some production factors tied to particular industries while others can move between industries

examples.en: The specific-factors model kept machinery in its original industry while allowing labour to move between sectors.
examples.zh: 「特定要素模型」把机器留在原行业，同时允许劳动者在部门之间流动。

examples.en: The tutor used the specific-factors model to discuss the short-run distribution of gains after export prices rose.
examples.zh: 出口价格上涨后，导师用「特定要素模型」讨论短期收益如何分配。

collocations: analyse factor returns in the specific-factors model

words.enDefinition: A mismatch between the chosen model and the relationship or data-generating process it is meant to represent.

examples.en: The specification error arises because the classroom model assumes a straight relationship for data generated from a curve.
examples.zh: 课堂模型假定关系是直线，但生成数据的关系是曲线，因此产生了「模型设定错误」。

examples.en: We discussed whether excluding the needed interaction represented a specification error in the wage exercise.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了在工资练习里，省略必要的交互项是否属于「模型设定错误」。

words.enDefinition: Policy aimed at limiting large fluctuations in activity, employment, or inflation

examples.en: Our class compared two approaches to stabilization policy after demand fell in the model.
examples.zh: 总需求在模型中下降后，全班比较了两种「稳定政策」的做法。

examples.en: The chapter discusses stabilization policy when inflation rises even as employment falls in the model.
examples.zh: 该章节讨论了模型中就业下滑而通胀上升时的「稳定政策」。

words.enDefinition: an oligopoly model in which a leader commits to a quantity and a follower then chooses its own quantity

examples.en: The Stackelberg model allowed the first producer to commit to output before the second producer chose its output.
examples.zh: 「斯塔克尔伯格模型」允许第一家生产者先承诺产量，第二家随后决定自己的产量。

examples.en: We solved the Stackelberg model by first finding how the follower would respond to each possible leader quantity.
examples.zh: 我们先求出跟随者对领导者各可能产量的回应，再求解「斯塔克尔伯格模型」。

collocations: identify the leader in a Stackelberg model
compare quantities under the Stackelberg model

words.enDefinition: The underlying one-period game whose choices and payoffs recur in a repeated game.

examples.en: The stage game gave each team two ways to contribute to maintaining the shared study space.
examples.zh: 「阶段博弈」给各队两种为维护共享自习空间作贡献的方式。

examples.en: Our tutor drew the stage game before discussing what changed when the same interaction was repeated.
examples.zh: 老师先画出「阶段博弈」，再讨论同样互动重复进行时会发生什么变化。

words.enDefinition: Combination of high inflation and weak or stagnant economic activity

examples.en: The model produced stagflation after a supply shock raised prices and lowered output.
examples.zh: 一次供给冲击使价格上升、产出下降后，模型出现了「滞胀」。

examples.en: We discussed stagflation when the case showed rising inflation alongside stagnant production.
examples.zh: 案例显示通胀加剧与生产停滞并存时，我们讨论了「滞胀」。

words.enDefinition: The introduction of treatment at different times for different units or groups in the same study.

examples.en: Staggered adoption occurs because the fictional schools start tutoring in three different years in the example.
examples.zh: 示例中的虚构学校在三个不同年度启动辅导，因此属于「分期实施」。

examples.en: We drew a timeline to show how staggered adoption affects who remains available for comparison.
examples.zh: 我们画了一条时间线，说明「分期实施」会如何影响仍可用作比较的学校。

words.enDefinition: in national accounts, the balancing difference between separately estimated measures of an amount that should agree in principle

examples.en: The statistical discrepancy accounts for the gap between the two independently estimated GDP totals in class.
examples.zh: 课堂示例用「统计差异项」列示两种独立估计的 GDP 总额之间的差额。

examples.en: We located the statistical discrepancy below the expenditure and income figures in the national accounts table.
examples.zh: 我们在国民账户表的支出和收入数据下方找到了「统计差异项」。

words.enDefinition: The assignment of the legal responsibility for a tax to a particular party.

examples.en: The worksheet assigned statutory incidence to sellers even though buyers bore part of the economic burden.
examples.zh: 虽然买方也承担部分经济负担，练习表仍把「法定税负归属」指定在卖方一侧。

examples.en: We changed the statutory incidence in the classroom model before comparing the resulting prices.
examples.zh: 我们先改变课堂模型中的「法定税负归属」，再比较变动后的价格。

collocations: compare statutory incidence with economic incidence
change the statutory incidence of a tax

words.enDefinition: The level of capital per worker that remains constant in a simplified growth model's steady state.

examples.en: Investment covers depreciation and capital dilution at steady-state capital per worker in the example model.
examples.zh: 在示例模型的「稳态每名工人资本」水平，投资正好弥补折旧和资本稀释。

examples.en: The class marked steady-state capital per worker where the two curves crossed on the diagram.
examples.zh: 全班在图中两条曲线的交点标出了「稳态每名工人资本」。

collocations: change in steady-state capital per worker

words.zhGloss: 斯托尔珀萨缪尔森定理
words.enDefinition: under a standard two-good two-factor model, a rise in a good's relative price raises the real return to its relatively intensive factor and lowers the other factor's return
acceptedZhAnswers: 斯托尔珀萨缪尔森定理

examples.en: The Stolper-Samuelson theorem linked a higher cloth price to changes in both real factor returns in our example.
examples.zh: 「斯托尔珀萨缪尔森定理」把示例中更高的布料价格与两种要素实际回报的变化联系起来。

examples.en: We checked the model assumptions before using the Stolper-Samuelson theorem to interpret a changed relative price.
examples.zh: 用「斯托尔珀萨缪尔森定理」解释相对价格变化前，我们核对了模型假设。

words.enDefinition: A game represented by its players, strategies and payoffs for each strategy profile.

examples.en: We represented the booking exercise as a strategic-form game with two strategies for each club.
examples.zh: 我们把预订练习表示为「战略式博弈」，每个社团有两种策略。

examples.en: The tutor asked which information a strategic-form game retained when we stopped drawing the move sequence.
examples.zh: 老师问，不再绘制行动顺序后，「战略式博弈」保留了什么信息。

collocations: write a strategic-form game as a table

words.enDefinition: the dependence of each firm's outcome on its own choices and the choices made by rivals

examples.en: The firms showed strategic interdependence because the profit from increasing output changed when competitors expanded too.
examples.zh: 厂商增产的利润取决于对手是否也扩产，体现了「战略相互依赖」。

examples.en: We represented strategic interdependence in a table showing how different pairs of output choices affected both producers.
examples.zh: 我们用一张表列出不同的两家产量组合如何影响各方，以表示「战略相互依赖」。

words.enDefinition: An experimental method eliciting choices for several possible situations before participants learn which situation occurs.

examples.en: Using the strategy method, we asked each participant how they would respond to every possible offer.
examples.zh: 使用「策略法」时，我们询问各参与者会怎样回应每种可能的提议。

examples.en: The tutor used the strategy method to collect choices for situations that did not actually occur.
examples.zh: 老师用「策略法」收集了参与者对于未实际发生情形的选择。

collocations: compare the strategy method with direct responses
collect choices using the strategy method

words.enDefinition: A specification of one strategy for every player in a game.

examples.en: The model evaluated a strategy profile after both groups had chosen plans for every possible situation.
examples.zh: 两个小组都为各种可能情况选好应对计划后，模型评估了一个「策略组合」。

examples.en: We changed one plan within the strategy profile and left the other group's plan unchanged.
examples.zh: 我们改变了「策略组合」中的一个计划，另一组的计划仍保持原样。

collocations: check whether a strategy profile is an equilibrium

words.enDefinition: The collection of complete plans a player is allowed to use in a game.

examples.en: Our worksheet listed each player's strategy set before constructing the table of possible payoffs.
examples.zh: 练习表在构建可能收益表之前，列出了每位参与者的「策略集合」。

examples.en: The strategy set grew when we added another possible response to the shared booking game.
examples.zh: 我们给共同预订博弈增添一种可能应对之后，「策略集合」变大了。

words.enDefinition: A strategy giving a higher payoff than each alternative for every strategy choice of the other players.

examples.en: Tuesday was a strictly dominant strategy because it gave the first club more points in every case.
examples.zh: 周二是「严格占优策略」，因为在每种情况下它都给第一个社团更多积分。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether either player had a strictly dominant strategy in the room-sharing exercise.
examples.zh: 老师问，在共用教室的练习里，有没有参与者存在「严格占优策略」。

collocations: check for a strictly dominant strategy

words.enDefinition: A strategy that yields a lower payoff than a particular alternative against every choice of the other players.

examples.en: We crossed out a strictly dominated strategy after finding another plan with higher payoffs in every column.
examples.zh: 发现另一个方案在每一列的收益都更高后，我们划掉了一个「被严格支配的策略」。

examples.en: The tutor asked why a strictly dominated strategy was never a best response in the example.
examples.zh: 老师问，为什么例题中「被严格支配的策略」从来不是最佳反应。

collocations: compare a strictly dominated strategy with its alternative

words.enDefinition: long-run reallocation of activity and workers across sectors of an economy as it develops

examples.en: The report traced structural transformation as employment shifted from agriculture toward manufacturing and services over several decades.
examples.zh: 报告跟踪了「结构转型」，期间就业在几十年里从农业转向制造业和服务业。

examples.en: We compared structural transformation across regions where new industries absorbed very different shares of the workforce.
examples.zh: 我们比较不同地区的「结构转型」，这些地区新行业吸收的劳动力比例差别很大。

collocations: study a period of structural transformation

words.enDefinition: Unemployment linked to a mismatch between workers and available jobs

examples.en: The exercise illustrates structural unemployment when vacancies require qualifications that local jobseekers lack.
examples.zh: 习题用空缺岗位要求本地求职者不具备的资质，说明「结构性失业」。

examples.en: Our group compared structural unemployment caused by a geographic mismatch with temporary search delays.
examples.zh: 小组比较了地域错配造成的「结构性失业」与暂时的求职延迟。

words.enDefinition: A game starting at a singleton information set, containing all successors without cutting through any information set.

examples.en: We checked whether the subgame included every possible response after the first club made its selection.
examples.zh: 第一个社团选定后，我们检查了「子博弈」是否涵盖随后的每种可能回应。

examples.en: The tutor asked why cutting the linked decision points would prevent that branch from being a subgame.
examples.zh: 老师问，为什么切开相连的决策点会使该分支无法构成「子博弈」。

collocations: check whether a branch begins a subgame

words.enDefinition: A strategy profile that forms a Nash equilibrium in every subgame, including the whole game.

examples.en: We tested a subgame-perfect equilibrium by checking the proposed plans after both possible first moves.
examples.zh: 我们检查了两种可能开局之后的拟议计划，以检验「子博弈完美均衡」。

examples.en: The tutor rejected one candidate for a subgame-perfect equilibrium because its later response was not optimal.
examples.zh: 老师否决了一个「子博弈完美均衡」候选方案，因为它在后期的回应不是最优。

collocations: derive a subgame-perfect equilibrium by backward induction

words.enDefinition: The amount the public authority pays to fund a subsidy in the scenario being studied.

examples.en: We found the subsidy cost by multiplying the payment per unit by the quantity receiving it.
examples.zh: 我们把单位补贴额乘以获得补贴的数量，求出了「补贴财政支出」。

examples.en: Our tutor compared subsidy cost with changes in social benefits and other costs in the classroom model.
examples.zh: 老师将「补贴财政支出」与课堂模型中社会收益和其他成本的变化作了比较。

collocations: estimate the subsidy cost at the new quantity

words.enDefinition: The division of the economic benefits of a subsidy across the groups it affects.

examples.en: The worksheet used subsidy incidence to show how buyers and sellers could both gain from the payment.
examples.zh: 练习表用「补贴归宿」展示买卖双方怎样都可能从这笔款项中受益。

examples.en: Our tutor analysed subsidy incidence after calculating changes in buyer and seller prices under the policy.
examples.zh: 老师计算了政策下买方和卖方价格的变动，再分析「补贴归宿」。

collocations: explain subsidy incidence with a diagram

words.enDefinition: Product whose demand rises when a similar alternative becomes more expensive

examples.en: In the example, oat milk is a substitute good when dairy milk becomes more expensive.
examples.zh: 在这个例子中，牛奶涨价时，燕麦奶是一种「替代品」。

examples.en: Our survey treated bus travel as a substitute good for taking the campus train.
examples.zh: 我们的调查把乘公交车视为乘校园列车的一种「替代品」。

words.enDefinition: Index distortion arising when weights miss shifts toward relatively cheaper purchases

examples.en: We discussed substitution bias after households switched from expensive pears to relatively cheaper apples.
examples.zh: 家庭消费者从较贵的梨转向相对便宜的苹果后，我们讨论了「替代偏差」。

examples.en: The fixed basket can create substitution bias when shoppers adjust what they purchase after prices change.
examples.zh: 价格变动后，购物者会调整所买商品，固定篮子可能因此产生「替代偏差」。

words.enDefinition: Demand change attributable to relative prices with purchasing power effects removed

examples.en: The example isolates the substitution effect by keeping the household on the same indifference curve.
examples.zh: 示例让家庭保持在同一条无差异曲线上，以单独分析「替代效应」。

examples.en: The substitution effect shifts purchases toward tea when it becomes cheaper relative to coffee.
examples.zh: 茶相对于咖啡变便宜时，「替代效应」使购买转向茶。

collocations: substitution effect of a price change

words.enDefinition: an expense required to enter a market that a firm cannot recover if it later leaves

examples.en: The exercise treated the custom installation as a sunk entry cost because no other producer could reuse it.
examples.zh: 由于没有其他生产者能重复利用定制装置，练习将其视为「无法收回的进入成本」。

examples.en: We compared the sunk entry cost with a lease payment that could be avoided by leaving the market.
examples.zh: 我们将「无法收回的进入成本」与退出市场后可以免去的租赁付款作了比较。

collocations: compare markets by sunk entry cost

words.enDefinition: Graph showing amounts buyers and sellers plan to trade at different prices

examples.en: I used a supply and demand diagram to show why the two sides planned different amounts.
examples.zh: 我用「供需图」说明买卖双方为什么计划交易不同的数量。

examples.en: The homework asks for a supply and demand diagram with both curves and their intersection marked.
examples.zh: 作业要求画一幅「供需图」，并标出两条曲线及其交点。

collocations: draw a supply and demand diagram
interpret a supply and demand diagram
label a supply and demand diagram

words.enDefinition: A national accounts table that reconciles the supply of products with how they are used.

examples.en: The supply and use table tracks how much flour came from local producers or imports.
examples.zh: 「供给使用表」记录面粉有多少来自本地生产，又有多少来自进口。

examples.en: We used the supply and use table to balance sales with final and intermediate uses.
examples.zh: 我们用「供给使用表」，将销售与最终用途和中间用途进行平衡核对。

collocations: compile a supply and use table
balance a supply and use table
national accounts supply and use table

words.enDefinition: a graph showing the quantity sellers are willing and able to offer at each possible price, holding other influences fixed

examples.en: Each point on the supply curve shows the amount sellers offer at one price.
examples.zh: 「供给曲线」上的每个点都显示卖家在某个价格下愿意出售的数量。

examples.en: We plotted the supply curve from a table showing bakery output at different prices.
examples.zh: 我们根据列出各个价格对应面包店产量的表格绘制了「供给曲线」。

words.enDefinition: a change in the quantity producers offer when a price, cost or other factor changes

examples.en: The supply response was small at first because the stores could not add workers immediately in the example.
examples.zh: 示例中的商店不能立即增聘人手，所以最初的「供给响应」较小。

examples.en: We compared the supply response before and after firms had time to adjust their plant sizes.
examples.zh: 在厂商有时间调整工厂规模前后，我们比较了「供给响应」。

collocations: allow for a delayed supply response

words.enDefinition: Table pairing possible prices with amounts sellers would offer at each

examples.en: Use the supply schedule to plot three points for the campus bike rental market.
examples.zh: 用「供给表」在校内自行车租赁市场的图上标出三个点。

examples.en: Our supply schedule shows how many trays the bakery would offer at different prices.
examples.zh: 我们的「供给表」展示了面包店在不同价格下各愿意出售多少托盘的产品。

words.enDefinition: Factor besides the good's own price that changes sales offered at given prices

examples.en: The students identified cheaper paper as a supply shifter for locally printed notebooks.
examples.zh: 学生们指出，纸张变便宜是本地印制笔记本的「供给曲线移动因素」。

examples.en: Our worksheet treats a larger number of sellers as a supply shifter for the market.
examples.zh: 习题把卖家数量增加视为该市场的「供给曲线移动因素」。

words.enDefinition: Sudden change in the amounts sellers offer at existing prices

examples.en: A flood caused a negative supply shock by closing several local farms in the model.
examples.zh: 在模型中，洪水使当地几家农场停产，造成了负向「供给冲击」。

examples.en: The seminar uses a positive supply shock to explain why the curve moves right.
examples.zh: 研讨课以正向「供给冲击」解释了为什么曲线会向右移。

collocations: respond to a positive supply shock

words.enDefinition: The set of pure strategies assigned strictly positive probability by a mixed strategy.

examples.en: The support of a mixed strategy included both times but excluded the room that was never selected.
examples.zh: 「混合策略的支撑集」包括两个时段，但不包括从未被选中的教室选项。

examples.en: Our tutor listed the support of a mixed strategy after calculating the probabilities in the example.
examples.zh: 老师算出例题中的概率后，列出了「混合策略的支撑集」。

collocations: identify the support of a mixed strategy
find strategies outside the support of a mixed strategy
check the support of a mixed strategy

words.enDefinition: A coherent framework for measuring economic activity and how income and wealth circulate within an economy.

examples.en: The system of national accounts connects the figures for production, income, and spending in our lesson.
examples.zh: 「国民账户体系」将课堂上的生产、收入和支出数据联系起来。

examples.en: We used the system of national accounts to compare the coverage of two fictional economies.
examples.zh: 我们用「国民账户体系」比较两个虚构经济体的统计覆盖范围。

collocations: apply the system of national accounts

words.zhGloss: 只能接受或拒绝的提议
words.enDefinition: An offer the recipient can accept or reject without proposing a counteroffer within the game.
acceptedZhAnswers: 只能接受或拒绝的提议

examples.en: The worksheet gave the second club a take-it-or-leave-it offer for one hour of studio time.
examples.zh: 练习表给第二个社团一项「只能接受或拒绝的提议」，内容是一小时的工作室使用时间。

examples.en: The tutor asked when the responder would accept a take-it-or-leave-it offer in the classroom example.
examples.zh: 老师问，课堂例题中的回应者在什么情况下会接受这项「只能接受或拒绝的提议」。

words.enDefinition: Equality of the preference curve slope and budget line slope at contact

examples.en: We used the tangency condition where the smooth indifference curve touched the budget line.
examples.zh: 光滑的无差异曲线与预算线相切时，我们使用了「相切条件」。

examples.en: The lecturer showed why the tangency condition may fail at an optimum on an axis.
examples.zh: 老师说明了最优点在坐标轴上时「相切条件」为何可能不成立。

words.enDefinition: a mismatch between who actually receives a programme and who is intended to receive it

examples.en: The evaluation measured targeting error after comparing the beneficiary list with the programme's stated eligibility rules.
examples.zh: 评估将受益者名单与项目公示的资格规则比较后，衡量了「救助对象识别偏差」。

examples.en: We discussed how incomplete survey coverage might contribute to targeting error in the experimental programme.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了调查覆盖不全为何可能导致实验项目出现「救助对象识别偏差」。

words.enDefinition: a tariff pattern in which more processed products face higher rates than less processed inputs

examples.en: The worksheet illustrated tariff escalation by showing higher rates for finished clothing than for unprocessed cotton.
examples.zh: 练习表用成衣税率高于未加工棉花的例子说明「关税升级结构」。

examples.en: We looked for tariff escalation along the processing stages in the example involving fruit and juice.
examples.zh: 我们查看水果和果汁的例子在各加工阶段是否存在「关税升级结构」。

collocations: analyse the effects of tariff escalation

words.enDefinition: a system applying a lower tariff up to a specified import quantity and a higher rate above it

examples.en: The tariff-rate quota applied a lower duty to imports admitted within the specified volume.
examples.zh: 「关税配额」对获准进入规定数量额度的进口品适用较低关税。

examples.en: We compared the two rates under the tariff-rate quota before interpreting the cost figures in the example.
examples.zh: 我们先对比「关税配额」的两种税率，再解读示例中的成本数据。

collocations: calculate duty under a tariff-rate quota
report imports within a tariff-rate quota

words.enDefinition: government revenue collected from taxes on goods traded across a border

examples.en: In the model, tariff revenue fell after the rise in duty sharply reduced the volume of imports.
examples.zh: 在模型中，关税上调使进口量骤降，之后「关税收入」也下降了。

examples.en: We calculated tariff revenue from the amount charged per unit and the quantity that was still imported.
examples.zh: 我们用每单位征收金额和仍有进口的数量计算「关税收入」。

collocations: estimate a change in tariff revenue

words.enDefinition: The economic cost borne by an individual or group as a result of a tax.

examples.en: The worksheet showed that the tax burden was shared between customers and sellers in the market.
examples.zh: 练习表显示，市场里的顾客和卖方共同承担「税收负担」。

examples.en: We compared the tax burden in two examples with different responses to a price increase.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两个对涨价反应不同的例题中的「税收负担」。

words.enDefinition: The amount stated for a good or service before the applicable tax is added.

examples.en: In the exercise, the tax-exclusive price was shown below the full amount paid by the buyer.
examples.zh: 练习中的「不含税价格」列在买方支付总额下方。

examples.en: Our tutor compared the tax-exclusive price with the total to check how much tax was charged.
examples.zh: 老师比较「不含税价格」与总额，核对加收了多少税。

collocations: calculate tax from a tax-exclusive price
compare the tax-exclusive price with the final amount

words.enDefinition: How the economic burden of a tax is divided among the people affected by it.

examples.en: The class analysed tax incidence by tracking changes in both the buyer price and the seller's receipts.
examples.zh: 全班通过跟踪买方价格和卖方实收金额的变化来分析「税负归宿」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked why tax incidence could differ from the rule about who forwarded payments to the government.
examples.zh: 老师问，「税负归宿」为什么可能与谁负责向政府缴款的规定不同。

collocations: explain tax incidence in a supply and demand model

words.enDefinition: A stated price that includes the tax payable on the transaction.

examples.en: The exercise displayed the tax-inclusive price paid by customers above the net amount received by sellers.
examples.zh: 练习把顾客支付的「含税价格」列在卖家收到的净额上方。

examples.en: We compared the tax-inclusive price in the diagram with what buyers paid before the tax was introduced.
examples.zh: 我们比较了图中的「含税价格」与征税前买家支付的价格。

collocations: compare the tax-inclusive price with the pre-tax amount

words.enDefinition: the reduction in overall surplus caused by a tax changing behaviour, after also counting the revenue collected, relative to the specified baseline

examples.en: The graph showed tax-induced deadweight loss from trades that would have benefited buyers and sellers before taxation.
examples.zh: 在这个模型中，征税使原本对双方有利的交易不再发生。图中展示了「税收造成的无谓损失」。

examples.en: Our tutor separated tax-induced deadweight loss from the revenue collected on transactions that still took place.
examples.zh: 老师把「税收造成的无谓损失」与仍发生的交易所产生的税收分开。

collocations: compare tax-induced deadweight loss across cases

words.enDefinition: A case in which the buyer's price changes by more than the change in tax per unit.

examples.en: The imperfectly competitive model showed tax overshifting when the buyer price rose more than the tax amount.
examples.zh: 在不完全竞争模型中，买方价格的涨幅超过税额，出现了「税收超额转嫁」。

examples.en: Our tutor checked the tax amount and buyer price change before describing the result as tax overshifting.
examples.zh: 老师核对了税额与买方价格的变化，才将结果描述为「税收超额转嫁」。

collocations: test whether the result indicates tax overshifting

words.enDefinition: The change in a buyer's price relative to the change in the tax per unit.

examples.en: We divided the change in the buyer price by the tax change to find the tax pass-through rate.
examples.zh: 我们用买方价格变动除以税额变动，求得「税收转嫁率」。

examples.en: Our tutor compared the tax pass-through rate in two fictional markets with different demand responses.
examples.zh: 老师比较了两个需求反应不同的虚构市场各自的「税收转嫁率」。

words.enDefinition: Money received by a government or other public authority through taxes.

examples.en: We calculated tax revenue by multiplying the amount per unit by the quantity sold after taxation.
examples.zh: 我们把单位税额乘以征税后的销量，计算出「税收收入」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked why higher tax revenue did not necessarily mean higher overall welfare in the model.
examples.zh: 老师问，为什么模型中较高的「税收收入」并不一定意味着较高的总体福利。

collocations: compare tax revenue under two policies
show tax revenue on a diagram

words.enDefinition: The difference a tax creates between the price buyers pay and the price sellers retain.

examples.en: The diagram showed a tax wedge between what customers paid and what sellers kept per sale.
examples.zh: 图中显示，顾客支付金额与卖家从每笔销售留存的金额之间出现了「税楔」。

examples.en: We labelled the tax wedge before calculating how the buyers and sellers shared the modelled tax.
examples.zh: 计算买卖双方如何分担模型中的税之前，我们先标出了「税楔」。

collocations: show the tax wedge between the two prices

words.enDefinition: Illustrative formula linking a policy rate to inflation and economic activity gaps

examples.en: We used a Taylor rule to compare rate prescriptions under two inflation forecasts.
examples.zh: 我们用「泰勒规则」比较了两种通胀预测下公式所指示的利率。

examples.en: The lecture changes a Taylor rule coefficient to show a larger response to inflation.
examples.zh: 课堂调整「泰勒规则」中的一个系数，展示对通胀反应更强的情形。

words.enDefinition: achieving the maximum feasible output from given inputs, or using no more inputs than needed for a given output

examples.en: The exercise described technical efficiency by asking whether the same workers and equipment could produce more output.
examples.zh: 练习询问同样的人手和设备能否生产更多，以说明「技术效率」。

examples.en: We compared technical efficiency before examining which workshop faced cheaper input prices in the example.
examples.zh: 我们先比较「技术效率」，再看示例中哪家车间面对更低的投入要素价格。

collocations: measure a loss of technical efficiency

words.enDefinition: The spread of existing production techniques or knowledge across firms, sectors, or countries.

examples.en: Technology diffusion helps explain why more workshops use the improved process in the later period.
examples.zh: 「技术扩散」有助于解释为什么后期有更多车间采用了改进后的流程。

examples.en: We compared two examples of technology diffusion with different rates of adoption across firms.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两个「技术扩散」示例，其中各企业采用技术的速度不同。

words.enDefinition: A regulatory requirement specifying equipment, methods or a type of technology that must be used.

examples.en: The classroom technology standard required each simulated plant to use the same kind of filter.
examples.zh: 课堂模型的「技术标准」要求每家模拟工厂使用同类过滤装置。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether a technology standard left firms room to choose a different production method.
examples.zh: 老师问，「技术标准」是否给企业留下选择其他生产方式的空间。

collocations: compare a technology standard with an outcome-based rule

words.enDefinition: A complete sequence of moves and chance events ending at a final outcome of the game.

examples.en: The terminal history ended with both groups accepting the proposed workshop times on the board.
examples.zh: 「终局历史」以两组都接受黑板所列工作坊时段结束。

examples.en: We recorded the full sequence of choices before assigning payoffs to the terminal history.
examples.zh: 我们先记录完整的选择顺序，再给「终局历史」赋予收益。

collocations: assign payoffs to a terminal history
compare the payoffs at different terminal histories

words.enDefinition: an increase in export prices relative to import prices, allowing a given volume of exports to purchase more imports

examples.en: Rising export prices and unchanged import prices produced a terms-of-trade improvement in the simplified example.
examples.zh: 在简化示例中，出口价格上涨且进口价格不变，带来了「贸易条件改善」。

examples.en: The report separated the terms-of-trade improvement from the change in the physical volume of goods sold.
examples.zh: 报告把「贸易条件改善」与商品实际销售量的变化区分开来。

words.enDefinition: a substantial change in the ratio of export prices to import prices caused by a new development

examples.en: A sharp drop in the price of its main export created a terms-of-trade shock in the model.
examples.zh: 主要出口品价格骤跌，在模型中造成了「贸易条件冲击」。

examples.en: We compared the effects of a terms-of-trade shock on two small economies with different export baskets.
examples.zh: 我们比较了「贸易条件冲击」对两个出口商品构成不同的小型经济体的影响。

collocations: estimate the effects of a terms-of-trade shock

words.enDefinition: economic analysis of how firms organise production and make decisions about inputs, output and pricing

examples.en: The theory of the firm helped the class explain why the workshop hired labour before expanding its premises.
examples.zh: 「厂商理论」帮助同学们解释为什么车间先增聘人手，再扩大经营场地。

examples.en: We applied the theory of the firm to compare the producer's decisions under different competitive conditions.
examples.zh: 我们运用「厂商理论」，比较该生产者在不同竞争条件下的决策。

collocations: study the theory of the firm
apply the theory of the firm
an assumption in the theory of the firm

words.enDefinition: charging different prices to distinct groups of buyers for the same product under a model of separate demands

examples.en: The museum's classroom pricing example used third-degree price discrimination by assigning separate prices to students and other visitors.
examples.zh: 课堂中的博物馆定价示例为学生和其他访客分别定价，属于「三级价格歧视」。

examples.en: We calculated the prices for third-degree price discrimination separately using each group's demand and the stated marginal cost.
examples.zh: 我们按各群体的需求与给定边际成本，分别计算「三级价格歧视」下的价格。

collocations: compare group prices under third-degree price discrimination

words.enDefinition: Independent verification that a product or provider meets a stated standard.

examples.en: The market example used third-party certification to show buyers whether the equipment met an agreed standard.
examples.zh: 市场例题用「第三方认证」向买家表明设备是否符合商定标准。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how third-party certification might change buyers' confidence in the quality of listed bicycles.
examples.zh: 老师问，「第三方认证」可能怎样改变买家对上架自行车质量的信心。

collocations: use third-party certification as a signal

words.enDefinition: Terms that allow each time period to have its own baseline shared by all units.

examples.en: Time fixed effects account for changes common to all schools in each year of the exercise.
examples.zh: 「时间固定效应」考虑练习中每年在所有学校都出现的变化。

examples.en: We included time fixed effects to distinguish shared yearly movements from differences across the individual schools.
examples.zh: 我们加入「时间固定效应」，将各校共有的年度变动与学校间差异区分开。

words.zhGloss: 不随时间变化的协变量
words.enDefinition: A measured characteristic that remains constant over time for a given unit.
acceptedZhAnswers: 不随时间变化的协变量

examples.en: The exercise treats a school's original building location as a time-invariant covariate in the sample.
examples.zh: 在样本中，练习把学校最初的建筑位置看作「不随时间变化的协变量」。

examples.en: We discussed why a time-invariant covariate cannot be identified separately from unit effects in this model.
examples.zh: 我们讨论为什么这个模型里的「不随时间变化的协变量」无法与单位效应分开识别。

words.enDefinition: A measured characteristic that can take different values for the same unit across periods.

examples.en: The school's average class size serves as a time-varying covariate in the classroom panel regression.
examples.zh: 课堂面板回归将学校平均班级规模作为「随时间变化的协变量」。

examples.en: We checked when the time-varying covariate was recorded relative to the tutoring offer in each school.
examples.zh: 我们核对了各校记录该「随时间变化的协变量」与发出辅导邀请的先后顺序。

words.enDefinition: A repeated-game strategy that starts with cooperation and then copies the other player's previous action.

examples.en: The tit-for-tat strategy began with a contribution and then copied the other team's last move.
examples.zh: 「一报还一报策略」先从出资开始，之后照做另一队上一轮的行动。

examples.en: We discussed how a mistaken choice could affect both groups using the tit-for-tat strategy.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了，一次错误选择可能怎样影响两个采用「一报还一报策略」的小组。

collocations: compare a tit-for-tat strategy with always cooperating

words.enDefinition: The full resource cost of achieving a specified reduction in pollution.

examples.en: The model compared total abatement cost under two policies that achieved the same overall emissions reduction.
examples.zh: 模型比较了两个实现相同总体减排量的政策各自的「减排总成本」。

examples.en: We added each factory's reduction costs to calculate total abatement cost for the entire exercise.
examples.zh: 我们把各工厂的减排成本相加，计算整个练习中的「减排总成本」。

collocations: minimize total abatement cost for a given target

words.enDefinition: the quantity of output produced with the amounts of inputs specified in the production analysis

examples.en: The total product rose when the bakery added a worker while continuing to use the same equipment.
examples.zh: 面包店增加一名工人、继续使用同一套设备时，「总产量」上升了。

examples.en: We recorded total product for each staffing level before calculating how much output an extra worker added.
examples.zh: 我们记录各用工水平下的「总产量」，再计算增聘一名工人带来的额外产出。

collocations: plot total product against labour input

words.enDefinition: a graph of total output against the amount of a varied input, holding other inputs fixed

examples.en: The total product curve flattened as more workers shared the same equipment in the production example.
examples.zh: 生产示例中，随着更多工人共用同一设备，「总产量曲线」逐渐变平。

examples.en: We read two points on the total product curve to calculate the output change between them.
examples.zh: 我们读取「总产量曲线」上的两点，计算两点之间的产量变化。

collocations: read the slope of a total product curve

words.enDefinition: a graph of the seller's total receipts across different quantities sold under the model's price schedule

examples.en: The total revenue curve initially increased as the lower price attracted enough additional customers in the exercise.
examples.zh: 在练习中，降价起初吸引了足够多的额外顾客，因此「总收益曲线」在这一段上升。

examples.en: The tutor compared the slope of the total revenue curve at two selected output levels.
examples.zh: 导师比较了「总收益曲线」在两个指定产量水平上的斜率。

collocations: find the maximum of a total revenue curve
read revenue from a total revenue curve

words.enDefinition: Method inferring demand elasticity from how sales revenue changes as price changes

examples.en: We applied the total revenue test after comparing receipts at two points on one demand curve.
examples.zh: 比较同一条需求曲线上两点的销售收入后，我们做了「总收益检验」。

examples.en: The total revenue test suggested demand was elastic because the price increase reduced sales revenue.
examples.zh: 由于涨价使销售收入下降，「总收益检验」表明需求富有弹性。

words.enDefinition: Overall satisfaction assigned to an entire bundle or quantity of goods

examples.en: We compared total utility across bundles before choosing which one to put on the slide.
examples.zh: 我们比较了各个组合的「总效用」，才决定把哪个放到幻灯片上。

examples.en: The table lists separate total utility values for one slice and for two slices.
examples.zh: 表中分别列出了吃一片和吃两片时的「总效用」值。

words.enDefinition: A transferable authorization to emit a specified amount under an emissions trading system.

examples.en: One factory sold a tradable emissions permit after reducing releases below its allocation in the classroom simulation.
examples.zh: 课堂模拟中，一家工厂将排放降至分配额度以下后，卖出了一份「可交易排放配额」。

examples.en: Our tutor used a tradable emissions permit to explain how a market price could reward lower emissions.
examples.zh: 老师用「可交易排放配额」解释市场价格怎样激励减少排放。

words.enDefinition: costs borne as workers, firms or regions adapt to a change in trade patterns or competition

examples.en: The study counted retraining and relocation among trade adjustment costs for workers leaving the affected industry.
examples.zh: 研究把再培训和搬迁计入离开受影响行业劳动者的「贸易调整成本」。

examples.en: Our model included temporary trade adjustment costs before comparing the longer-term gains predicted from lower tariffs.
examples.zh: 对比降低关税所预测的长期收益前，我们的模型计入了暂时的「贸易调整成本」。

collocations: distinguish trade adjustment costs from permanent losses

words.enDefinition: a shift toward lower-cost imports replacing higher-cost domestic production after a preferential trade arrangement

examples.en: The exercise showed trade creation when a lower-cost member supplier replaced costly domestic production after the agreement.
examples.zh: 协定实施后，成本较低的成员供应商替代了高成本国内生产，练习称其为「贸易创造」。

examples.en: We measured trade creation by comparing domestic output before and after imports from partner economies became cheaper.
examples.zh: 我们比较伙伴经济体进口品降价前后的国内产量，以衡量「贸易创造」。

collocations: distinguish trade creation from trade diversion

words.enDefinition: a switch from a lower-cost external supplier to a higher-cost preferred supplier because of tariff differences

examples.en: The class illustrated trade diversion by comparing production costs before adding the tariff that favoured a partner.
examples.zh: 同学们先比较生产成本，再加入对伙伴有利的关税，以演示「贸易转移」。

examples.en: Our example showed trade diversion when the partner became cheaper after duty despite having higher production costs.
examples.zh: 尽管伙伴的生产成本更高，但计入关税后其价格更低，示例体现了「贸易转移」。

collocations: explain the risk of trade diversion
model trade diversion after an agreement

words.enDefinition: reducing barriers that restrict international trade in goods or services

examples.en: The example described trade liberalisation after duties on several imported components were lowered in the model.
examples.zh: 在模型的若干进口元件关税下调后，示例说明了「贸易自由化」。

examples.en: We compared the projected impact of trade liberalisation across industries using imported inputs in different proportions.
examples.zh: 我们比较「贸易自由化」对各产业的预测影响，这些产业使用进口要素的比例不同。

collocations: analyse the effects of trade liberalisation
study a period of trade liberalisation

words.enDefinition: concentrating production in a narrower range of activities as an economy exchanges goods with trade partners

examples.en: In the model, trade specialisation shifted workers toward the industry with the lower relative production cost.
examples.zh: 在模型中，「贸易分工」使劳动者转向相对生产成本较低的行业。

examples.en: We compared trade specialisation across two examples with very different opportunities to exchange goods abroad.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两个示例中的「贸易分工」，两者从国外交换商品的机会很不相同。

words.zhGloss: 贸易额与 GDP 之比
words.enDefinition: the sum of exports and imports expressed as a percentage or fraction of gross domestic product
acceptedZhAnswers: 贸易额与 GDP 之比

examples.en: We calculated the trade-to-GDP ratio by adding exports and imports before dividing by the published output figure.
examples.zh: 我们先加总出口和进口，再除以公布的产出数字，求得「贸易额与 GDP 之比」。

examples.en: The tutor explained why a trade-to-GDP ratio above one could occur in a highly connected small economy.
examples.zh: 导师说明，为什么联系紧密的小型经济体的「贸易额与 GDP 之比」可能大于一。

words.enDefinition: Overuse or depletion of a shared resource when individual users do not bear the full costs of their use.

examples.en: The exercise illustrated the tragedy of the commons when total withdrawals left the shared well nearly empty.
examples.zh: 取水总量使共享水井近乎干涸，练习借此展示了「公地悲剧」。

examples.en: We asked whether agreed access rules could prevent the tragedy of the commons in the classroom fishery.
examples.zh: 我们问，共同商定的使用规则能否防止课堂渔场出现「公地悲剧」。

collocations: explain the tragedy of the commons
illustrate the tragedy of the commons
a model of the tragedy of the commons

words.enDefinition: The pattern of economic variables as a growth model moves toward its long-run path after a change.

examples.en: The tutor plotted the transition dynamics after raising the saving rate in the classroom model.
examples.zh: 老师在提高课堂模型的储蓄率后，绘出了「过渡动态」。

examples.en: We compared transition dynamics for two starting levels of capital in the same model.
examples.zh: 在同一个模型中，我们比较了两个初始资本水平的「过渡动态」。

collocations: transition dynamics toward a steady state

words.enDefinition: Property requiring that linked comparisons imply a consistent ranking across three options

examples.en: The student's ratings violate transitivity of preferences because her first choice changes in a cycle.
examples.zh: 这名学生的评分违反了「偏好的传递性」，因为她的首选项在两两比较时形成了循环。

examples.en: We used transitivity of preferences to infer a ranking between bundles A and C.
examples.zh: 我们利用「偏好的传递性」推导了组合 A 和 C 的排序。

words.enDefinition: A group of units that first receive treatment in the same period in a staggered design.
